author: brendanbyrne
body:
## Summary

Read-side foundation for the Pending Races & Grace Period feature, per [`reviews/design/2026-04-19-pending-races-and-grace-period.md`](reviews/design/2026-04-19-pending-races-and-grace-period.md) (fully signed off). Enforcement (skip endpoint, ordered-submit check, HTTP integration tests) is intentionally **deferred to PR 3D-2**.

After this PR the system can:
- Track per-race presence at race-creation time.
- Track which races a user has pending (correctly excluding submitted, skipped, absent-at-creation, and grace-expired).
- Surface a user's pending list as `your_pending` on the session detail polling response.

After this PR the system **cannot yet**:
- Skip a pending race via API (no endpoint).
- Block out-of-order run submission (`create_run` still accepts any order).

That gap is intentional — 3D-1 is read-side only.

## Schema (consolidated migration edited in place)

- `session_participants` gains `UNIQUE(session_id, user_id)` — single mutable row per (session, user) replaces the old multi-row history design. The partial unique index `(user_id) WHERE left_at IS NULL` stays; it still enforces "active in only one session at a time."
- New `session_race_participations` table: composite PK `(session_race_id, user_id)`, `ON DELETE CASCADE` on the **race-side** FK (`skip_turn`'s delete-and-replace relies on it), plain `REFERENCES` on the user-side FK (rows are never deleted by design — preserves the audit trail), index on `user_id`.

## Service changes

- **`helpers::insert_race_participations`** snapshots currently-present users into `session_race_participations` inside the same transaction as the race insert. Wired into `next_track` and `skip_turn`. Single `insert_many` per call.
- **`join_session`** rewritten for single-row mutate-on-rejoin. Within the 5-min grace window, rejoin only clears `left_at`; outside the window, `joined_at` resets to `NOW()` — which forfeits pre-gap pending records via the `get_pending_races` derivation.
- **`get_pending_races`** implements the 6-clause derivation from DESIGN.md (presence row + not skipped + no run + within grace + post-`joined_at` + session is active). Uses `find_by_statement` per the §5.1 ORM convention for multi-table JOINs. The `sessions.status = 'active'` clause was added in commit `a975225` after PR review caught a phantom-pending bug for sessions that close while a user is still inside their grace window.
- **`get_session_detail`** now takes `Option<&str> requesting_user_id` and includes `your_pending: Vec<SessionRaceInfo>` in the response. Route handler passes the auth user.

`SessionRaceInfo.submissions` is intentionally empty for pending races to avoid an N+1 on the polling path; the design review didn't require submissions on pending entries. Easy to add later if needed.

## Tests

**19 new tests, 204 total** (was 185 on main). All pass.

- 3 race-creation hook tests in `services::sessions::tests::test_create_session_race_*` — presence snapshot correctness, atomicity (FK violation rolls back the race insert).
- 6 pending-query tests in `services::sessions::tests::test_pending_*` — happy path, exclusions for submitted/skipped/absent-at-creation, ordering, no schema cap.
- 7 grace-period tests in `services::sessions::tests::test_pending_*` and `test_*_grace_*` — in-session, within grace, expired, within-grace rejoin (preserves `joined_at`), after-grace rejoin (resets `joined_at`, forfeits pending), multiple flaps, lazy-check intent assertion.
- 1 closed-session regression test (`test_pending_excludes_closed_session_even_within_grace`) added in `a975225` — exercises the `close_stale_sessions` path.
- 2 helper unit tests in `services::helpers::tests::insert_race_participations_*` added in `2be5b18` — direct coverage for the snapshot helper, including the empty-snapshot edge case.

`backdate_participant`, `insert_session_race`, and `insert_race_participation` test helpers added for fine-grained timestamp manipulation without sleeping.

## Reviewer note

**Reset the dev DB before booting** to pick up the schema change (per the prelaunch convention):
```
rm data/db/beerio-kart.db
```
The consolidated migration rebuilds the schema on next startup; SeaORM seeds run automatically.

## What this PR does NOT do

- `POST /sessions/:id/races/:race_id/skip` endpoint — PR 3D-2.
- Ordered-submit enforcement in `create_run` — PR 3D-2.
- HTTP-layer integration tests for the new behavior — PR 3D-2.
- Frontend consumption of `your_pending` — separate UI design.

## Test plan

### 1. Test suite (fast path — covers all logic)

```bash
git fetch origin phase-3/3d-1-pending-foundation
git checkout phase-3/3d-1-pending-foundation
rm -f data/db/beerio-kart.db
cd backend && cargo test
```

**Expected:** `test result: ok. 204 passed; 0 failed` total across all targets — broken down as 138 lib + 27 api_integration + 21 auth_integration + 8 auth_middleware + 10 session_integration.

To run only the tests added/modified in this PR:

```bash
cd backend && cargo test --lib -- \
    services::sessions::tests::test_create_session_race \
    services::sessions::tests::test_pending \
    services::sessions::tests::test_rejoin_within_grace \
    services::sessions::tests::test_rejoin_after_grace \
    services::sessions::tests::test_multiple_short_flaps \
    services::sessions::tests::test_lazy_check \
    services::helpers::tests::insert_race_participations
```

**Expected:** 19 tests, all pass.

### 2. End-to-end smoke test (HTTP + direct DB inspection)

Requires `jq` and `sqlite3`. Run from the repo root with the backend booted in another terminal:

```bash
# Terminal 1 — backend (will block; leave running)
cd backend && rm -f ../data/db/beerio-kart.db && JWT_SECRET=smoke-test-secret COOKIE_SECURE=false cargo run
# Wait for "Seeding complete" before continuing.
```

```bash
# Terminal 2 — set up env vars and run the smoke test
API=http://localhost:3000/api/v1
DB=data/db/beerio-kart.db

# Sanity check: backend is up. `curl -s` swallows connection errors silently,
# which would otherwise leave $A empty and produce confusing `null` outputs
# downstream. Run this first to fail fast if the server isn't listening yet.
curl -fsS "$API/hello" -o /dev/null && echo "backend up" || \
    { echo "backend not reachable on $API — start it in terminal 1 first" >&2; }

# Register two users; capture access tokens and user IDs.
A=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/auth/register" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"username":"alice","password":"smoketest123"}')
TOKEN_A=$(echo "$A" | jq -r .access_token)
USER_A=$(echo  "$A" | jq -r .user.id)

B=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/auth/register" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"username":"bob","password":"smoketest123"}')
TOKEN_B=$(echo "$B" | jq -r .access_token)
USER_B=$(echo  "$B" | jq -r .user.id)

echo "alice=$USER_A bob=$USER_B"
```

**Expected:** two non-empty UUIDs printed. If either is `null`, the register call failed — re-check the backend log.

```bash
# Step A: alice creates a session, bob joins.
SESSION=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/sessions" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_A" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"ruleset":"random"}' | jq -r .id)

curl -s -X POST "$API/sessions/$SESSION/join" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_B" -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n"
# Expected: 204
```

```bash
# Step B: alice picks the next track. This is the call that should
# create one session_race_participations row per currently-present user.
RACE=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/sessions/$SESSION/next-track" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_A" | jq -r .id)
echo "race=$RACE"
```

**Verify in the DB** — should show **2 rows** (one for alice, one for bob), both with `skipped_at = NULL`:

```bash
sqlite3 -header -column "$DB" \
    "SELECT user_id, created_at, skipped_at
     FROM session_race_participations
     WHERE session_race_id = '$RACE';"
```

**Expected output (2 rows, ordering may differ):**

user_id                               created_at

body:
Closes three small daemon tech-debt items surfaced by the PR #167 review.

## Commits

1. **refactor(shared): createHello takes options object for optionals** (`b8528a9`)
   Replaces the trailing positional optionals (`directory`, `resumeSessionId`, `lastReceivedIndex`, `mode`) with a single `CreateHelloOptions` object. Utility clients now write `createHello(id, '1.0.0', { mode: 'query' })` instead of `createHello(id, '1.0.0', undefined, undefined, undefined, 'query')`. All callsites in daemon CLI clients, scripts, web hooks, and tests are updated.

2. **refactor(daemon): type AdapterMetadata.platformData** (`586bf58`)
   Replaces `Record<string, unknown>` with a named `AdapterPlatformData` interface. `onConnect` in `connection-events.ts` now reads `metadata.platformData?.resumeSessionId` and `metadata.platformData?.mode` directly, no more string-key + cast. Renaming an adapter-side key now breaks the build instead of silently producing wrong behavior. Each adapter populates only the fields it owns (WebSocket: directory/resumeSessionId/mode, Telegram: chatId/topicId/directory, Relay: code).

3. **test(daemon): cover onConnect query-mode and resume branches** (`ce11098`)
   Adds the missing unit coverage flagged by the PR #167 review:
   - `connection-events.test.ts`: resumeSessionId-matches-primary attach, helloAck replay metadata + replayBatch when history exists, busy-session queueing with read-only replay, query-mode does not displace active connection or queue, omitted-platformData behavior, tracking happens before NO_SESSION branch
   - `websocket-server.test.ts`: `Connection.connectionMode` getter passes 'query' through from hello (and is undefined when omitted), matching the existing connectionDirectory pattern
   - `ls-client.test.ts`: assert the hello carries `mode: 'query'` so utility clients do not auto-attach
   - All tests use the real `SessionRegistry` (no mocks).

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run typecheck` clean
- [x] `bunx biome check` clean on touched files
- [x] `bun test packages/daemon/tests/cli packages/daemon/tests/session packages/shared/tests packages/daemon/tests/websocket-server.test.ts` — 892 pass, 0 fail
- [x] `bun test packages/daemon/tests/cli/handlers/connection-events.test.ts` — 11 pass (was 5)
- [ ] Run full integration suite on CI (unchanged behavior; only types and tests moved)

author: ghost
body:
### Summary
This PR enhances the health diagnostics endpoint by adding real-time visibility into the transaction mempool.

### Changes
1. **Mempool Monitoring**: Updated the  endpoint to include a count of pending inputs in the UTXO mempool.
2. **Operational Insight**: Helps node operators monitor transaction throughput and detect potential mempool congestion or stuck transactions.
3. **Robustness**: Implements safe database queries with fallback values to ensure the diagnostics endpoint remains responsive even if the mempool table is locked or missing.

Closes #2295

body:
## Summary

Two complementary fixes for the PR #51 contamination failure (see `INVESTIGATION-pr51-contamination.md`), where chud auto-published a draft PR whose diff was entirely commits from three other in-flight sessions.

- **Worktree base contamination** (`src/chud/worktree.py`): `git worktree add -b <branch>` ran without a base ref, so new chud branches silently inherited whatever the parent repo's local HEAD pointed at. Now resolves the remote default branch (with `gh` fallback), best-effort `git fetch origin <base>`, then forks from `origin/<base>` (falls back to local `<base>`, raises `WorktreeError` if neither exists).
- **Auto-publish ignored session authorship** (`src/chud/pr.py`, `src/chud/types.py`): the existing "0 commits ahead of `origin/<base>`" gate doesn't fire when the branch carries foreign commits. Capture worktree HEAD at attach time as `Worktree.start_head` and gate `publish_draft_prs` on `rev-list start_head..HEAD == 0` → silent discard. Backwards-compatible: legacy entries with `start_head=None` fall through to the existing origin-count check.

body:
## Summary

Coordinates the dismissible-banner code so we have one shared primitive instead of two. Pulls the dismissal storage + close-button logic into `DismissibleNotice` and rewrites `FederalScopeBanner` as a thin wrapper around it.

This is the follow-up flagged in PR #125's description, now that PR #124's `FederalScopeBanner` is on master.

## Changes

### `src/components/DismissibleNotice.jsx`
- Add `persistence` prop: `'session'` (default) or `'local'`. Default behavior is unchanged, so the existing AIAnalysis position-documentation banner keeps its session-storage semantics.
- Add `containerStyle` and `closeButtonStyle` props. Both merge on top of the defaults so callers can override or extend the styling without rewriting the chrome.
- No call sites to update for the existing AIAnalysis usage — it passes only `storageKey` + `children`, which still works.

### `src/components/FederalScopeBanner.jsx`
- Removed: direct `localStorage` handling, `dismissed` state, the `useEffect` that read storage on mount, the `handleDismiss` function, the outer `<div role="note">` wrapper, and the dismiss button.
- All of the above now come from `DismissibleNotice`.
- Kept: the same `STORAGE_KEY` value (`'tx360.federalScopeBanner.dismissed'`) so users who already dismissed the banner stay dismissed after this change ships.
- Kept: the amber styling (passed via `containerStyle`), the ⚠ icon, the "Federal tax only." copy, the "What's included?" expand/collapse toggle, and the full computed/not-computed details list.

## Net effect

- One dismissible-banner component instead of two parallel implementations.
- Two persistence modes (session vs local) cleanly expressed via a prop.
- File size: FederalScopeBanner.jsx 3,483 → 2,712 chars (-22%); DismissibleNotice.jsx 1,836 → 2,428 chars (+32%).

## Verification after merge

- AI Position Documentation disclaimer in AIAnalysis still appears on first invocation per session and stays dismissed for the rest of that session.
- Federal scope banner above the federal liability total still appears, dismisses with the X, and stays dismissed across page reloads on the same device.
- "What's included?" toggle still expands the computed/not-computed details list.

## No tests added

Same rationale as PR #125: adding tests for these UI components would require standing up jsdom + testing-library, which is an architectural decision worth making deliberately. Flagging again for a future test-infrastructure PR.

author: eygraber
body:
## Summary

- Phones letterbox or stretch 16:9 / 21:9 video surfaces in portrait. Now the video player screen requests `SCREEN_ORIENTATION_LANDSCAPE` while in composition and restores the prior `requestedOrientation` on dispose, so navigating back returns the activity to whatever orientation the rest of the app uses.
- Gated on `Configuration.smallestScreenWidthDp < 600` so tablets and larger Android form factors keep their natural orientation.
- Implemented as `@Composable expect/actual` so the call site is platform-agnostic. `androidMain` does the real work using `LocalActivity.current` from `activity-compose`; `cmpMain` is a no-op for JVM, iOS, and WasmJs (Desktop/Web have no Activity to rotate).

## Out of scope

- iOS orientation locking. The issue calls it out (`AppDelegate.supportedInterfaceOrientationsFor` / `UIViewController.supportedInterfaceOrientations`), but the iOS player itself was added in #58 and isn't currently exercised end-to-end. Tracking remains under #241; the cmpMain no-op keeps iOS unblocked until then.

body:
## Summary

Adds `ServerCapabilities.knownDevices: List<KnownDevice>` to `InitializeResult` so clients building a `renderNow.overrides.device` picker can read the catalog off the wire instead of re-bundling `DeviceDimensions`. First step on the "config negotiation" thread we discussed — **flips the device catalog from a duplicated-on-each-side hardcode into a daemon-advertised list**.

- **Wire shape** — Each entry carries `id` plus resolved `widthDp` / `heightDp` / `density` so a UI can label "Pixel 5 — 393×851 dp @ 2.75x" without re-resolving. Populated at `initialize`-handler time from `DeviceDimensions.KNOWN_DEVICE_IDS`, sorted alphabetically so the client sees a stable order across runs (catalog map is insertion-ordered today, but the contract should be independent of catalog-edit ordering).
- **`spec:width=…,height=…,dpi=…`** — not enumerable; documented as a free-form override the daemon still parses at resolve-time.
- **Backwards-compatible** — defaulted to `emptyList()`. Pre-feature daemons advertise nothing and clients treat absent and `[]` identically.
- **Mirrored on TypeScript** — `ServerCapabilities.knownDevices` plus the `KnownDevice` interface in `daemonProtocol.ts`.
- **Docs + fixtures** — `PROTOCOL.md § 3` updated; the shared `daemon-initializeResult.json` fixture now includes `id:pixel_5` + `id:wearos_small_round` so the round-trip tests on both sides exercise the new field.

## Test plan

- [x] `:daemon:core:test` — 27/27 `MessagesTest` (incl. updated fixture round-trip), 11/11 `JsonRpcServerIntegrationTest` (one flaky pre-existing test on the first run, clean on rerun — unrelated to this change which is `initialize`-only)
- [x] `:daemon:core:ktfmtCheck` — clean
- [x] `ktfmtCheckAll` — clean across the repo

## Notes

- Includes ktfmtFormatAll output for `DesktopHost.kt` (pre-existing unrelated format drift the global pre-commit hook required — same pattern as the previous two PRs in this thread).
- Natural follow-up: a small MCP `list_devices` tool that just returns this list. Out of scope here — wire shape lands first; tool wrapper after.

author: claude-murgat
body:
## Summary

Two CI infra issues blocking the tier4-failback workflow on the new Debian self-hosted runner:

### 1. PATH missing `emulator/` and `platform-tools/`
- `android-actions/setup-android@v3` only adds `cmdline-tools/latest/bin` to PATH
- On managed Ubuntu runners, `emulator` and `adb` happen to be on PATH via other setup
- On our self-hosted Debian, `nohup emulator -avd ...` fails with `cannot execute 'emulator'`
- Emulators never boot → `Wait for emulators to fully boot` step hangs 20 min
- **Fix:** explicit step prepending `$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT/emulator` and `.../platform-tools` to `$GITHUB_PATH`

### 2. `adb logcat -d` hangs forever when device is gone
- `Collect logcat per emulator (always)` runs after every job (incl. failures)
- If the emulator never started (issue #1) or was torn down, `adb -s emulator-XXXX logcat` hangs waiting for device
- The trailing `|| true` is never reached
- Observed: 19h of zombie `adb` processes from a cancelled run, blocking the runner from picking new jobs
- **Fix:** wrap dump with `timeout 10`

Both fixes are purely additive — happy path unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] Confirmed locally that `$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT/emulator/emulator` exists on the runner
- [x] Confirmed `nohup: impossible d'exécuter la commande 'emulator'` is the root cause of empty `reports/emulator-*.log`
- [ ] After merge, re-trigger `Tier 4 — Failback E2E (nightly)` and confirm boot + wait + cluster + pytest steps run

author: neuromechanist
body:
## Summary

Implements Ctrl+Z support for `remi <args>` so the user can drop back to the shell with `[1]+ Stopped` and resume with `fg`. The PTY-hosted Claude keeps running across the suspend. Fixes #361.

## Root cause

`remi <args>` puts stdin into raw mode while forwarding bytes to the PTY-hosted Claude. In raw mode the kernel does NOT translate Ctrl+Z (`0x1A`) into SIGTSTP -- it forwards the literal byte to the child, which discards it. The keystroke was silently swallowed.

## Approach

Two small pieces, kept in two files:

1. **`DetachScanner` gets an optional `onSuspend` callback.** When wired, the scanner intercepts the `0x1A` byte before it reaches the PTY. When the callback is omitted (e.g. legacy tests, future re-use) the byte passes through unchanged. The scan-ahead batching loop also breaks on `0x1A` only when interception is active.

2. **New `cli/suspend-handler.ts`** owns the SIGTSTP/SIGCONT lifecycle:
   - On SIGTSTP (from the byte path or `kill -TSTP <pid>`): tear down raw mode + pause stdin, then self-send SIGSTOP. SIGSTOP is uncatchable, so the kernel suspends only the remi process. The shell sees a stopped job.
   - On SIGCONT (from `fg`/`bg` or `kill -CONT <pid>`): restore raw mode and call `onResume`.
   - Re-entrancy guard prevents double teardown if SIGTSTP fires twice in a row.
   - Tests inject a `kill` seam to verify the signal flow without actually suspending the test runner.

## Child-process-group decision

The PTY child runs in its own session because `Bun.spawn` with the `terminal:` option uses forkpty/setsid under the hood. Sending SIGSTOP to `process.pid` only suspends remi; the Claude child is unaffected. No `detached: true` change to the spawn site was needed.

## Removed

The old top-level `process.on('SIGTSTP', ignore)` handler in `cli.ts`. It was a guard that prevented wrapper-mode remi from suspending; now wrapper mode handles SIGTSTP properly via `installSuspendHandler`. Non-wrapper modes (`remi daemon`, `remi ls`, etc.) get the kernel default, which is fine: the daemon is typically headless and the ls/attach clients are short-lived.

## Test plan

Automated (passing locally, 672 daemon tests):
- [x] `bun test packages/daemon/tests/cli/detach-scanner.test.ts`: 18 tests including 5 new `onSuspend` cases
- [x] `bun test packages/daemon/tests/cli/suspend-handler.test.ts`: 6 new tests covering byte path, SIGCONT resume, dispose, re-entrancy
- [x] `bun test packages/daemon/tests/pty-sigtstp.test.ts`: still green (the underlying runtime contract that suspend-handler depends on)
- [x] `bun run typecheck` clean
- [x] `bunx biome check` clean

Manual:
- [ ] `remi <args>` -> Ctrl+Z -> shell prompt with `[1]+  Stopped  remi`
- [ ] `fg` resumes remi cleanly; raw mode restored; further keystrokes flow to Claude
- [ ] `bg` works (remi continues in background; user can use the shell)
- [ ] Verify Claude PTY child kept running during suspend (e.g. `ps`, or reattach from another client)
- [ ] `kill -TSTP <remi-pid>` from another shell also suspends; `kill -CONT <remi-pid>` resumes

Fixes #361

author: vikingowl91
body:
## Summary

First CI workflow for the repo. Runs on every PR and push to `main` as a single `validate` job with 9 steps:

| # | Check |
|---|---|
| 1 | `bash -n install.sh` |
| 2 | `shellcheck install.sh` |
| 3 | `bash -n` every Cursor hook script |
| 4 | `shellcheck` every Cursor hook script |
| 5 | `tomllib` parse every Gemini CLI TOML prompt |
| 6 | `json` parse `ADAPTERS/cursor/hooks/hooks.json` |
| 7 | Codex `SKILL.md` frontmatter (`---`, `name:`, `description:`) |
| 8 | All 19 canonical files present (mirrors `install.sh` `REQUIRED_FILES`) |
| 9 | Wire-flag set in `README.md` matches `install.sh` |

`permissions: contents: read` only. No `${{ github.event.* }}` substitutions in any `run:` command — injection-safe by construction.

## Why these checks

The first 7 catch the kinds of bugs that would otherwise only surface at install time on a user's machine. Check 8 prevents accidental file deletion that would break `install.sh`'s sanity check. Check 9 prevents README/installer drift — the kind that creeps in across multiple adapter PRs.

## Follow-up

After this merges, flip the `protect-main` ruleset's **Require status checks to pass** rule on, with `validate` as the required check. That closes the final gap in the branch protection setup.

## Test plan

- [x] YAML lint — `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` passes
- [x] All 9 steps dry-run-passed locally before commit
- [x] First PR through the new ruleset (this PR) — verifies signed commits + linear history rules don't block normal PR work

## Summary

This PR fixes a couple of mobile UX/runtime issues by making Settings drawers render more safely and tightening when camera permissions are requested. It also includes a small visual polish update for connected account provider icons.

---

## Why is this change necessary?

The current mobile behavior can trigger unstable drawer interactions in Settings and request camera access too aggressively. This change is necessary to prevent drawer-related crashes, avoid unnecessary permission prompts until the camera view is actually active, and clean up a small inconsistency in connected account icon presentation.

---

## Changes

- Reworked mobile Settings drawer state to use a single active drawer instead of multiple simultaneously mounted drawer states.
- Conditionally render Settings drawers only when active to avoid overlapping drawer behavior and reduce crash risk.
- Added a short interaction lock and disabled background scrolling/taps while drawer transitions are happening.
- Updated delete account and interests flows to use the shared drawer open/close behavior.
- Changed camera permission handling to refresh on active view state and only request permission when the camera screen is active and permission is still not-determined.
- Removed the previous focus-effect-based permission request flow in favor of a simpler useEffect tied to screen activity.
- Increased Apple and Google connected account icon sizes and aligned Apple icon color usage with the current theme text color.

v3.4.0 
There are a few changes in this release to highlight:

1. `Constraints` now has a property `IncludePrerelease`. When set to true the `Check` and `Validate` methods will include prereleases.
2. When an AND group has one constraint with a prerelease but more than one constraint then prereleases will be included. For example, `>1.0.0-beta.1 < 2`. In the past this would not have included prereleases because each constraint needed to have a prerelease. Now, only one constraint needs to have a prerelease. This is considered a long standing bug fix. Note, this does not carry across OR groups. For example, `>1.0.0-beta.1 < 2 || > 3`. In this case, prereleases will not be included when evaluating against `>3`.
3. `NewVersion` coercion with leading "0"'s is restored. This can be disabled by setting the package level property `CoerceNewVersion` to `false`.

author: matthewmckee4
body:
## Summary

Adds nextest-style [test groups](https://nexte.st/docs/configuration/test-groups/) (#563, #564) to karva, in two commits: the `group(...)` filter predicate first, then the surrounding configuration.

The `[test-groups.<name>]` table declares groups, and per-profile `[[profile.*.overrides]]` entries assign matching tests to a group via filter expressions:

```toml
[test-groups.database]
max-threads = 4

[[profile.default.overrides]]
filter = "tag(database)"
test-group = "database"
```

The new `group(...)` predicate then targets the resolved group, so `-E 'group(database)'` runs only database-tagged tests and `-E 'not group(database)'` excludes them.

Group resolution happens worker-side at filter-eval time, using the runtime tags the worker already extracts via the existing extension machinery. The main process forwards the resolved override list as TOML through a hidden `--group-overrides` CLI argument; no new dependencies are needed because `karva_metadata` already pulls in `toml`. Validation that every override references a declared group (and that override filters do not themselves use `group(...)` to avoid circular references) happens in the main process before any worker spawns.

`max-threads` is intentionally not enforced by the partitioner in this PR. Honouring it requires either a coordinator-based scheduler or a two-pass discovery phase, both of which are larger architectural changes that are best landed separately. The schema and runtime predicate are useful on their own — `--group-overrides` gives users a way to filter by group today, and a follow-up PR can add scheduling without changing the user-facing surface.

Profile inheritance preserves first-match-wins: a named profile's overrides are evaluated before the default profile's, and within a profile, top-down. Overrides that match but do not set a `test-group` are skipped during group resolution rather than terminating the search, mirroring nextest's per-setting first-match-wins model.

author: weetime
body:
## Summary

Issue #53 PR 53.3 (Phase 3 of 4). Replaces the Phase 1 stub runtimes with real implementations, makes the runner image tool-agnostic, splits Dockerfiles per tool, and converts the legacy benchmark / load-test controllers into thin facades over the unified `RunService` shipped in PR #73 (Phase 2).

After this PR, ModelDoctor can drive guidellm benchmarks AND vegeta load tests through one unified codepath: `RunService` → tool-adapter `buildCommand` → driver (subprocess or k8s Job) → generic Python wrapper → tool subprocess → callbacks `/state` `/log` `/finish` → `RunCallbackController` → `parseFinalReport` → `Run.summaryMetrics`.

PR 53.4 (Phase 4) will add the genai-perf adapter and verify the acceptance gate (`packages/tool-adapters/src/core/interface.ts` git diff against main must be empty after Phase 4 — Phase 3 just made the last interface change via Pre-B's `getMaxDurationSeconds`).

## What's in this PR (18 commits)

### Pre-flight (Pre-A + Pre-B, before plan §Task 3.1)
- **Pre-A** — schema polish on Phase 1 deliverables. 4 user-flagged items (I2 `processor.min(1)`, I3 `requestRate` float support, I4 `superRefine` per-field path, M3 meaningful `paramDefaults` test) + 3 gemini polishings (vegeta success bounded percent, requests/rate/throughput non-negative, guidellm requests counts non-negative). 4dbcfea + a2ef704.
- **Pre-B** — per-adapter `getMaxDurationSeconds(params): number` on `ToolAdapter` interface. guidellm returns `params.maxDurationSeconds`, vegeta returns `params.duration`, genai-perf throws (Phase 4 stub). RunService.start uses this to size the HMAC callback TTL instead of a global env. **Last interface change before Phase 4 freezes the contract.** 05ab5c9 + 44b1029.

### Phase 3 main path
- **Task 3.1 — guidellm runtime**: `buildCommand` emits guidellm CLI argv with api_key routed through `secretEnv.OPENAI_API_KEY` (Phase 3 wrapper injects into `--backend-kwargs` at runtime). `parseFinalReport` ports `apps/benchmark-runner/runner/metrics.py` mapper. Fixture-based tests. 6c05463.
- **Task 3.2 — vegeta runtime**: shell-pipeline `buildCommand` (`/bin/sh -c 'cat targets.txt | vegeta attack | tee attack.bin | vegeta report > report.txt'`); api_key in `inputFiles["targets.txt"]` only (never argv/env/secretEnv). `parseFinalReport` ports the regex parser with proper ms unit conversion (handles µs/ms/s). a2df1f7 + 624189e.
- **Task 3.3 — generic runner**: `apps/benchmark-runner/runner/main.py` rewritten tool-agnostically. Reads `MD_RUN_ID/MD_CALLBACK_URL/MD_CALLBACK_TOKEN/MD_ARGV/MD_OUTPUT_FILES`, spawns argv, batches stdout/stderr to `/log`, base64-encodes outputFiles on `/finish`. Old guidellm-specific `argv.py/env.py/metrics.py` deleted. 25 pytest tests pass. 42a1d83 + 7fe83bd.
- **Task 3.4 — Dockerfile split**: `apps/benchmark-runner/images/{guidellm,vegeta}.Dockerfile`. guidellm keeps `gpustack/benchmark-runner:v0.0.3` base. vegeta is `python:3.11-slim` + the vegeta v12.13.0 static binary downloaded from `tsenart/vegeta` GitHub releases (peterevans image is stale; tag 12.10.0 doesn't exist). **SHA-256 verified for both linux_amd64 and linux_arm64.** Both images run as non-root with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE`. CI `docker-build` job converted to a matrix over `[guidellm, vegeta]` with scoped GHA cache. b197016 + 0e3a156 + 5c7fbe6.
- **Task 3.5 — BenchmarkController facade**: `apps/api/src/modules/benchmark/` reduced to controller + mappers + module shim. ~14 legacy files deleted (service, reconciler, drivers, internal callback controller). Routes `/api/benchmarks/*` keep their request/response shape so the FE doesn't break (#54 retires the facade). 13 → 15 tests after follow-up. b398d19 + 4aec299.
- **Task 3.6 — LoadTestController facade**: same pattern for vegeta. `POST /load-test` preserves legacy synchronous response by polling `RunService.findById` until terminal. 16 tests. ebfe00c + 941528a.

### Verification (Task 3.7)
- 96598aa: biome format on `run.service.spec.ts` (Pre-B drive-by debt).
- 75422ac: biome lint+format on Task 3.1/3.2/3.5 files (per-task review missed repo-wide config).

## Out of scope (deferred to PR 53.4 / future)

- **genai-perf adapter runtime** + Phase 4 acceptance gate verification (PR 53.4).
- **Run reconciler.** The legacy benchmark reconciler was deleted with Task 3.5. RunModule has no replacement yet — a stuck Run that never sends /finish stays in `running` until manual cancel. Tracked as future work in plan §3.5.4.
- **Dup-name race in `RunService.create`** (also flagged in #73 follow-up). \`countActiveByName\` + \`repo.create\` is not atomic. Proper fix: Postgres partial unique index on \`(user_id, name) WHERE status NOT IN ('completed','failed','canceled')\`.
- **\`waitForTerminal\` cleanup-on-timeout** in load-test facade. Currently leaks a running Run if the HTTP deadline fires. #54 deletes the polling path.
- **Admin cross-user list scoping.** Both facades always pass \`user.sub\` to RunService.list — admins lose the ability to see other users' runs through the legacy endpoints. Phase 3 stopgap; #54 ships proper authz on /api/runs.
- **vitest \`fileParallelism: false\`** in apps/api/vitest.config.mts (PR #73 carry-over). Proper fix is per-worker postgres schema isolation.
- **Old DB rows.** Pre-Task-3.6 rows have \`apiType/rate/duration\` in \`scenario\` (not \`params\`) and \`summaryMetrics\` in raw \`LoadTestParsed\` shape (not the new \`{tool, data}\` envelope). The new mappers strict-decode the envelope only — legacy rows show \`null\`/defaults. \`prisma migrate reset --force\` clears them; #54 retires the affected endpoints.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm -r build\` — clean across contracts / tool-adapters / web / api.
- [x] \`pnpm -r lint\` — zero biome findings (apps/web has 6 pre-existing warnings, no errors).
- [x] \`pnpm -F @modeldoctor/tool-adapters test\` — 47/47 pass (covers guidellm + vegeta fixture-based parsing + zod constraint tightening).
- [x] \`pnpm -F @modeldoctor/api test --run "src/modules/benchmark"\` — 15/15 pass.
- [x] \`pnpm -F @modeldoctor/api test --run "src/modules/load-test"\` — 16/16 pass.
- [x] \`pnpm -F @modeldoctor/api test --run "src/modules/run/run.service"\` — 14/14 pass.
- [x] benchmark-runner pytest — 25/25 pass (test_main 11 + test_callback 14, run inside ephemeral venv).
- [x] @modeldoctor/contracts — 86/86 pass.
- [x] @modeldoctor/web — 458/458 pass.
- [ ] Manual subprocess smoke (\`POST /api/runs\` → status:completed) — **skipped, no localhost LLM target available in this environment**. Unit tests already exercise \`parseFinalReport\` against committed fixtures.
- [ ] CI \`docker build -f apps/benchmark-runner/images/guidellm.Dockerfile\` — to be validated on PR open via CI matrix.
- [ ] CI \`docker build -f apps/benchmark-runner/images/vegeta.Dockerfile\` — same.

**Pre-existing test failures** (verified to also fail on \`main\` at 3baf257): 19 \`PrismaClientInitializationError\` failures across \`run.repository.spec.ts\`, \`run.controller.spec.ts\`, \`e2e-test.service.spec.ts\` when \`DATABASE_URL\` isn't set. These are not regressions.

## Deployment-ordering note

The legacy \`POST /api/internal/benchmarks/<id>/{state,metrics}\` callback path is removed by Task 3.5. Task 3.3 already updated the runner image to use \`/api/internal/runs/<id>/{state,log,finish}\`. **In a rolling deploy, the runner-image upgrade must precede or land with the API upgrade** — otherwise old runner pods will 404 on /state and the run will appear stuck.

## Related

- Issue: #53
- Spec: \`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-02-issue-53-tool-adapter-framework-design.md\`
- Plan: \`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-02-issue-53-tool-adapter-framework.md\` §Phase 3
- Previous: PR #72 (53.1 skeleton) + PR #73 (53.2 callback v2)
- Next: PR 53.4 (genai-perf + acceptance gate)

body:
## Summary

Five interrelated fixes uncovered today by running `jobsmith apply` against a real JD URL end-to-end. Each bug appeared sequentially as the prior one was resolved; together they take the apply pipeline from "fails at gather phase 1" to "completes phase 3 render."

| Bug | Phase | Failure mode | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bug-5f4a6233` | gather | Plain-text halt instead of marker on unfrozen-contracts path | Prompt now emits `<<PHASE_FAILED: gather: …>>` |
| `bug-8c19a5af` | parser | `_PHASE_FAILED_RE` truncated on any `>` char in description | Switched `[^>]+?` → `.+?` with `re.DOTALL` |
| `bug-8a68a43b` | gather | Deterministic session UUID collided with orphaned `.jsonl` on retry | uuid4 + persistence + stale-orphan detection |
| `bug-1b7fea73` | draft | `max_turns=30` shared across resumed gather→draft session | Always start a fresh session at the gather→draft boundary |
| `bug-e752c9f0` | render | Render's 6-specialist sequential workflow exhausts 30 turns | Phase-specific `_PHASE_MAX_TURNS = {gather: 30, draft: 30, render: 60}` |

## Stats

- 5 files changed, +510 / -37
- New helpers: `_get_or_create_session_id`, `_claude_session_file_path`, `_PHASE_MAX_TURNS`
- New tests: 8 (session-id persistence, stale-orphan detection, phase-2-fresh-session, phase-specific max_turns, angle-bracket-rich PHASE_FAILED parsing)
- **432 tests pass** (424 baseline + 8 new) · 0 new lint errors

## Backward compatibility

- `headless.deterministic_session_id` retained (legacy fallback when `app_dir is None`); new code paths use `_get_or_create_session_id`
- `headless.run_phase` default `max_turns=30` unchanged; per-phase override is opt-in at the `apply.py` call site
- No prompt structure changes outside the one-line gather halt-path replacement
- All 424 tests from PR #23 baseline still pass

## Test plan

- [ ] Pull, `uv sync --extra test`, run `uv run pytest` — should be 432 passed
- [ ] On a slug whose previous gather failed: re-run `jobsmith apply <url>`. Stale-orphan detection should print `jobsmith: regenerated session ID; previous orphan at …` to stderr and proceed past gather without "Session ID already in use."
- [ ] On an apply where contracts are not yet frozen: the gather phase aborts with a clean message ("Contracts not frozen; freeze specialist-contracts.yaml before running apply.") instead of the generic phase_complete error
- [ ] Render phase completes Step 7 → Step 9 (resume render → ATS check → visual-layout review → cover-letter writer → index writer) on a non-trivial JD without `max_turns_reached`

author: chenhui-su
body:
Fixes #116

## Summary

`node-pty` is listed as a required dependency, but its native build fails on Android/Termux because `binding.gyp` references an undefined `android_ndk_path` variable. This causes `npm i -g codexapp` to hard-fail on Termux before the package can even finish installing.

The fix moves `node-pty` from `dependencies` to `optionalDependencies`. When the native build fails on unsupported platforms (Termux/Android), npm skips it gracefully instead of aborting the entire install. The app already handles the missing PTY module at runtime by reporting "Integrated terminal is unavailable on this host".

## Changes

- `package.json`: move `node-pty` from `dependencies` to `optionalDependencies`

## Verification on Android 15 / Termux

**Environment:**
- Android 15, Termux
- Node v24.14.1, npm 11.13.0
- Branch: `fix/issue-116-termux-node-pty-optional`

**Steps & key output:**

```bash
# 1. Clone fix branch
git clone -b fix/issue-116-termux-node-pty-optional https://github.com/chenhui-su/codex-web-ui.git
cd codex-web-ui

# 2. Install deps — postinstall succeeds, node-pty failure no longer blocks
npm install
# > added 298 packages, and audited 299 packages in 1m
# > found 0 vulnerability

# 3. Build CLI
npm run build:cli
# > ESM dist-cli/index.js     433.38 KB
# > ESM ⚡️ Build success in 670ms

# 4. Global install — completes without error
npm uninstall -g codexapp
npm i -g .
# > added 1 package in 919ms

# 5. codexapp command is available
ls "$(npm prefix -g)/bin" | grep codex
# codexapp
# codexui

# 6. App launches successfully
codexapp --no-login
# Codex Web Local is running!
#   Version:  0.1.87
#   Bind:     http://0.0.0.0:5900
#   Codex sandbox: danger-full-access
#   Approval policy: never
#   Local:    http://localhost:5900
#   Network:  http://192.168.31.64:5900
#   Password: emn-1z5-okr
```

**Before the fix** (issue #116): `npm i -g codexapp` fails with `gyp: Undefined variable android_ndk_path in binding.gyp` and exits with code 1.

**After the fix**: install completes; app starts and gracefully reports terminal unavailability when PTY is missing.

## Impact on supported platforms

On platforms where `node-pty` builds successfully (Linux, macOS, Windows), `optionalDependencies` are installed identically to regular `dependencies`. No behavioral change on supported hosts — the integrated terminal continues to work as before.

## Summary

Adds a `Tier.BATCH` to the LLM router. Routes non-interactive heavy-reasoning workloads (deep_dive, regression eval at `--tier batch`) to a CPU-only DeepSeek-V4-Flash 158B llama.cpp server on grid-svr port 8082. Direct cost replacement for OpenAI calls in those paths.

## What's new

- **`llm/router.py`** (+38/-1)
  - `Tier.BATCH = "batch"` enum
  - `_create_llamacpp_batch_client` factory mirroring the oracle pattern
  - Dispatch + provider mapping wired
  - Fallback chain (BATCH only): `["llamacpp_batch", "llamacpp_oracle", "openrouter", "openai"]`
  - **Opt-in only** — batch is NEVER auto-added to interactive tier fallbacks. Slow CPU model would otherwise block chat / deep_dive's primary path.

- **`config.py`** (+13/-2)
  - `LLAMACPP_BATCH_{ENABLED, BASE_URL, CHAT_MODEL, TIMEOUT_SECONDS}` settings
  - Default `ENABLED=False`. Set `LLAMACPP_BATCH_ENABLED=true` in `.env` to activate.
  - Renamed legacy `LLM_BATCH_BASE_URL` → `LLAMACPP_BATCH_BASE_URL` for naming consistency with `LLAMACPP_ORACLE_*`, `LLAMACPP_QUICK_*`, `LLAMACPP_Z4_*`.

- **`intelligence/deep_dive.py`** (+25/-25)
  - `_call_best_llm` step 2 switched from `Tier.ORACLE` + `provider="openai"` to `Tier.BATCH`. No provider override — falls back to the chain if local is down.
  - `tier:batch` Langfuse tag preserved via the `extra_metadata` flow shipped in #83.

- **`scripts/run_regression_eval.py`** (+39/-9)
  - New `--tier {local,reason,oracle,batch}` CLI flag (default `oracle`)
  - Threaded through `run_chatbot` and `get_llm()`
  - Enables per-tier regression baselines (Phase 8 of the rolled-out plan)

## Backed by

DeepSeek-V4-Flash 158B Q4_K_M (Apr 22 2026 release, MIT) at `/data/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/DeepSeekV4-Flash-158B-Q4_K_M.gguf` (112 GB on disk, mmap'd into grid-svr's 512 GB RAM). llama.cpp build `aab6821`, port 8082. Measured **~5.5 tok/sec** on dual E5-2697 v2 (DDR3-1866 bandwidth-bound, as expected for 17B-active MoE).

## Test plan

- [x] All 18 tests in `test_llm_router.py` pass
- [x] Smoke: `get_llm(Tier.BATCH)` returns `LlamaCppClient` with `is_available=True`, `.chat(...)` returns content (or `reasoning_content` fallback when prompt is too short for both thinking + answer to fit in `max_tokens`)
- [ ] Production verification (post-merge): `deep_dive` step 2 traces in Langfuse should now tag `tier:batch` and route to local instead of OpenAI; cost dashboard should show OpenAI calls drop in deep_dive flow
- [ ] First weekly regression eval run against `--tier batch` to establish baseline

## Note on commit contents

Two `outputs/capital_flow_research/*.json` files snuck into the commit from the working tree (research artifacts, not sprint code). Reviewer can drop them in a follow-up if not wanted.

## Follow-ups

- Wire `audio_briefing.py` to `Tier.BATCH` once we've measured deep_dive's cost reduction
- Phase 8: extend weekly regression cron to fire one run per tier
- Phase 14: model warm-pool — mmap multiple GGUFs on grid-svr so swapping batch/oracle models is 0 ms

author: nicholas-fedor
body:
This PR enhances thread safety across the codebase and modernizes the CI/CD configuration for better reliability and parallel test execution.

### Problem

The codebase had several concurrency issues:
- `TestDirection` rateCapture channel was unbuffered, risking goroutine blocking
- Global `ByteRate` unit variable accessed without synchronization
- `Locations` map modified concurrently without protection
- `DataManager` fields accessed unsafely during handler registration and rate calculations

Additionally, packet loss handling had issues:
- Response validation required minimum 4 elements, not 3
- loopSampler returned errors unnecessarily when transient failures should be ignored

Finally, the project was lacking GitHub workflows and proper release pipelines.

### Solution

- Added mutex protection for `ByteRate` global unit variable access
- Introduced `sync.RWMutex` for `Locations` map read/write operations
- Added mutex locking in `DataManager` for concurrent handler registration, reset, and rate calculation methods
- Buffered the `stopCapture` channel to prevent blocking goroutines
- Fixed packet loss response validation to check for minimum 4 elements
- Simplified loopSampler to suppress transient network errors and continue sampling
- Added `t.Parallel()` to all tests for improved parallel test execution
- Updated golangci-lint configuration for module path
- Added multiple GitHub workflows and updated GoReleaser configurations to support stable and nightly (rolling) releases.

### Changes

- concurrency: Buffer stopCapture channel to prevent goroutine blocking
- bugfix: Fix packet loss response validation to check for minimum 4 elements
- refactor: Simplify loopSampler error handling for transient network failures
- refactor: Add mutex protection for concurrent access in DataManager, Locations, and ByteRate
- test: Add t.Parallel() support across all test functions
- ci: Add GitHub workflows and release pipelines for stable and nightly builds

### Motivation

- Provide a one-step automated installer to provision an Ubuntu chroot inside Termux using `proot-distro` to simplify setup on Android devices. 
- Ensure the Ubuntu environment is usable after install by provisioning packages, creating a non-root `ubuntu` user, configuring locale and timezone, and adding a convenient `ubuntu` alias.

### Description

- Add `scripts/termux_ubuntu_install.sh` which detects Termux, updates packages, installs `proot-distro`, and installs Ubuntu if not present. 
- Create a first-run provisioning script at `$HOME/.termux-ubuntu-init.sh` that runs `apt update/upgrade`, installs essential packages, creates the `ubuntu` user with passwordless sudo, generates `en_US.UTF-8` locale, and sets the timezone. 
- Execute the provisioning inside the installed distro with `proot-distro login ubuntu -- bash /root/.termux-ubuntu-init.sh` and add an `alias ubuntu='proot-distro login ubuntu'` to `~/.bashrc`. 
- Update `README.md` with a usage snippet showing `bash scripts/termux_ubuntu_install.sh`.

### Testing

- Performed a shell syntax check with `bash -n scripts/termux_ubuntu_install.sh` which completed without errors.

author: benbaichmankass
body:
## Summary

CP-2026-05-02-02 follow-up to #261. The previous `.github/workflows/hf-cron.yml` was a single-line shorthand that wasn't valid YAML — every scheduled run since it landed had been failing daily, hiding any real CI failure under a flood of red. This is the cause of the "tons of failed GitHub Actions" the operator flagged.

- **Rewrite `hf-cron.yml` in long form.** Drop the daily cron trigger; the autonomous training/improvement workflow now runs via `training-run.yml` (CP-2026-05-02-01). The file is `workflow_dispatch`-only so the operator can still fire ad-hoc HuggingFace AutoTrain runs manually if needed. Re-enabling the schedule should be a deliberate decision once the AutoTrain dataset is actually wanted on cadence.
- **Add `tests/test_workflow_yaml_valid.py`.** Parametrised over every `.github/workflows/*.yml`; asserts each file parses and has the GitHub Actions minimum shape (top-level `on`/`jobs`, each job has `runs-on` or `uses`). Catches the same bug shape at PR time instead of waiting for the next scheduled run to fail.

## Implications for live trading

None — the broken workflow had no path to the live trader (`ict-trader-live` runs from `main` via `ict-git-sync`, not via Actions). The fix is pure CI hygiene: it stops the daily failure noise and prevents the same shape of bug from recurring silently.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_workflow_yaml_valid.py` — 3 pass (one per workflow file).
- [x] `python3 scripts/check_dry_run_in_diff.py /tmp/pr.diff` — clean.
- [ ] After merge, verify the daily HF cron stops appearing in the Actions tab.

author: alexsiri7
body:
## Summary

Implements OAuth 2.1 + PKCE on the Kindred MCP server so Claude.ai's connector can authenticate end users via Google (proxied through Supabase). Adds the six discovery/AS endpoints required by the November 2025 MCP authorization spec, RFC 8707 resource indicators, and HS256-signed JWT minting/validation. The existing connector-token flow is preserved as a fallback so current users see no regression.

Fixes #11.

## Why

Claude.ai's MCP connector follows a strict 6-step OAuth 2.1 handshake (`POST /mcp` → 401 → `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` → `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` → `/oauth/register` → `/oauth/authorize` → `/oauth/callback` → `/oauth/token` → authenticated `POST /mcp`). Today every step except the final tool call returns 404, so Claude.ai can't connect at all. Tool *invocation* additionally crashes with a `ContextVar LookupError` because the ASGI middleware silently passes unauth requests through.

## Changes

- **New `mcp/oauth/` package** (`__init__.py`, `state.py`, `routes.py`, `supabase.py`):
  - In-memory client/session/auth-code/refresh-token stores guarded by an `asyncio.Lock` (single Uvicorn worker; codes have a 10-min TTL).
  - PKCE S256 verification (RFC 7636 §4.6); `code_challenge_method=plain` is rejected.
  - HS256 JWT mint/verify with audience binding (RFC 8707): `aud = MCP_BASE_URL + "/mcp"` baked in via a `canonical_resource_url()` helper used by both minter and verifier to avoid trailing-slash drift.
  - Six Starlette handlers wired via `mcp.custom_route(...)`: `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (RFC 9728), `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414), `/oauth/register` (RFC 7591), `/oauth/authorize`, `/oauth/callback`, `/oauth/token`.
  - Server-side Supabase code-for-session exchange (anon key, separate from the service-role client used by `mcp/db.py`).
- **`mcp/main.py`**: short-circuit `/.well-known/*` and `/oauth/*` in the ASGI middleware (no auth needed); try JWT first then fall back to the connector-token DB lookup; emit a proper 401 with absolute-URL `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="kindred", resource_metadata="..."` on failure (per claude-code issue #46539, the value must be absolute).
- **`mcp/auth.py`**: `resolve_user_id` now routes by an `eyJ` prefix heuristic (JWT → JWT path; else → DB path); `verify_access_jwt` enforces audience.
- **`mcp/settings.py`**: new fields `mcp_base_url`, `secret_key`, `supabase_jwt_secret`, `supabase_anon_key`.
- **`mcp/requirements.txt`**: add `pyjwt>=2.9` and `httpx>=0.27`.
- **`.env.example`**: document the four new env vars.
- **Tests** (35 new cases across `test_oauth.py`, `test_auth.py`, `test_settings.py`): PKCE roundtrip, JWT roundtrip, every endpoint's happy path + validation rejections, audience enforcement, code reuse, refresh-token rotation, middleware 401 shape.

### Deviations from plan

- Routes are mounted via `FastMCP.custom_route(...)` (the SDK-blessed way to add unauthenticated public routes) instead of rebuilding the ASGI tree with a top-level `Starlette(routes=[...])`. Keeps `build_app()` a one-liner.
- A *mismatched* `resource` parameter on `/authorize` returns 400 `invalid_target` rather than silently overriding the canonical URL — RFC 8707 §2 calls out the confused-deputy risk of silent override.

## Validation evidence

| Gate | Result |
|------|--------|
| `mcp` ruff | All checks passed |
| `mcp` mypy | No issues in 12 source files |
| `mcp` pytest | 51 passed |
| `web/backend` ruff | All checks passed |
| `web/backend` mypy | No issues in 11 source files |
| `web/backend` pytest | 11 passed (no regression in connector-token flow) |
| `web/frontend` lint / typecheck / test / build | All green |

Acceptance criteria from the issue (AC1–AC7) are covered by unit tests except AC3 (end-to-end Claude.ai connector flow), which requires a deploy with the env vars below — see "Manual steps" section.

## Manual steps before deploy

1. Set Railway env vars on the MCP service:
   - `MCP_BASE_URL=https://kindred-mcp.interstellarai.net` (no trailing slash)
   - `SECRET_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)` (≥32 bytes)
   - `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=<from Supabase dashboard>`
   - `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET=<from Supabase dashboard>` (same value web/backend uses)
2. Confirm the Supabase project's redirect-URL allow-list includes `https://kindred-mcp.interstellarai.net/oauth/callback`.

## Out of scope (tracked as follow-ups)

- Persist OAuth state to Supabase (in-memory today; Railway restart kills in-flight flows, but 10-min TTL means Claude.ai retries cleanly).
- JWKS endpoint + RS256 migration.
- One-time-use refresh-token family invalidation.
- Per-tool MCP scopes; revocation endpoint (RFC 7009).
- TTL sweep for in-memory codes/sessions.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on push.
- [ ] After deploy with env vars set: `curl -i https://kindred-mcp.interstellarai.net/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` returns 200 with the canonical resource URL.
- [ ] After deploy: `curl -i -X POST https://kindred-mcp.interstellarai.net/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'` returns 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer ... resource_metadata="https://..."` (absolute URL).
- [ ] After deploy: adding `https://kindred-mcp.interstellarai.net/mcp` to a Claude.ai connector triggers a Google login and tools become callable end-to-end.
- [ ] Existing connector-token paste flow still works for users who already minted one.

body:
## Summary

The toml 0.8 to 1.1 bump (#104) introduced a silent regression in `load_cargo_metadata`. In toml >= 1.0, `Value`'s `FromStr` impl parses a single TOML *value* rather than a TOML *document*, so `raw.parse::<toml::Value>()` on a full `Cargo.toml` returns `Err("unexpected content, expected nothing")` and the loader silently falls back to defaults.

Switch to `toml::from_str(&raw)` so the entire file is interpreted as a document.

## Failures fixed (4 total)

- `settings::tests::cargo_metadata_overrides_defaults` (lib)
- `loads_from_cargo_metadata_only` (tests/integration_settings.rs)
- `nested_database_override_passes_validation` (tests/integration_settings.rs)
- `invalid_environment_is_rejected` (tests/integration_settings.rs)

All four asserted on values loaded from `[package.metadata.surql]` and got defaults instead because parsing aborted at the document boundary.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check` clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean
- `cargo build --workspace --all-features` clean
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast` shows 1054 lib passed / 0 failed and 5/5 in `integration_settings`

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduce 4 failures on origin/main
- [x] Apply 1-line fix in `src/settings.rs`
- [x] Confirm all four tests pass
- [x] Full local gates green

body: ## Summary Phase 2 of the x-radius parity roadmap — turns the panel into a true multi-tenant ISP system with reseller hierarchy and granular per-manager permissions. ### What's new **Database (`db/04-phase2-managers-rbac.sql`, idempotent):** - New `managers` table with self-referencing `parent_id`, JSON `permissions` and `allowed_profile_ids`, `balance`, `profit_share_percent`, `max_users_quota`, `is_root`. - Existing `admin_users` row migrated → root manager (id=1, `permissions=["*"]`); the table is then dropped. - `subscriber_profiles.manager_id` FK added (defaults legacy rows to root). The Phase-1 stub `parent_manager_id` is dropped. - `profiles.owner_manager_id` FK added (NULL = global / shared). **Backend:** - New `app/permissions.py` defines 14 perms: `users.{view,create,edit,delete,renew,toggle}`, `profiles.{view,manage}`, `managers.{view,manage}`, `invoices.{view,manage}`, `reports.view`, `settings.manage`. Wildcard `"*"` grants all. - `app/models.Manager` + Pydantic `ManagerOut/Create/Update/TreeNode/AdminMe`. - `auth.py` rewritten to use `managers` (login, `/auth/me`, `/auth/change-password`); JWT subject is the username, resolved to a Manager in `get_current_manager()`. - `security.py` adds `visible_manager_ids(db, current)` (BFS over the subtree) + `require_permission(*perms)` dependency factory that raises 403 with a clear `Missing permission: X` detail. - New `routers/managers.py`: - `GET /api/managers` — list visible managers (root: all; sub-manager: own subtree) - `GET /api/managers/tree` — nested hierarchy - `POST /api/managers` — create sub-manager. Permissions are sanitized: a sub-manager can never grant a perm it doesn't have, can never grant `"*"`, and `is_root` cannot be set on creation. - `PATCH /api/managers/{id}` — guards root (cannot disable / cannot strip is_root), prevents non-root from escalating their own perms. - `DELETE /api/managers/{id}` — refuses if subtree owns subscribers or has children. - `users.py`, `profiles.py`, `dashboard.py` all scoped: - `_filter_visible_usernames`, `_ensure_user_in_scope`, `_resolve_target_manager_id` for users. - `_allowed_profile_ids_for` whitelist for profiles. - Dashboard radacct/radpostauth/online/lifecycle counters all filtered to the current manager's subtree usernames. - Every endpoint gated with `require_permission(...)`; out-of-scope reads return 404 (masking) instead of 403 to prevent probing. **Frontend:** - `lib/api.ts` adds `Permission` (14 string-literal union), `ALL_PERMISSIONS`, `Manager`, `ManagerTreeNode`, `ManagerCreatePayload`, `ManagerUpdatePayload`, `AdminMe`, plus `manager_id`/`manager_username` on `UserSummary` & `SubscriptionInfo`. - `lib/auth.tsx` hydrates `effective_permissions` from `/auth/me` (and re-fetches after login) and exposes `hasPermission(perm)`. - New `pages/Managers.tsx`: list + tree views, create/edit dialog with a 14-checkbox permission grid, profile-allowlist multi-select, balance / profit-share / quota inputs. - `Layout.tsx` filters nav items by permission (Users / Online users / Profiles / Managers hidden when missing the required perm). - `Users.tsx` table now shows the owning manager's username. - Full EN + AR translations for `nav.managers`, `managers.*`, and per-permission labels. ### Verified locally (Docker stack) ``` ruff app/ → all checks passed npm run lint → 0 errors (4 pre-existing warnings) npm run build → tsc --noEmit OK; vite build OK docker compose build backend → OK mysql < 04-phase2-managers-rbac.sql → idempotent, applied cleanly ``` End-to-end against the live local stack: - `POST /auth/login` (admin/admin) → 200; `/auth/me` returns all 14 `effective_permissions`. - `POST /api/managers` creates `reseller1` with `["users.view","users.create","users.edit"]`, parent=admin, Arabic full_name preserved. - Login as `reseller1`: - `/auth/me.effective_permissions` = exactly the 3 granted perms (no expansion to `"*"`). - `GET /api/managers` → **403 "Missing permission: managers.view"**. - `GET /api/users` → 0 items (no users assigned yet). - `POST /api/users {username:"reseller-bob"}` → 201 with `manager_id=2, manager_username="reseller1"` auto-assigned. - `GET /api/users` (after creation) → 1 item (`reseller-bob`). - `GET /api/users/alice` (owned by root) → **404 "User not found"** (scope masking). - `DELETE /api/users/alice` → **403 "Missing permission: users.delete"**. - Login as root admin: `GET /api/users?q=reseller-bob` → shows the user with `manager_id=2, manager_username="reseller1"`. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Re-confirm the migration is safe to run on the live VPS DB. The script drops `admin_users` and adds the `managers` table. A pre-deploy `mysqldump` backup is recommended (the deploy guide already does this for Phase 1). - [ ] Verify the existing root admin's password from Phase 1 still works after deploy — the migration copies `admin_users.password_hash` verbatim into `managers.password_hash`. - [ ] Smoke-test: create a sub-manager via the new Managers page, log in as that sub-manager, confirm: - Nav hides Managers (no `managers.view` perm) and Profiles (if not granted). - Users page only shows users owned by that manager / its descendants. - Dashboard counters reflect only the scoped users (sessions / accepts / rejects today). - [ ] Click around the Managers page in both English and Arabic (RTL) and check that the permission checkbox grid wraps cleanly on a phone (the dialog is `max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto`). - [ ] (Optional) Verify deletion guards: with a sub-manager that owns subscribers, `DELETE /api/managers/{id}` should 400 with a clear "still owns subscribers" message. ### Notes - This PR does **not** add invoices, WhatsApp/Baileys, VPN, or audit logs — those are Phases 3, 4, 5 in the roadmap. - Out-of-scope reads return 404 (not 403) on purpose to avoid leaking which usernames exist in other managers' subtrees. - The frontend currently does not enforce route guards (a sub-manager who types `/managers` directly will hit the endpoint and get a 403 from the API). Adding route-level guards is a small follow-up if desired. - After merging, the deploy steps for the VPS are: `git pull origin main`, run the migration via `docker compose exec -T db mysql ... < db/04-phase2-managers-rbac.sql`, then `docker compose build` + `up -d`. author: ryanssareen
body:
## Summary
Foundation for the desktop-app build. Converts the single-package repo into npm workspaces:
- \`packages/core/\` — shared agent loop, tools, session io, config, version, update-check.
- \`packages/cli/\` — Ink TUI + login flows. Still publishes as \`@ryanisavibecoder/ccr\`.
- \`packages/electron/\` — empty skeleton ready for Unit 4 (Codex).

Build pipeline: \`tsc\` for \`@ccr/core\`, \`tsup\` for the CLI (inlines \`@ccr/core\` via \`noExternal\`). The published tarball drops from ~38 files to 4: \`package.json\`, \`README.md\`, \`dist/cli.js\`, \`dist/cli.js.map\` — ~115KB total. Sandbox \`npm install /tmp/...tgz\` + \`ccr --version\` confirmed standalone.

## Why tsup instead of \`bundleDependencies\` (per-plan note)
The plan called for \`bundleDependencies: ["@ccr/core"]\` to bundle the workspace package into the published tarball. **\`bundleDependencies\` does not include workspace symlinks under npm 10** (known limitation). tsup is the modern monorepo standard. Result is a smaller, cleaner published artifact. Library-style import from \`@ryanisavibecoder/ccr\` (vestigial) is dropped; the only public surface is the \`ccr\` bin. Consumers wanting library access should depend on \`@ccr/core\` directly (currently a private workspace package; revisit if external library use materializes).

## Test plan
- [x] \`npm run -w @ccr/core build\` and \`npm run -w @ryanisavibecoder/ccr build\` both succeed clean from scratch
- [x] \`npm run -w @ryanisavibecoder/ccr test\` — all 11 terminal-auth scenarios pass
- [x] \`node packages/cli/dist/cli.js --version\` prints \`ccr 1.4.5\`; \`--help\` prints the full help
- [x] \`npm pack -w @ryanisavibecoder/ccr\` produces a 4-file tarball; sandbox install + bin run from a temp dir works without any other packages
- [ ] \`ccr login\` (manual smoke once merged — couldn't run inside the build process)

## Hand-off
Ready for Codex (Unit 4 — Electron scaffold + main-process agent host).

Refs Unit 1 of \`docs/plans/2026-05-02-001-feat-desktop-app-v1-plan.md\`.

author: andreisugu
body:
This pull request introduces major enhancements to the audit logging and recovery features, focusing on improved traceability, data retention, and administrative control. The most significant updates include implementing paginated audit log retrieval, adding point-in-time recovery (PITR) capabilities, introducing audit log archiving (both automated and manual), and updating the frontend to support these features. Additionally, there are improvements to audit rollback logic and notification logging.

**Audit Logging and Recovery Enhancements:**

* Added paginated retrieval of audit logs via the API and updated the frontend to support pagination, making it easier to browse large audit histories. (`backend/src/routes/audit.js`, `src/pages/AuditLogs.jsx`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0da275ab87af85e0f64c855807961fb112cfd7045b269170519981aad4f1f0b3L9-R39) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-13d63344accfdb0faec531bb3d4ea82ae06c1edfbc13176bae5f9b25bd070f71L134-R142)
* Implemented point-in-time recovery (PITR) functionality, allowing administrators to revert all tracked changes to a specific timestamp, with a new UI component for granular recovery. (`backend/src/routes/audit.js`, `src/pages/AuditLogs.jsx`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0da275ab87af85e0f64c855807961fb112cfd7045b269170519981aad4f1f0b3R160-R222) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-13d63344accfdb0faec531bb3d4ea82ae06c1edfbc13176bae5f9b25bd070f71R215-R248) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-13d63344accfdb0faec531bb3d4ea82ae06c1edfbc13176bae5f9b25bd070f71R343-R373)
* Enhanced audit rollback logic to support undoing DELETE actions by re-inserting records, improving the robustness of rollback operations. (`backend/src/routes/audit.js`)

**Audit Log Archiving and Retention:**

* Introduced an audit log archiving mechanism that moves logs older than 5 years to an archive table, with both a scheduled daily job and a manual trigger endpoint, and corresponding frontend controls. (`backend/src/services/auditService.js`, `backend/src/services/schedulerService.js`, `backend/src/routes/admin.js`, `src/pages/AuditLogs.jsx`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4a45ca69022d854ed82a8237f8a47281ed785503f11092b27852bff9b32f2708R147-R191) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b035f81d71c4fdfb99ef15bbf5b688495885590e73a8042ef459e317998d00f2R5-R6) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b035f81d71c4fdfb99ef15bbf5b688495885590e73a8042ef459e317998d00f2R21-R35) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d14e2e00faabcd5cfeebd550296f2898b9682a8acb2e6ee73b881bdcd5b9551dR277-R288) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-13d63344accfdb0faec531bb3d4ea82ae06c1edfbc13176bae5f9b25bd070f71R215-R248)

**Other Improvements:**

* Standardized audit log entries for database recovery actions by using a fixed UUID for the `entity_id` field. (`backend/src/routes/admin.js`, `backend/src/routes/audit.js`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d14e2e00faabcd5cfeebd550296f2898b9682a8acb2e6ee73b881bdcd5b9551dL257-R257) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0da275ab87af85e0f64c855807961fb112cfd7045b269170519981aad4f1f0b3R160-R222)
* Updated notification logging to store the full message body instead of a truncated preview, ensuring complete records of sent communications. (`backend/src/routes/notifications.js`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-827b655147c9a2214722ed46bcdfbad0c5841988c17592a405440e99cfdca37fL95-R96) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-827b655147c9a2214722ed46bcdfbad0c5841988c17592a405440e99cfdca37fL149-R149)

## Summary
Improve `mcaptui` responsiveness and readability when browsing large topics and large message payloads.

## What Changed
- truncate large `List`, `Array`, and `Map` values in the detail pane after 32 items or entries while preserving the total count and showing an omission row

Large decoded payloads could make the detail pane hard to navigate in a terminal, and long topic/message loads could leave the UI without visible progress for too long. This keeps the TUI usable on heavier MCAP inputs.

Users get a more navigable detail pane for large collections and more incremental feedback while loading decoded messages.

author: fenar7
body:
## Summary

- **Primary drag zone moved to the page preview/thumbnail area** in reorder mode. Users can now naturally initiate a drag by grabbing the large image area, which is the intuitive interaction target.
- **Footer controls remain a safe, isolated click zone.** The rotate and delete buttons are siblings (not children) of the preview drag zone, so no `stopPropagation` gymnastics are needed — their events never reach the drag activator.
- **6-dot handle kept as a visual affordance** (`aria-hidden`, no listeners) to communicate reorderability to sighted users without re-introducing drag conflicts.

## Implementation choice

Used dnd-kit's `setActivatorNodeRef` — the purpose-built API for scoping drag initiation to a sub-element while the outer card remains the sortable node. This is the minimal robust approach: no event suppression hacks, no wrapper re-architecture, no workspace-specific patches. The fix lands entirely in the shared `PdfPageGrid` component and automatically applies to both `organize-workspace` and `merge-workspace`.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `components/shared/pdf-page-grid.tsx` | Move `setActivatorNodeRef`, `sortable.attributes`, `sortable.listeners` to preview div; add `cursor-grab` + hover ring; demote handle to `aria-hidden` visual |
| `components/shared/pdf-page-grid.test.tsx` | Expand test coverage: preview zone carries drag affordance, `cursor-grab` class, `tabIndex` from dnd-kit attributes, rotate/delete isolation, non-reorder mode regression |

## Test plan

- [x] `pdf-page-grid.test.tsx` — 13 tests, all green
- [x] `merge-workspace.test.tsx` — 5 tests, all green
- [x] TypeScript — zero errors in changed files (pre-existing unrelated errors elsewhere unchanged)
- [x] Drag affordance present on preview area in reorder mode
- [x] Footer controls (rotate, delete) fire callbacks without interfering with drag
- [x] Non-reorder modes unaffected (no `cursor-grab`, no drag title)
- [x] Keyboard accessibility: `tabIndex={0}` and `aria-roledescription` from `sortable.attributes` placed on the preview activator node

## Non-blocking watchouts

- Touch drag now activates from the preview area (was handle). The 200ms delay / 5px tolerance `TouchSensor` config is unchanged and sufficient. No visual regression for touch users.
- The handle SVG is now `aria-hidden` and has no `cursor-grab`; sighted users who previously grabbed the handle by habit will still see the grip dots and naturally discover the larger preview area is draggable.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

First implementation of `pomo` — a small pomodoro CLI that logs every session to a local SQLite file and gives you simple per-day / per-task aggregations.

**What's included:**
- **CLI** (`src/pomo/cli.py`): Click-based, with `start`, `done`, `cancel`, `current`, `log`, `stats`, `tasks`, and `path` subcommands. `start` runs a live `rich.Live` countdown by default; `--no-wait` only records the start and exits. Completion fires a desktop notification (or terminal bell as a fallback).
- **Storage** (`src/pomo/db.py`, `src/pomo/paths.py`): a single SQLite file at `$XDG_DATA_HOME/pomo/pomo.db` (overridable with `$POMO_HOME`). One `sessions` table with status `running` / `done` / `cancelled` and an index on `started_at`. Schema is created idempotently with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`.
- **Aggregations** (`src/pomo/stats.py`): `per_day` returns one bucket per day in the requested window (including empty days) and `per_task` returns the top tasks by total focused time. `ascii_bar_chart` renders a tiny horizontal bar chart for the stats command.
- **Notifications** (`src/pomo/notify.py`): tries `notify-send` on Linux, AppleScript on macOS, and falls back silently to a terminal bell — every step is best-effort and never raises.
- **Tests** (`tests/`): 17 unit tests covering DB invariants (single-running, status transitions, ordering, status-and-time filtering), stats aggregations (empty days, untagged label, sort order, bar chart widths), and path resolution (`POMO_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, dir creation). All pass locally.
- **CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): ruff + pytest on Python 3.10 / 3.11 / 3.12.
- **README**: install, usage, example output (incl. an example `pomo stats` rendering), storage / `POMO_HOME` notes.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] After merge, change the repo's default branch to `main` in **Settings → Branches** (the integration token couldn't do this automatically — `main` exists but the feature branch is currently default, same as on `soundbox`).
- [ ] Smoke-test the CLI end to end: `pip install -e .` then `pomo start "test" -d 1` (one minute), let it finish, then `pomo log` and `pomo stats --days 1` and confirm the run shows up.
- [ ] Sanity-check the `current` command mid-run: in another terminal run `pomo current` while a session is going and confirm the remaining time looks right.
- [ ] (Optional) Confirm `notify-send` (Linux) or AppleScript (macOS) actually fires when a session completes — falls back silently to a terminal bell otherwise, so absence of a desktop notification isn't a hard failure.

### Notes

- **Time zone handling**: sessions are stored in UTC ISO-8601, and `stats.per_day` buckets them by the **local** calendar date. This is the behavior most people expect for a "today" / "this week" view, but worth flagging — if you regularly travel across time zones, daily counts will look slightly off around the boundary.
- **`POMO_HOME` for syncing**: setting `POMO_HOME=/path/in/Dropbox` is the supported way to keep your pomodoro history in sync across machines. The schema is small + stable + foreign-key-free, so concurrent writes from two machines that occasionally both run pomodoros at the same time are unlikely to cause real conflicts (each gets its own row).
- I used a two-commit history (`Initial commit` on `main` + `feat: initial pomo scaffold` on the feature branch) so the PR has a substantive diff to review.

author: starrlizzard
body:
## Summary

Phase A of the MIDI shaping work for v0.16.0. Continuous MIDI targets (Block Mix, Block Balance, Block Level) now have per-mapping CC range, parameter range, and response curve shaping. Defaults reproduce existing behaviour exactly.

- **Engine** — `MidiMapper::Mapping` extends with `ccMin`, `ccMax`, `paramMin`, `paramMax`, `curve` (Linear/Log/Exp/Sigmoid). `paramMin`/`paramMax` use NaN sentinels for "use parameter default range". `OutboundEvent` snapshots shaping fields on learn-complete to avoid races between audio and message threads. JSON round-trips backwards-compatibly (omitted when default).
- **UI** — `MidiAssignDialog` rebuilt around the Options-panel titlebar pattern (codified in CLAUDE.md). New `ContinuousShaping` block with two anchor columns (CC value, parameter value) and curve-first ordering. New `MappingPreview` SVG renders the curve with d3-shape, ResizeObserver-driven viewBox for distortion-free scaling, hover crosshair + readout. New shared `Select` primitive (Radix-based, dialog-aware z-index) replaces ad-hoc dropdowns in dialog and bypass-mode select.
- **Docs** — Manual page extended with "CC Range and Curves" section. Three new manual test cases (TC-MI-013/014/015) for range mapping, inversion, and curve change.

## Test plan

- [x] `make test` — engine unit tests for `MidiMapper` shaping pass
- [x] `cd ui && npm test` — UI tests for ContinuousShaping, MappingPreview, MidiAssignDialog pass
- [x] Open MIDI assign dialog on Block Mix; verify curve dropdown shows options inside dialog
- [x] Set Min CC=20, Max CC=100, Min Mix=0%, Max Mix=100%; verify CC 50 yields ~37.5%
- [x] Invert: Min Mix=100, Max Mix=0; verify CC 0 → 100%, CC 127 → 0%
- [x] Switch curve to Log/Exp/Sigmoid; verify preview redraws and CC sender produces matching values

This is Phase A of a two-PR v0.16.0 plan. Phase B (per-mapping threshold for binary targets) follows in a separate PR.

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The build was failing with `npm error code EINTEGRITY` because `package-lock.json` contained malformed integrity hashes — the `sha512-` prefix was missing and the checksums didn't match the actual npm registry tarballs. Railpack runs `npm ci`, which strictly validates these hashes, causing every deploy to fail. Additionally, `node_modules/` was committed to the repo and not gitignored, compounding the build issues.

## Solution

Deleted `package-lock.json` entirely so Railpack falls back to `npm install`, which resolves and generates a fresh, valid lockfile at build time. Added `node_modules/` to `.gitignore` to prevent the directory from being tracked in version control going forward.

### Changes
- **Deleted** `package-lock.json`
- **Modified** `.gitignore`

author: arnavpundir22
body:
# NSoC'26

Closes Issue #10

## Summary 
- Five frontend bugs fixed across Navbar, LandingPage, App, and ThemeContext.

### Changes:-
1. Dead Navbar Language Dropdown Removed (Navbar.jsx, Navbar.css)
The 🌐 language button in the Navbar had no effect — selecting a language only called console.log. The real language control is already LanguageFilter inside LandingPage. Removed all dead state, refs, event handlers, JSX, and the corresponding CSS blocks (.language-btn, .language-dropdown*, .language-option*).

2. Search Debounced (LandingPage.jsx)
fetchNews was called on every single keystroke, burning through the NewsAPI free-tier quota (100 req/day). Added a 400 ms debounce via useEffect + a local setTimeout. The live searchQuery still drives client-side filteredArticles for instant UI feedback; only the API call is delayed.

3. Error Boundary Added (ErrorBoundary.jsx new, App.jsx)
Any render crash would silently unmount the entire app. Created a class-based ErrorBoundary with getDerivedStateFromError + componentDidCatch. It shows a friendly "Something went wrong" fallback with a Try again button. Reset increments an internal resetKey to force a full child remount, ensuring the same error doesn't immediately retrigger. Wrapped all page slots in App.jsx.

4. Sports & Health Categories Added; Dead "Local" Removed (LandingPage.jsx)
Sports and Health articles existed in real API responses but had no option in the category dropdown, making them unreachable. Local always returned zero results. Added the former two, removed the latter.

5. Dark-Mode Flash-of-Unstyled-Content Fixed (ThemeContext.jsx)
data-theme was previously applied only inside useEffect, which runs after the first paint — causing a white flash for dark-mode users on page load. Moved the document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', …) and document.body.className writes into the useState lazy initializer so they execute synchronously before React renders anything.

### Testing
- npm run build passes with zero errors ✅
- Pre-existing ESLint warnings (unused vars in unrelated files) are unchanged and not introduced by this PR

## Summary

Brings **factory-LUT 2-bit grayscale rendering** and **native PXC image format** support from crosspoint-reader PR #1614 into CrossInk, plus a user-facing **EPUB Image Quality** setting (Normal/High) so users can opt into the sharper rendering or stay on the legacy differential-LUT path.

### What's in the PR

**PR #1614 port** (most of the diff — already on this branch via earlier merges):
- `GrayscaleMode` (FactoryFast / FactoryQuality / Differential) and `DisplayState` in GfxRenderer
- `secondaryFrameBuffer` + single-pass grayscale render
- DirectPixelWriter API refactor: `beginRow(y, startX)` + `writePixel(value)` (X is now stateful)
- HalDisplay `displayGrayBuffer(turnOff, lut, factoryMode)` — LUT plumbing to SDK
- `open-x4-sdk` submodule bumped to `7dd61fa` "feat: add factory LUT grayscale support"
