author: nokkies
body:
💡 **What:** The `ReadAllCustomNowAsync` method has been refactored to use `Task.WhenAll` to execute custom entry read requests concurrently rather than sequentially.

🎯 **Why:** The previous implementation used a `foreach` loop to `await` each `ReadCustomNowAsync` call sequentially. In a networked environment, this introduces an N+1 query bottleneck because each subsequent read had to wait for the previous roundtrip to complete, heavily degrading UI performance when there were many custom entries.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** In a standalone benchmark simulating 100 entries and a 10ms network round-trip delay per read:
*   **Baseline (Sequential):** ~1200 ms
*   **Optimized (Task.WhenAll):** ~13 ms
*   **Net Improvement:** ~99% faster for the specific network I/O bounds, scaling horizontally rather than sequentially.

author: fmguerreiro
body:
## Summary

Closes #303.

`pg_proc.{proargtypes, prorettype}` and `pg_aggregate.aggtranstype` are bare OIDs with no per-arg typmod, so introspect emits `numeric` for `numeric(10,2)`, `character varying` for `varchar(255)`, etc. The parser, however, preserved the user-supplied form. `Function::signature()` keys diverged for any scalar typmod-bearing arg, return type, or aggregate stype — mirroring the gh#299 array-element pattern fixed in #304 but for scalars.

The fix extends `normalize_pg_type` to strip a trailing `(...)` typmod after the `public.` prefix strip and before alias canonicalization. Order of operations is now:

1. `TABLE(...)` — recurse per column
2. `SETOF` — recurse on inner
3. Array `[]` — recurse on element (recursion now also handles the typmod strip, so the explicit `strip_outer_typmod` call in this branch is folded in)
4. Strip `public.`
5. Strip trailing `(...)` typmod (new)
6. Alias canonicalization

This is consistent with the precedent from #304 where storage-time normalization was used for arrays. The cosmetic concern about emitted DDL preserving user input precision (`numeric(10,2)` → `numeric` in pgmold-emitted SQL) applies equally to the array case from #304 and is tracked separately in #305 as an architectural follow-up; PG drops the typmod on its end regardless, so the resulting `pg_proc` state is identical.

## Test plan

- [x] `function_signature_strips_scalar_typmod` — the parser-vs-introspect equality assertion that the issue asked for. Replaces the `function_signature_preserves_scalar_typmod` scope marker added in #304.
- [x] `function_arg_semantically_equals_scalar_typmod_alias` — sentinel asserting `numeric(10,2)` ≡ `numeric` at the `FunctionArg::semantically_equals` layer.
- [x] `normalize_pg_type_strips_typmod` (renamed from `_strips_array_element_typmod`) — extends the unit-level checks to cover `char(2) → character`, `numeric(10,2) → numeric`, `varchar(255) → character varying`, leaving the array assertions intact.
- [x] `normalize_pg_type_handles_common_aliases` — `timestamp(6) → timestamp without time zone`, `time(6) → time without time zone` (typmod-strip + alias), and `timestamp(3) with time zone` is preserved (input does not end in `)` so the strip is a no-op).
- [x] `parse_function_signature_handles_nested_parens_in_types` — the grant-key path now produces the canonical `public.trunc(numeric)`.
- [x] `canonical_args_strips_numeric_precision` — comment-key path produces `numeric`, matching the introspect side.
- [x] `parse_function_arguments_with_commas_in_type` — the `parse_function_arguments` helper used by introspect emits the bare `numeric`.
- [x] Existing convergence corpus (`tests/corpus/sagri_mrv.sql`) only uses `char(2)[]` (array) for typmod-bearing function args, so no canary regression risk.

author: hasparus
body: ## Summary The `@hasparus/tailwind` package's `exports` field only declared the `require` condition — no `import`. Modern bundlers that resolve using the `import` condition (notably `@tailwindcss/vite`) fail to resolve the package even though `dist/*.js` are ESM. ## Repro In a Vite project using `@tailwindcss/vite`: ```css @plugin "@hasparus/tailwind/scrollview-fade"; ``` Vite errors: ``` [vite] Internal server error: "./scrollview-fade" is not exported under the conditions ["module", "browser", "development", "import"] from package @hasparus/tailwind ``` ## Fix Add `"import"` alongside `"require"` in both subpath exports. Move `"types"` first per [Node.js docs](https://nodejs.org/api/packages.html#conditional-exports) recommendation (TS resolves first match). Bump 1.1.7 → 1.1.8. ```jsonc "exports": { ".": { "types": "./src/index.ts", "import": "./dist/index.js", "require": "./dist/index.js" }, "./scrollview-fade": { "types": "./src/scrollview-fade.ts", "import": "./dist/scrollview-fade.js", "require": "./dist/scrollview-fade.js" } } ``` ## Test plan - [x] Verified locally in a Vite + `@tailwindcss/vite` project: `@plugin "@hasparus/tailwind/scrollview-fade"` resolves; CSS compiles with all `scrollview-fade-*` utilities and the two `@property` rules. - [x] Publish 1.1.8 after merge. ---

author: teknium1
body:
When `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is set in both the parent shell (stale) and `~/.hermes/.env` (fresh), `_seed_from_env` now prefers the `.env` value. Before this fix, any stale export from a parent process (Codex CLI, test scripts, previous install) silently overrode the key the user just wrote to `.env`, wrote the stale value to `auth.json`, and caused persistent 401 errors with no obvious cause.

Cherry-picked from @franksong2702's #18256 onto current main, plus 2 regression tests (precedence + fallback).

## What changed
- `agent/credential_pool.py`: `_seed_from_env` uses a local `_get_env_prefer_dotenv()` helper that reads `~/.hermes/.env` first, then falls back to `os.environ`.
- `tests/agent/test_credential_pool.py`: 2 regression tests added —
  - `test_load_pool_prefers_dotenv_over_stale_os_environ` covers the bug.
  - `test_load_pool_falls_back_to_os_environ_when_dotenv_empty` guards the Docker/K8s/systemd path where `.env` is absent and runtime env vars are the only source.

## Why only in credential-pool seeding (not globally)
The `.env` file is the user's managed Hermes config; inside Hermes' own credential-pool cache seeding, it's authoritative. General env resolution (`hermes_cli/env_loader.py`) still honors 12-factor precedence (os.environ wins) for runtime-injected secrets — changing that would break Docker/K8s deployments that only set env vars. The narrow scope here only affects which value ends up written to `auth.json`, not general env resolution.

## Validation
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_credential_pool.py` → 41 passed (39 existing + 2 new).
- E2E: real `HERMES_HOME`, real `.env` file, stale shell export of `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, seeded `auth.json` with the stale key. After `load_pool("openrouter")`: selected entry's access_token is the fresh `.env` value, and `auth.json` on disk is rewritten with the fresh key.

Closes #18254.

author: lanteiraph
body:
## Summary

Opt-in debug overlay that visualises anchored-object placement state on the canvas. Useful when "the image looks wrong" — surfaces the exclusion area, the page-edge clamp boundary, and the paint-order metadata.

When \`editor.debug.anchoredObjects\` is true, paints on every visible page:

author: lawsonak
body:
## Summary

The bulk upload's background removal used to require the tab to stay open because `@imgly/background-removal` ran in the browser. With the server scaled to 6 cores / 6GB, it's now realistic to run the same model server-side. The user can close the tab the moment uploads finish.

## Server-side additions

- **Deps**: `@imgly/background-removal-node` + `onnxruntime-node`. CPU-only ONNX inference. Model lazy-loaded once per Node process.
- **`lib/bgRemovalServer.ts`** — wraps the package, runs a worker pool at concurrency **3** (sweet spot for 6 cores: enough throughput without starving Next.js + Prisma).
- **`/api/items/bg-remove-batch`** — accepts `{ itemIds, background: true }`, kicks off processing, returns immediately with a queued ack. Fires a `Notification` when done (or fails) just like `/api/ai/tag-bulk`. Per-user inflight lock prevents double-batching.
- **`next.config.mjs`** — marks both packages as `serverComponentsExternalPackages` so webpack doesn't try to bundle the native `.node` binary or the on-disk model assets.

## Wizard changes

- **Step 1**: "Remove backgrounds" toggle copy flips from "Runs in this tab — keep it open" to "Runs on the server. Safe to close the tab — you'll get a notification."
- **Step 2**: no longer has a separate bg phase or per-job `removing-bg` state. After uploads finish, AI tagging and bg removal both fire in parallel as background dispatches; wizard auto-advances to step 3 immediately.
- **Step 3**: new ✂️ banner alongside the 🤖 AI banner when server bg removal is queued.
- The persistent "background removal stops if you close" warning is gone — neither flow stops on tab close anymore.

Single-photo edits (`ItemPhotoEditor`, `ItemAngles`, `AddItemForm`) still use the browser-side `lib/bgRemoval.ts`. The user is already on those pages.

## Expected perf on 6c/6GB

~5-10s per photo, 3 in parallel. A 50-photo batch finishes in ~3-5 minutes after the user closes the tab.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`
- [ ] After deploy: bulk-upload 5 photos with bg removal on → confirm step 3 shows the ✂️ banner; close the tab; ~30s later confirm the notification bell shows "Background removal complete" and items have `imageBgRemovedPath` populated
- [ ] Larger batch (20+ photos) → confirm server stays responsive (other pages still load while batch runs)
- [ ] First call after server restart takes longer (model download) — confirm it doesn't time out

author: ansocode
body:
## Summary

Phase 2b of the open-core hybrid extraction. After Phase 2a (PR #880, merged) wired the public-side loader to dynamic-import `@studio-saelix/sencho-pro`, this PR makes production Docker builds actually install the package so the runtime path uses it.

**Single image.** `saelix/sencho` remains the only published image. The original ADR's dual-image plan was rejected because customers buying paid tiers would otherwise need GitHub auth to pull a second image, breaking the purchase flow. Same image for Community and paid; activation is a license-key paste in Settings, identical to today.

## What changed (2 files)

### `Dockerfile` (prod-deps stage)

After `npm ci --omit=dev`, a new `RUN` block installs `@studio-saelix/sencho-pro` using a BuildKit secret-mounted `github_token` for `npm.pkg.github.com` auth.

- `.npmrc` carrying the token is written and removed inside the same `RUN`. `/root/.npm` is wiped to scrub potential verbose-log artifacts.
- The token never enters an image layer — BuildKit excludes secret content from both layer filesystems and cache keys; `docker history` shows the literal `$(cat /run/secrets/...)` command, not the substituted value.
- Empty-secret branch (no `github_token` provided, e.g. local dev or fork PRs) skips the install with a notice. The image still runs through the loader's in-tree `LicenseService` fallback.

`PRO_PACKAGE_VERSION` is a build arg pinned by CI to a literal SemVer (`0.1.0` today) so the scan build and the publish build resolve to the same package version. Default of `latest` keeps local builds convenient; CI always overrides. When the pro package ships a new version, bump this string in `docker-publish.yml` in the same PR that ships the matching public Sencho release.

### `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml`

Both `docker/build-push-action` invocations (pre-publish scan + multi-arch publish) now pass:

```yaml
secrets: |
  github_token=${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
build-args: |
  ...
  PRO_PACKAGE_VERSION=0.1.0
```

The auto-provisioned `GITHUB_TOKEN`'s `packages:read` scope is sufficient because the public Sencho repo and the private package live in the same `Studio-Saelix` GitHub org. Moving the package to a different org would silently break this contract; the Dockerfile comment block records the invariant.

## What's NOT changed

`ci.yml`'s PR-time Docker validation job is intentionally not modified. PRs from forks have no access to the org's packages; passing the secret would split behavior. The PR build runs the empty-secret branch and exercises the loader's in-tree fallback path — proves the image still builds without the package. Production publish is the only place the install actually runs.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit` clean (no TS changes)
- [x] Code-reviewer: ship-ready after MEDIUM-1 (version-pin via build-arg) and MEDIUM-2 (npm log scrub) folded in. NIT-3 (same-org-required comment) also added.
- [ ] **CI exercises the conditional logic** when this PR runs the `Docker Build & Scan` job — without the secret, the empty-secret branch fires and the build still succeeds.
- [ ] **First post-merge release** is the only place the actual install + publish path runs end-to-end. The pre-publish smoke test boots the image and calls `/api/health`; `loadEntitlementProvider()` runs during bootstrap before the listener binds, so a failed dynamic import or constructor throw would prevent `/api/health` from ever returning 200 and the smoke test would fail.

## Out of scope

**Cleanup PR (after Phase 2b is verified working in production):** remove `services/LicenseService.ts` from the public repo and switch the loader fallback from `LicenseService.getInstance()` to `new CommunityEntitlementProvider(...)`. The Community fallback still serves a purpose (local dev environments without GitHub Packages auth, future explicit Community-only builds).

**Phase 3 (future):** add Cloud Backup wire format, telemetry, and other genuinely-private modules to the same `@studio-saelix/sencho-pro` package as new exports. The Dockerfile install path covers them automatically.

body:
## Problem

Nixpacks was ignoring the `.nvmrc` file and defaulting to Node.js 18.20.5, causing the Next.js build to fail with "Node.js version '>=20.9.0' is required". Neither the `.nvmrc` nor the `engines` field in `web/package.json` was sufficient to override Nixpacks' Node.js version selection.

## Solution

Added a `nixpacks.toml` at the repo root that explicitly sets `nixPkgs = ["nodejs_20"]` in the setup phase. This is the authoritative way to pin a Node.js version in Nixpacks and will override any auto-detected version, ensuring the build runs on Node.js 20 as Next.js requires.

### Changes
- **Created** `nixpacks.toml`

## Summary

Production security hardening. All changes reviewed via `production-code-audit` skill.

### Critical fixes
- **Authorization header**: was truncated to 8 chars + `...`, now uses full `${panel_token}` (API calls were silently failing)

- **yq auto-install**: install script downloads yq for safe YAML parsing, graceful grep/awk fallback

author: wifsimster
body:
## Summary

Three targeted fixes to `.github/workflows/release.yml`:

1. **Drop the dead race-handler loop in `publish`.**
   The job had a 3-attempt push/rebase loop guarding against a sibling Release run racing on main. With the workflow's concurrency group (`release-main`, `cancel-in-progress: false`) whole runs are already serialized, so the loop is unreachable in practice. Worse, its "sibling won — exit 0" branches did **not** short-circuit the `Create GitHub Release` step that follows, which would then fail trying to (re)create a release for an existing tag. Replaced with a plain push that fails loudly.

2. **Fix `BUILD_DATE`.**
   It was set from `github.event.repository.updated_at`, which is the repo's last-update timestamp at trigger time — not the build time. Now captured once in the `decide` job via `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` and exposed as an output, so both arch matrix builds stamp the same value into the OCI image label.

3. **Treat `refactor:` commits as patch releases.**
   They ship user-visible changes (e.g. #125 — admin moderation UI consolidation) and were silently dropped by the previous regex.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes on this branch
- [ ] Manual trigger of `workflow_dispatch` still works (path unchanged)
- [ ] Next merge to main with a `refactor:` commit produces a patch release
- [ ] Inspect a future image: `docker buildx imagetools inspect wifsimster/the-box:latest` should show `org.opencontainers.image.created` matching the workflow run time, not the repo's last-push time

body:
## Summary

### Cart correctness (P1)
- **`CartContext.addToCart` race fixed.** Synchronous `useRef` flag replaces the `if (isLoading) return` guard so two rapid clicks can no longer both pass it and create duplicate Shopify carts.
- **"Buy it now" reuses existing cart.** Previously created a fresh cart on every click and silently abandoned anything in the user's drawer.
- **`CartContext.loadCart` no longer wipes localStorage on transient Shopify 5xx.** Two consecutive throws no longer empty real users' carts during brief outages — we only clear when Shopify definitively returns null (cart deleted/expired).
- **`CartDrawer` clears pending gift-attribute debounce on unmount.** No more `setTimeout` firing `updateAttributes()` against an abandoned drawer state.
- **`CartUpsell` stops double-fetching.** Recommendations API now carries full variant data (including images) so the second `getProductsByHandles` round-trip is gone on the happy path. `getProductsByCollection` projects `variant.image` to support this.

### Accessibility (P1/P2)
- **`TradeOrderForm` errors are announced.** Both PIN-stage and order-stage error messages wrapped in `role="alert" aria-live="assertive"` — screen reader users now hear "Invalid PIN".
- **`AgeGate` focuses the dialog, not the Yes button.** Previous behaviour announced the affirmative button before the heading and legal warning.
- **CartDrawer ✓/✗ discount glyphs are screen-reader-friendly.** `aria-hidden` glyphs with `sr-only` "Applied: " / "Not applicable: " labels.
- **HeroSection carousel announces slide changes.** `aria-roledescription="carousel"` + polite live region.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green (Build, Lint/Typecheck, CodeQL)
- [ ] Devtools throttling → click Add-to-cart twice in <100ms — only one cart is created (was two)
- [ ] Add an item to cart, click "Buy it now" on a different product — checkout shows BOTH items
- [ ] Open cart drawer with a gift message, close drawer immediately — no stale `updateAttributes` request fires (Network tab)
- [ ] Open cart drawer — `Network` shows one `cart-recommendations` request, no follow-up `getProductsByHandles` call

- [ ] First-time visit triggers AgeGate → screen reader reads heading + description before button

body:
### Motivation

- Make CORS handling more flexible per-request so the API can respond with the appropriate `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` for hosted instances using comma-separated origins.  
- Improve external price lookup robustness by matching a variety of symbol formats from Chainlink/Pyth feeds.  
- Expose a compact `mapped-prices` endpoint that returns a single normalized price per market and ensure market data is fresh when requested.

### Description

- Introduced `resolveCorsOrigin(req)` and replaced hard-coded `config.corsOrigin` usage in `writeJson`, `writeSseHead`, and `writeMetrics` so the response `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` is resolved from the incoming request.  
- Changed JSON/SSE/metrics helper signatures to accept `req` (`writeJson(req, res, ...)`, `writeSseHead(req, res)`, `writeMetrics(req, res, ...)`) and updated all call sites accordingly.  
- Re-ordered the health and authorization checks so health endpoints remain public and private routes are still protected by `isAuthorized(req)`.  
- Added a new `mapped-prices` API (`GET /mapped-prices` and `/v1/mapped-prices`) that refreshes the market snapshot if empty, then returns per-market `mappedPrice` and `source` chosen from Chainlink or Pyth (Chainlink preferred).  
- Ensured `GET /markets` refreshes market snapshot when empty by calling `refreshMarketSnapshot(...)` before returning data.  
- In `marketData.js`, added `symbolCandidates` and `lookupExternalPrice` helpers to normalize symbol formats (e.g. `BTCUSDT`, `BTC/USDT`, `BTC-USD`, `BTCUSD`, etc.) and use them to lookup `pyth` and `chainlink` entries when building the market snapshot.  

### Testing

- Ran the project's automated test suite with `npm test` and lint checks; all tests completed successfully.  
- Manually exercised API endpoints in a local environment to validate `GET /health`, `GET /markets`, and `GET /mapped-prices` returned expected payload shapes and that CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` reflects allowed origins.  
- Verified that external feed lookups now match feeds with alternate symbol formats and that `mapped-prices` prefers Chainlink when available.

author: jfberry
body:
## Summary

Two related changes landed on this branch:

1. **Forum-topic delivery + commands** — Poracle can now deliver alerts to a Telegram supergroup forum topic (via `discord:topic`-style composite IDs `<chatID>:<topicID>` and `bot.TypeTelegramTopic`), and the polling bot recognises commands run inside topics so `/track`, `/area`, `/channel add` etc. all target the topic's human row rather than the parent group.

2. **Telegram library migration** — swapped the unmaintained `github.com/go-telegram-bot-api/telegram-bot-api/v5 v5.5.1` (last touched 2021) for the actively-maintained `github.com/go-telegram/bot v1.20.0`. The new library has first-class topic support, which let us delete most of the v5.5.1 forum-topic JSON-decode workaround that landed earlier on the branch.

## Changes

### Delivery (phase 1)
- `bot.TypeTelegramTopic = \"telegram:topic\"`.
- `delivery/telegram.go` splits a composite `<chatID>:<topicID>` Target, threads `topicID` through every `send*` helper, and applies `message_thread_id` to each request body. The persisted sentID stores the composite chat segment so Edit/Delete can recover the topic.
- Tests cover the split, send-with-topic, no-thread-id-on-plain-group, and edit-strips-topic paths.

### Polling bot (phase 2)
- `handleMessage` reads `m.MessageThreadID` and uses `composeTopicChannelID` for `ctx.ChannelID` so `BuildTarget` looks up the topic's human row.
- Reply path threads the topic through `sendReplies(chatID, threadID, userID, replies)` and the per-step send helpers.
- `/channel add` inside a topic registers `telegram:topic` with the composite ID.
- `/identify` reports chat + topic + user IDs.

### Library migration (12 commits, plus a review-driven cleanup)
- `*tgbotapi.BotAPI` → `*gotgbot.Bot`. Polling now uses `WithDefaultHandler` + `b.api.Start(ctx)`.
- `*tgbotapi.Message` → `*models.Message`. `MessageThreadID` is a first-class field, so the v5.5.1 raw-JSON re-decode in `topic.go` is gone (~85 lines deleted).
- `member.Status` → `member.Type` (`models.ChatMemberType` enum). A small `chatMemberUser` helper extracts the User pointer from the discriminated-union variants (Owner, Administrator, Member, Restricted, Left, Banned).
- `api/config_resolve.go`'s `GetChat` is now context-aware (`c.Request.Context()` propagates).
- Old library dropped from `go.mod` after migration.

### Review + simplify pass
- Panic-recovery deferred in `handleUpdate` (the new library does NOT recover handler panics).
- `Bot.Close()` made idempotent via `sync.Once`.
- Dropped redundant `sendPlainToTopic` (functionally identical to `sendTopicMessage`).
- `reconciliation.sendSplitMessage` now delegates to `bot.SplitMessage` instead of hand-rolling a splitter.
- 4 sites switched from `m.Chat.Type == \"private\"` to `m.Chat.Type == models.ChatTypePrivate`.

## Test plan

Build + automated tests:
- [x] `go test ./...` — all 25 packages green
- [x] `go build ./cmd/processor` — 53MB binary builds clean
- [x] `gofmt -d ./...` — clean
- [ ] CI Docker build green

Manual smoke (against a live Telegram test guild, after the build):
- [ ] `/identify` in DM → bot replies with user ID
- [ ] `/identify` in a group → bot replies with chat + user ID
- [ ] `/identify` in a forum topic → bot replies with chat + topic + user ID
- [ ] `/poracle` registration in a group
- [ ] `/track everything iv100` in a DM → tracking row added; `/tracked` shows it
- [ ] `/channel add` inside a forum topic → registers \`telegram:topic\` with composite ID
- [ ] A real webhook fires and an alert lands in the topic
- [ ] Existing (non-topic) Telegram alert delivery still works for groups and DMs
- [ ] Reconciliation \`/start\` DM flow still works (channel-membership probe via \`GetChatMember\`)

## Out of scope

- Discord bot (different SDK, untouched).
- Webhook-mode polling for the new library — kept poll-based to preserve deployment story.
- Sequential-vs-parallel \`GetChat\`/\`GetChatMember\` calls in startup/reconciliation — pre-existing pattern, not introduced by this branch.
- Telegram name-composition fragmentation across 4 sites — predates this branch.

body:
## Summary

- Add `rsigma_detection_matches_by_rule_total{rule_title, level}` and `rsigma_correlation_matches_by_rule_total{rule_title, level, correlation_type}` as labeled `IntCounterVec` metrics alongside the existing aggregate counters.
- Extend the `MetricsHook` trait with two new default methods (`on_detection_match_detail`, `on_correlation_match_detail`) so `NoopMetrics` and external consumers remain backward-compatible.
- Add `Level::as_str()` and `CorrelationType::as_str()` to `rsigma-parser` for label string conversion.
- Update the README metrics table to include all 19 metrics with a Labels column.

## What this enables

A single PromQL query like `increase(rsigma_detection_matches_by_rule_total[5m]) > 0` produces separate alert instances for each `{rule_title, level}` combination, replacing the need for N individual alert rules. This is inspired by the Grafana Managed Alerting's [dynamic labels](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/alerting/examples/dynamic-labels/) feature.

author: neuromechanist
body:
## Summary

- Wires the Phase 3 audio encoder to a native Swift Qwen3 text decoder, giving the engine a complete Swift / MLX-Swift transcription path with no Python sidecar.
- New `Qwen3ASRPipeline.transcribe(pcm:language:maxNewTokens:)` returns `Qwen3ASRTranscription { text, language, generatedTokens, numAudioTokens, totalSeconds }`. Output matches the upstream `mlx_audio` Python reference exactly on the canonical clip and on the EN/AR/FA WER subsets.
- New `Qwen3ASRTextDecoder` (28 layers, 16/8 attention/KV heads, head_dim 128, hidden_size 2048, intermediate_size 6144, tied word embeddings) with a precomputed-embeddings forward used by the pipeline after splicing audio_tower hidden states into the prompt.

## Parity (canonical 12.6 s English clip)

| Check | Reference | Swift | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt token IDs | 179 | 179 | exact |
| `<|audio_pad|>` slots | 164 | 164 | exact |
| audio_tower output count | 164 | 164 | exact |
| Generated tokens | greedy stream | identical | exact |
| Decoded text | (Python ref) | identical | exact |
| Detected language | English | English | exact |

## WER subset parity (5 utterances per language)

| Lang | Python WER | Swift WER | Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EN | 0.0842 | 0.0842 | 0.0000 |
| AR | 0.1200 | 0.1200 | 0.0000 |
| FA | 0.4000 | 0.4000 | 0.0000 |

## Latency micro-benchmark

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Cold-start pipeline load | ~1.1 s |
| Resident memory after load | ~2.5 GB |
| Warm transcribe — 2 s clip | ~0.15 s |
| Warm transcribe — 5 s clip | ~0.32 s |
| Warm transcribe — 15 s clip | ~0.70 s |

4. Ensuring `vibe/index.html` uses absolute paths for the main entry point to support deep-link refreshes.

All backend tests passed and frontend verification confirmed that SPA routing and reloads work correctly without MIME type issues.

body:
…tendus

L'utilisateur signale 3 problèmes :
1. "Donne-moi les corrigés" → bot redemande la quantité d'exercices au lieu de générer les corrigés des exercices déjà fournis.
2. Les matières proposées dans la clarification sont génériques et ne reflètent pas le programme officiel CEB (Curriculum de l'Éducation de Base) du Ministère.
3. Demande de tests et d'audit du bot.

CHANGEMENTS

A. Nouvel intent "correction_request"
   - Ajouté à la taxonomie VALID_INTENTS (passe de 10 à 11 intents)
   - Documenté dans le prompt classifier avec règle critique : "Donne-moi les corrigés / Les corrections / Tu peux corriger ? / Les réponses / Les solutions → correction_request, JAMAIS exercise_request"
   - Few-shot prompting : 2 exemples ajoutés
   - Heuristique fallback : détecte "corrigé(s)", "correction(s)", "corriger", "solutions", "réponses" mais EXCLUT les cas où l'utilisateur veut de NOUVEAUX exercices :
     - "donne-moi des exercices avec corrigé" → exercise_request
     - "d'autres exercices" → exercise_request - "génère 5 exercices" → exercise_request - "donne-moi les corrigés" seul → correction_request
   - Bug regex : (exercice|exo|devoir)\b ne matchait pas "exercices" pluriel → ajout de s? : (exercice|exo|devoir)s?

B. Module INTENT_MODULES["correction_request"] (nlp_service.py)
   - Format strict : ### Corrigés des exercices, puis ### Exercice 1, Énoncé:, Solution: (raisonnement pas-à-pas), Réponse: (résultat)
   - Pour les maths : montre le RAISONNEMENT, pas juste le résultat
   - Pour le français : réponse + EXPLICATION grammaticale
   - Si l'historique ne contient pas d'exos : honnête + propose d'en générer

C. Handler _handle_correction (chat_service.py)
   - Recherche dans l'historique le DERNIER message assistant qui contient "Exercice 1" ou "exercice 1"
   - Si trouvé : enrichit le message LLM avec les exercices à corriger (jusqu'à 2500 chars), demande les corrigés ordonnés
   - Si pas trouvé : propose à l'utilisateur de générer des exercices d'abord (clarification structurée avec boutons)

D. Matières adaptées au programme CEB officiel sénégalais
   Méthode statique _get_subjects_for_level(niveau) qui retourne :
   - CI/CP (Étape 1) : Langue et Communication, Mathématiques, Découverte du Monde, EPS, Vivre Ensemble, Arts
   - CE1/CE2 (Étape 2) : ajout Anglais (initiation)
   - CM1/CM2 (Étape 3) : Sciences et Vie, Histoire-Géo, Anglais, Éducation Civique et Morale (préparation CFEE)
   - Préscolaire : Langage, Découverte du Monde, Activités d'éveil
   - Collège (6e/5e) : Mathématiques, Français, Histoire-Géo, SVT, Sciences Physiques, Anglais, ECM, EPS
   - Collège (4e/3e) : ajout Espagnol et Arabe (LV2)
   - Lycée : Mathématiques, Français, Philosophie, Histoire-Géo, SVT, Physique-Chimie, Anglais, Espagnol, Arabe, EPS

E. Tests pytest étendus (44/44 passants, +12 nouveaux)
   - test_heuristic_correction (6 cas)

body:
## Summary

- **Fix inflación ×4.33**: la fórmula de Simulator.scala dividía por `86_400_000` ms/día y luego multiplicaba por `hourMultiplier` sin normalizar. Con `sum(HourDistribution) = 104`, generaba 4.33× más personas de lo esperado. Ahora: `baseCount = dailyEntrance × hourMultiplier / 104 × TimeStepMs / 3_600_000`, lo que garantiza que la integral diaria = `dailyEntrance`.
- **Fix andenes simétricos**: el frontend dividía el total de la línea entre el nº de andenes en la estación → siempre el mismo valor por dirección. Ahora se envían conteos per-andén (`CODIGOANDEN`) y per-actor-de-estación desde el backend.
- **Gente en tránsito**: los datos de estación ya se trackeaban en el simulador pero solo llegaban como totales por línea. Ahora se envían por actor de estación y el frontend los suma correctamente por estación física (con matching de nombres sin diacríticos).

## Cambios

**Backend (`metro-sim`)**
- `Simulator.scala`: nueva fórmula de spawn; `partialPerson` separado del multiplicador de hora
- `messages/Messages.scala`: dos nuevos `UIMessage` — `PeopleInSpecificPlatform(anden, people)` y `PeopleInSpecificStation(stationId, people)`
- `Line.scala`: en cada `LineTick` reenvía conteos individuales de andén y estación a UI
- `UI.scala`: publica `peopleInPlatform:{codigoanden}` y `peopleInStation:{stationId}` al WebSocket

**Frontend (`metro`)**
- `messages.ts`: interfaces `PeopleInPlatform` y `PeopleInStation`
- `simulation-state.service.ts`: mapas `andenPeople` y `stationIdPeople`; se limpian en reset
- `train.component.ts`: `buildStationLineMap` también construye `stationPlatformIds`; `stationLabelItems` usa counts per-andén (rompe la simetría) y suma actors por estación física para tránsito

## Test plan

- [ ] Arrancar simulador y esperar 2 min simulados: verificar que en Empalme los dos andenes muestran valores distintos
- [ ] Verificar que el número total de personas en el sistema es razonable (no 80 personas por andén a los 2 min)
- [ ] Verificar que el panel de estación muestra TRANSIT con personas en tránsito (entre entrada y andén)
- [ ] Verificar que el reset limpia los nuevos conteos correctamente

body:
## Task Manager REST API with Flask and SQLite

**Complexity:** medium

### Requirements

1. Implement a Flask-based REST API providing endpoints to perform CRUD operations on tasks.
2. Persist tasks in a SQLite database with fields: task id, description, priority, due date, and created/updated timestamps.
3. Implement user authentication via API keys; each API request must include a valid API key to access endpoints.
4. Validate input data for tasks, ensuring priorities follow allowed values (e.g., low, medium, high) and due dates are valid ISO 8601 date strings.
5. Handle error scenarios gracefully, returning appropriate HTTP status codes and messages for authentication failures, invalid data, not found tasks, etc.
6. Support common CRUD operations for tasks: create (POST), read (GET), update (PUT/PATCH), and delete (DELETE).
7. Ensure that the API only allows authenticated users to access and manipulate their own tasks (tasks must be associated with a user).

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a valid API key, when a client sends a POST request to /tasks with valid task data, then a new task is created and persisted with status 201.
2. Given an invalid or missing API key, when any endpoint is accessed, then the API returns a 401 Unauthorized response.
3. Given a request with invalid task data (e.g., malformed due date), when the client sends it to the API, then the API returns a 400 Bad Request response.
4. Given a valid API key and task ID, when the client sends a GET request to /tasks/{id}, then the API returns the corresponding task data with status 200.
5. Given a valid API key and task ID, when the client sends a DELETE request to /tasks/{id}, then the task is deleted and the API returns status 204.
6. Given a valid API key and correct task modification data, when the client sends a PUT or PATCH request to /tasks/{id}, then the task is updated accordingly with status 200.
7. Given a valid API key, when a client requests a list of tasks, then the API returns only tasks owned by the API key's user with status 200.

### QA Review

**Verdict:** APPROVED | **Score:** 96% | **Iterations:** 1

author: hariseldon343
body:
## Summary

Adds a persistent DB-backed cache for OpenAI embedding API calls inside `cnx_openai_embed_texts()`. Hits return without an API call; misses are batched into a single OpenAI request and stored with `INSERT IGNORE` (safe under parallel writes).

- New table `embedding_cache` (migration `88_embedding_cache.sql`) keyed by `(text_hash, model)` with binary float32 vectors via `pack('g*', ...)`.
- 100% backward-compatible wrapper: same input/output shape, same error contract.
- Feature flag `RAG_EMBEDDING_CACHE_ENABLED` (default `true`) for emergency rollback without dropping the table.
- Per-call hit/miss counters logged as JSON-lines to `logs/embedding_cache.log`.
- CLI maintenance tool `tools/embedding_cache_stats.php` with `--prune-older=DAYS`.

## Why

Embeddings are deterministic for `(model, normalized_text)`. The RAG pipeline (indexing + retrieval) repeatedly embeds identical chunks and recurring queries. A persistent cache eliminates redundant API spend (e.g. ~$0.02 / 1M tokens on `text-embedding-3-small` adds up on bulk re-index) and removes ~100–300ms per call of network round-trip.

**Hit rate target:** >70% combined (>80% indexing, >50% queries) at steady state.

## Schema

| Column        | Type               |
|---------------|--------------------|
| `id`          | BIGINT UNSIGNED PK |
| `text_hash`   | CHAR(64) (sha256)  |
| `model`       | VARCHAR(64)        |
| `dim`         | SMALLINT UNSIGNED  |
| `vec`         | LONGBLOB (float32) |
| `token_count` | INT UNSIGNED NULL  |
| `hit_count`   | INT UNSIGNED       |
| `created_at`  | TIMESTAMP          |
| `last_hit_at` | TIMESTAMP NULL     |

Unique key `(text_hash, model)`. `ROW_FORMAT=COMPRESSED KEY_BLOCK_SIZE=8`. Verified `dim` on read; mismatch is treated as cache miss (self-healing).

## Why no `tenant_id`

Deliberate, documented exception to CLAUDE.md §3.1. Embeddings are pure deterministic functions of `(model, text)`; cross-tenant sharing maximizes hit rate without introducing PII risk beyond what was already sent to OpenAI. Only the SHA-256 hash is stored, not the source text. Rationale in `docs/performance/rag-embedding-cache.md`.

## Risk / Rollback

- **Feature flag rollback:** set `RAG_EMBEDDING_CACHE_ENABLED = false` in `config.php` to bypass the cache without touching DB.
- **Full rollback:** run `database/migrations/88_embedding_cache_rollback.sql` (drops the table). The wrapper degrades cleanly to the original direct-API behavior.
- **Concurrency:** parallel processes computing the same hash are safe due to `INSERT IGNORE` on the unique key.
- **DB unavailable:** lookup/store both swallow exceptions and log to `error_log`; the wrapper falls back to API call (non-blocking pattern from CLAUDE.md).

## Test plan

- [ ] Apply migration: `mysql -u root collaboranexio < database/migrations/88_embedding_cache.sql`
- [ ] Trigger an indexing job that calls `cnx_openai_embed_texts()` — first run populates cache, second identical run returns 0 API calls (verify via `logs/embedding_cache.log`)
- [ ] Run `php tools/embedding_cache_stats.php` and confirm entry counts
- [ ] Toggle `RAG_EMBEDDING_CACHE_ENABLED = false` and confirm passthrough behavior (every call hits OpenAI)
- [ ] Verify `--prune-older=N` deletes only stale entries with `--dry-run` first
- [ ] Confirm normalized hashing: `"Foo  bar"` and `"foo bar"` produce the same hash

author: hariseldon343
body:
## Summary

Idempotent schema migration that ensures `deleted_at TIMESTAMP NULL` and a composite `(tenant_id, deleted_at)` index exist on **5 tenant-scoped tables**, unblocking the universal `WHERE tenant_id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL` pattern (CLAUDE.md sec. 3.1, BUG-072, BUG-127) consistently across the schema.

**Tables**: `tasks`, `notifications`, `chat_channels`, `chat_messages`, `chat_message_reads`

## Why a safety-net migration

On the canonical local dev DB (MariaDB 10.4.32, verified 2026-05-02) all 5 tables already have the column and an equivalent `(tenant_id, deleted_at)` index under various legacy names. The migration is idempotent and a **no-op** there. It exists for environments seeded from older snapshots, partial backups, or pre-soft-delete forks (older prod, fresh installs from older SQL dumps in this repo).

## Why no FK changes

Existing `FOREIGN KEY ON DELETE CASCADE` relationships are intentionally **left untouched**. Soft-deleting a tenant means the tenants row stays — `CASCADE` never fires for soft deletes. Touching FKs introduces lock/risk on busy tables for zero benefit. The `deleted_at IS NULL` filter is enforced at the application layer, like the rest of the codebase already does for `users`, `tenants`, `files`, `events`, etc.

## Why no backfill

`NULL == not deleted`. Existing rows remain live. No `UPDATE` is run.

## MariaDB 10.4 specifics

- All ALTERs use `information_schema`-guarded `PREPARE` blocks (no `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` / `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` in 10.4).
- Composite-index guard checks for **any** index whose first two columns are `(tenant_id, deleted_at)`, so it does not duplicate legacy indexes (e.g. `idx_task_tenant_deleted` on `tasks` already shaped that way).
- Online DDL (`ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE`) is documented for manual application on busy production tables (cannot be used inside `PREPARE` on MariaDB 10.4).

## Required follow-up code changes

`docs/migrations/87_soft_delete_extension.md` lists call sites that currently `SELECT/COUNT FROM` these tables **without** `deleted_at IS NULL`. Application-code fixes are intentionally **out of scope** here and will land in a follow-up PR.

Highlights:
- `api/router.php:545,585,627` (dashboard/list/notifications)
- `api/projects_complete.php:144,145,325,738` (project task counts/lists)
- `api/notifications.php:111,166,293`
- `api/channels.php:183,298,482,705,886,1322`
- `includes/polling.php:175,498` (filters `is_deleted=0` already; `deleted_at` filter still missing)
- `api/messages.php`, `api/chat_messages.php`, `api/chat-poll.php` (multiple)

Audit/migration tools (`tools/db_remediation_*`, `tools/apply_db_remediation_*`, `run_simple_task_migration.php`) and hard-cleanup (`api/users/cleanup_deleted.php`) are intentionally excluded — they are global-scope by design.

## Risk / Rollback

- **On current local DB / repo state**: zero — every block is a no-op.
- **On environments missing columns**: small. Column adds are fast and online on InnoDB; only `CREATE INDEX` on multi-million-row tables warrants the manual `ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE` path documented in the migration header.
- **Rollback** (`87_soft_delete_extension_rollback.sql`):
  - Drops only the standardized index names this migration creates; leaves pre-existing differently-named indexes intact.
  - Drops `deleted_at` columns **only if zero non-NULL values** exist; otherwise emits a `WARN` row and skips, to prevent silent data loss.

**This PR does NOT apply the migration to any DB.** Application is the user's call.

## Test plan

- [ ] Re-read the migration once for SQL syntax sanity.
- [ ] Apply locally on a clean checkout: `mysql -u root collaboranexio < database/migrations/87_soft_delete_extension.sql` and confirm zero errors and zero schema drift on the canonical dev DB (expected: every block prints an "already exists / already present" `SELECT`).
- [ ] Apply rollback: `mysql -u root collaboranexio < database/migrations/87_soft_delete_extension_rollback.sql` and confirm rollback refuses any drops where soft-deleted rows are present (none expected on dev DB).
- [ ] Re-apply forward migration; confirm idempotent (still no errors).
- [ ] Optional: spin up a clean DB without these columns/indexes to verify the create-path works end to end.

body:
## Summary

- Replaces all 4 `Get-Content -Raw` calls in `Install-Playbook.ps1` with `[System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($path, [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8)` — fixes ANSI codepage corruption of non-ASCII content (en-dashes, em-dashes, arrows) in `jit-claude.md` and user `CLAUDE.md` files on PowerShell 5.1
- Extends `build-release.ps1` null-byte preflight to cover `.md` and `.json` files in addition to `.ps1`/`.sh`

Fixes #9

## Root cause

PowerShell 5.1's `Get-Content -Raw` without `-Encoding` reads BOM-less UTF-8 files via the system ANSI codepage (CP1252). The 3-byte UTF-8 sequence `\xe2\x80\x93` (en-dash `–`) is decoded as three CP1252 characters (`â€"`), which `WriteAllText(..., UTF8Encoding::new($false))` then re-encodes as 8 bytes. Every reinstall compounds the inflation, producing "hundreds of KB of corrupted character encoding."

`jit-claude.md` contains 42 non-ASCII bytes (14 multi-byte sequences). Any existing user `CLAUDE.md` with non-ASCII content is also at risk.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verified `Get-Content -Raw` on a UTF-8 file produces `â€"5` (corrupted); `ReadAllText(UTF8)` produces `–5` (correct) — tested in PowerShell 5.1
- [ ] Confirmed all 4 text-content `Get-Content` calls are fixed; 3 remaining calls (lines 244, 532, 699) read ASCII-only version strings and are safe
- [ ] End-to-end inject simulation: non-ASCII user content preserved, file size stable across 3 consecutive runs (idempotent)
- [ ] `build-release.ps1`: 108 `.md`/`.json` files in `dist/stage` pass null-byte check

author: alexanderbates
body:
Integrate adjust_influence into calculate_influence

calculate_influence now returns both the raw influence column and the
three log-compressed adjusted_influence columns by default.  Users can
compare adjusted vs unadjusted scores from a single call rather than
having to import adjust_influence and post-process the output
themselves; opt out with adjust=False.

The log compression is parameterised via two new kwargs on
calculate_influence: adjust_const (the exp(-c) junk-node floor /+c
shift, default 24) and adjust_signif (rounding, default 6).

adjust_influence is exposed as a @staticmethod on InfluenceCalculator
(`InfluenceCalculator.adjust_influence(df, const=..., signif=...)`),
so advanced workflows can still post-process aggregated DataFrames
(e.g. summing per-(target_class, seed_class) across multiple seeds
before log compression in a worked example).  The staticmethod is
reachable both from the class (no instance needed) and from any
instance, and is the only public way to call adjust_influence -- the
package no longer exposes it as a module-level name.

Its output is three columns:

- adjusted_influence = sign(x) * (log(max(|x|, exp(-const))) + const)
- adjusted_influence_norm_by_targets (divides by n_targets per group)
- adjusted_influence_norm_by_sources_and_targets (divides by
  n_sources * n_targets per group)

The function dispatches on the presence of 'target' and 'seed' columns:
when present it groups and sums per (target, seed); when absent it
treats each row as its own group, which is the case for the DataFrame
calculate_influence builds.  Sign is preserved, so signed-mode input
yields signed-mode output.

Update 2026-06-04: addressed review feedback by moving
adjust_influence from a module-level function into the
InfluenceCalculator class as a @staticmethod; PRs 3/6, 5/6, and 6/6
in this series have been rebased accordingly.

Closes #1149

## Summary

- Re-aligned all 10 entries in `tileops/manifest/normalization.yaml` to canonical `add-manifest` output (mirrors PRs #1150 / #1151 / #1152 / #1156 / #1157 for elementwise + reduction families).
- 6 PyTorch-reference ops regenerated from `torch.nn.functional` docs; 4 custom ops (`ref_api: none`) hand-verified against on-disk kernel/op code with conventional renames only.
- Standardized output tensor name (`y` -> `output`) across all entries.

## Notable interface changes

- **`RMSNormFwdOp`**: drop unsupported `dim`; add `normalized_shape: list[int] | tuple[int, ...]`; `eps` default `null` (`Optional[float]`); **status flipped `implemented` -> `spec-only`** (impl `__init__(M, N)` does not accept `normalized_shape`; follow-up code PR required).
- **`LayerNormFwdOp`**: add `normalized_shape` per `torch.nn.functional.layer_norm`; **status flipped `implemented` -> `spec-only`** for the same reason.
- **`BatchNormFwdOp`**: reorder inputs to `(input, running_mean, running_var, weight, bias)` and params to `(training, momentum, eps)` per `torch.nn.functional.batch_norm`; flip `training` default `true` -> `false` (PyTorch default); drop non-PyTorch outputs `mean`/`rstd` from the signature.
- **`GroupNormFwdOp`**: rename `groups` -> `num_groups` in params, `shape_rules`, and workload keys per `torch.nn.functional.group_norm`.

body:
Overhaul tests; bundle C. elegans connectome for fixtures

Replaces the legacy single-test scaffold (tests/test_InfluenceCalculator.py
plus toy_network_example.sqlite and an example notebook) with a focused
pytest suite that exercises the constructor surface introduced by the
recent parameter rework and the integration of adjust_influence into
calculate_influence:

- Constructor validation: signed=True without inhibitory_nts raises;
  lambda_max outside (0, 1) raises (parametrised over five values);
  unknown syn_weight_measure raises.
- Construction smoke: unsigned and signed builds, the 'norm'
  syn_weight_measure path, and excluded_nts dropping pre-neurons.
  Wrapped in pytest.importorskip so they skip cleanly on machines
  without PETSc/SLEPc rather than failing the suite.
- InfluenceCalculator.adjust_influence staticmethod: column shape,
  log-+-const anchor at the strongest influence, exp(-const) floor
  mapping zero raw influence to zero adjusted, sign preservation in
  signed mode, and the two validation errors (both score columns
  present, no score column).
- calculate_influence integration: default returns adjusted columns
  alongside raw, adjust=False returns raw only, signed mode produces
  some net-negative downstream targets.
- Bundled-data sanity check on column presence and row counts.

Bundles the C. elegans hermaphrodite chemical connectome (300 cells,
3,539 edges, 20,672 synapses) under InfluenceCalculator/data/ as two
CSVs plus an importable wrapper (celegans_edgelist(),
celegans_meta()).  Provenance and citation BibTeX live in the module
docstring so help(InfluenceCalculator.data) surfaces them.  The CSVs
are an OpenWorm distribution extract (accessed February 2026)
aggregating White et al. 1986 and Cook et al. 2019 with WormAtlas /
CenGen annotations.

The conftest fixture builds a temporary SQLite database from the
bundled CSVs to drive InfluenceCalculator's still-SQLite-only
constructor.  Once the DataFrame / from_csv constructors land in a
later PR the fixture can collapse to a path handoff.

Update 2026-06-04: tests now drive the @staticmethod form
(`InfluenceCalculator.adjust_influence(...)`) after the corresponding
refactor on PR 2/6.

author: alexanderbates
body:
Refactor __init__ to take DataFrames; add from_XXX classmethods

The internal data structure built by InfluenceCalculator is a sparse
PETSc matrix populated from an edge list, so the input format closest
to that representation is a pandas DataFrame edge list (plus optional
metadata DataFrame).  __init__ now takes those directly:

    InfluenceCalculator(edgelist_df, meta_df=None, signed=False, ...)

Five classmethod loaders adapt other input formats to the DataFrame
__init__.  Each one reads the format, then forwards every other kwarg
through **kwargs so the loaders do not have to repeat the constructor
signature:

- from_sql(filename, **kwargs)             -- SQLite (meta + edgelist_simple)
- from_csv(edgelist_path, meta_path, ...)
- from_parquet(edgelist_path, meta_path, ...)  (requires pyarrow / fastparquet)
- from_feather(edgelist_path, meta_path, ...)  (requires pyarrow)
- from_numpy(adjacency_matrix, neuron_ids=None, meta_df=None, **kwargs)

This is a breaking change for callers using the previous SQLite-only
__init__.  Update those call sites to InfluenceCalculator.from_sql.

from_numpy converts non-zero entries of the adjacency matrix into a
synthesised edge list with a 'count' column and forwards through
__init__.  Because count_thresh is applied to that synthesised column,
callers passing pre-normalised float weights should set count_thresh=0.

Three module-level validation helpers -- _validate_meta,
_validate_and_prepare_edgelist, and _check_parquet_available /
_check_feather_available -- enforce the column requirements with
descriptive ValueErrors that name the missing column and list the
columns the caller actually passed.  When 'norm' is absent it is
computed from 'count' as count / sum(count) per post; when 'weight' is
present (instead of 'count') it is treated as a pre-normalised input
and count_thresh is bypassed.  The redundant inline top_nt checks
inside _create_sparse_W are removed since validation runs upfront.

Tests are updated to drive the DataFrame __init__ directly and add
format-equivalence checks (from_sql vs DataFrame, from_csv vs
DataFrame, from_numpy smoke).  conftest.py exposes the bundled CSVs
four ways: as DataFrames, as filesystem paths via
importlib.resources.as_file(), and as a session-scoped temporary
SQLite database for from_sql.

body:
## Summary

- The Codex OAuth state cookie (encrypted PKCE verifier + state) flagged `Secure` only when `NODE_ENV === "production"`. Vercel preview/staging deploys run over HTTPS but do not set `NODE_ENV=production`, so the cookie shipped without `Secure` in those environments — an on-path attacker who downgraded a single request could capture the OAuth state and complete the flow as the victim.
- Default to `secure: true` and gate opt-out behind a positive `WALLIE_ALLOW_INSECURE_COOKIES=1` env flag for local HTTP dev only.
- Audit of other `cookies.set` callsites (`src/`): `@supabase/ssr`'s `setAll` adapter forwards library-owned options, and the callback's `clearCookie` only writes `value=""` with `maxAge: 0`. The Codex OAuth route was the only sensitive write that needed the fix.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm format:check`
- [x] `pnpm lint`
- [x] `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm test` — 214/214 pass, including 2 new tests in `src/app/auth/codex/route.test.ts` asserting (a) `Secure` ships when `NODE_ENV` is non-`production`, and (b) `WALLIE_ALLOW_INSECURE_COOKIES=1` is the only way to opt out

Closes WAL-7.

author: alexanderbates
body:
Add C. elegans worked example; rewrite README around the new knobs

examples/celegans_worked_example.py is a self-contained end-to-end run
on the bundled C. elegans connectome.  Per-seed influence from every
sensory neuron (83 cells -> 46 cell classes after collapsing bilateral
pairs) onto every non-sensory target (187 -> 136 classes), summed per
(target_class, seed_class), log-adjusted via
InfluenceCalculator.adjust_influence with an auto-calibrated
const = -log(min_nonzero |sum|), and rendered as two heatmaps grouped
by anatomical body_part with average-linkage clustering within each
group.  The script encodes its design choices as constants at the top:
LAMBDA_MAX=0.5 (the small graph needs the leading mode damped or it
dominates every column), COUNT_THRESH=0,
EXCLUDE_BODY_PARTS={'pharynx'}, plus C. elegans neurotransmitter
conventions (only ACh and GABA have unambiguous signs; glutamate /
dopamine / serotonin / octopamine are excluded).

The cell-class regex collapses trailing L/R suffixes only -- omitting
the seemingly more "complete" DL|DR|VL|VR alternatives because Python's
leftmost-first alternation would otherwise match DL at position 2 of
AVDL (with lookbehind V) and produce AV instead of AVD.

Two output heatmaps land in docs/images/ alongside four explanatory
images for the README: a source-to-targets schematic and an
adjusted_influence-vs-traversal-depth scatter pulled from the
natverse/influencer R sibling package, and a bespoke annotated linear
dynamical model + a 12s propagation-to-steady-state animation on a
28-node toy graph.

README is restructured around the parameters a user actually tunes:

- Description: derives the rescaling W_tilde = (lambda / lambda_max(W))
  W with the reverb-knob metaphor, names lambda_max as the constructor
  argument, and gives species-specific guidance (~0.99 for whole-CNS
  Drosophila BANC, ~0.5 for C. elegans).  syn_weight_measure documented
  as a deliberate 'count' default with the rationale that signed mode
  pairs cleanly with raw counts but distorts 'norm' (columns no longer
  sum to 1).
- Usage: lists all six entry points (DataFrame __init__ plus from_sql,
  from_csv, from_parquet, from_feather, from_numpy), names the required
  edge list and meta columns, and explicitly states that missing
  columns raise an actionable ValueError.
- adjust_influence section: explains the log-+-const transform and the
  exp(-const) junk-node floor, gives the auto-calibration recipe for
  non-BANC datasets, summarises the three output columns, documents
  the implicit (target, seed) grouping, and reminds the reader that
  adjust_influence is a @staticmethod on InfluenceCalculator
  (callable as `InfluenceCalculator.adjust_influence(df, const=...)`)
  rather than a free module-level function.

Update 2026-06-04: example call site and the README description both
use `InfluenceCalculator.adjust_influence(...)` after the
staticmethod refactor on PR 2/6.  Also adds the Nature DOI for the
BANC paper now that it is in press (10.1038/s41586-026-10735-w).

author: apolyakov
body:
This PR extends the `CollectConstVarsPass` compiler optimization to support the `+` operator (array union/addition) for constant expressions. This moves evaluation of constant `arr + arr` expressions from request execution time to kPHP initialization stage.

Implementation Details:
The optimization is currently limited to `arr + arr` case only. While the optimization would be safe for some other cases as well (the runtime handles type coercion), `K2` runtime's implementation of string addition requires `RuntimeContext` to be initialized (which is not initialized at the time of constant initialization stage). To ensure compatibility with both legacy and `K2` runtimes, we restrict this optimization to array addition only.

Example:
Before this change, an expression like `['a' => 1] + ['b' => 2]` would be evaluated on every request. After this change, it's evaluated once during initialization and stored as a constant variable.

body:
Adds GitHub Actions pipelines for the three deployable components, modeled after [`qkfang/quant-agent/.github/workflows`](https://github.com/qkfang/quant-agent/tree/main/.github/workflows).

### Workflows
- **`10_deploy_iac.yml`** — Deploys `bicep/main.bicep` to resource group `rg-zava-claims` (deployment name `zava-claims-dev`). Triggered by `bicep/**` changes or manual dispatch.
- **`20_deploy_backend_api.yml`** — Python 3.11 build of `src/api/` (matches backend App Service `linuxFxVersion: PYTHON|3.11`), deployed via `azure/webapps-deploy@v3`. Triggered by `src/api/**` changes or manual dispatch.
- **`21_deploy_frontend.yml`** — Node 20 + Vite build of `src/ui/` (matches frontend `NODE|20-lts`), publishes `dist/`. Triggered by `src/ui/**` changes or manual dispatch.

### Conventions
- All workflows use the `dev` environment, authenticate via `azure/login@v1` with the `AZURE_CREDENTIALS` secret, and declare `permissions: contents: read`.
- Web App names are pulled from repo variables `FRONTEND_APP_NAME` / `BACKEND_APP_NAME` since the Bicep appends a `uniqueString`-derived suffix; these need to be set after the first IaC deployment.

### Notes for reviewers
- `src/api/` does not yet exist in the repo; the backend workflow is scaffolded to activate once sources land. The `requirements.txt` install step is guarded with an `if [ -f ... ]` so manual dispatch doesn't hard-fail before then — happy to switch to a strict check if preferred.
- Resource group `rg-zava-claims` is assumed pre-created (matching the reference repo's pattern); the commented `az group create` line is left in for parity.

author: copilot
body:
Adds the 16-cell thesis sweep, replaces CSV-based log loading with a persistent parquet cache, and turns on lossless end-of-training compression for both logs and checkpoints. Notebooks are migrated to the new loader and a one-shot migration script handles the existing 20 GB of logs + 2.5 GB of checkpoints. Bumps `version` to **8.6.4** with a corresponding `docs/changelog.md` entry.

### `configs/sweeps/thesis_experiments.yaml`
5 structural variants × 3 seeds (`1729, 8191, 6561` — default-sweep seeds minus `5041`) + 1 high-inflation cell on seed `1729` = 16 jobs.

- `lrf_low_22pct` — pre-FF55 LRF (`ets.lrf_phase{1,2}=0.022`)
- `lrf_high_6pct` — aggressive future LRF (`0.060` / `0.063`)
- `no_market_stability` — `ets.msr.enabled=false` **and** `ets.unsold_to_msr=false`
- `all_financial_objectives` — every learning agent `[1.0, 0.0]`
- `balanced_identical` — identical mix/budget/capex/debt for all 8 agents (means of default arrays); reward weights split 4 financial / 4 ESG so preference is the only experimental axis
- `high_inflation` — `penalty.inflation_rate=0.060`, `inflation_random_std=0.045`, seeds `[1729]`

The `parallel_workers` knob carries an inline sizing guide grounded in physical-core count + per-job RAM (~4–6 GB resident): D16ds_v5 → 4 (default; 8 physical cores × 2 BLAS threads), D32 → 8, **D64 → 16** (all 16 jobs in parallel, ≈ 1× single-job wall time).

### `src/utils/run_data.py` — persistent parquet cache
Drop-in replacement for `pd.read_csv` on training/year logs. Survives across kernels and notebooks.

- Streaming CSV→parquet on first load: float64→float32, int64→int32 (lossless, range-checked), zstd compression. ~5–10× smaller, ~5–20× faster reload.
- Cache key = `(size, mtime_ns)` embedded in parquet metadata; auto-invalidates on stale source. Atomic `tmp`→`rename` build so an interrupted run can't leave a corrupt cache.
- `columns=` pushed down to the parquet reader — the original `MemoryError` goes away because notebooks only ever materialise the few fields they actually plot.
- `load_run_csv` accepts either a `.csv` or a `.parquet` path interchangeably; `cache_path_for` is idempotent on parquet input. CSV may be deleted after caching; the loader falls back to parquet for the disk-space workflow.
- `glob_run_logs(pattern)` — CSV-style globs that also find parquet siblings (and prefer CSV when both exist), so notebook discovery keeps working after CSVs are deleted.
- `load_sweep(spec_path)` returns `{(variant, seed): {ep_df, yr_df, config, ...}}` matching the existing notebook dict shape.

```python
from src.utils.run_data import load_run, load_run_csv, load_sweep, glob_run_logs

ep_df, yr_df = load_run(training_log_path, year_log_path)

# Column projection — reads ~1% of the year log
yr_df = load_run_csv(year_log_path, columns=["episode", "year", "clearing_price", "tnac"])

# Glob that survives CSV deletion
ppo_paths = glob_run_logs("results/sweep/*/training_log_s*.csv")

# Whole sweep at once
runs = load_sweep("configs/sweeps/thesis_experiments.yaml")
```

### Lossless end-of-training compression
At clean end of `train_one_seed`, `scripts/train.py` now runs two lossless compression steps so cloud workers ship the small form back to your laptop:

1. `compress_logs(...)` converts `(training_log, year_log)` to zstd parquet, verifies the parquet's row count against the source CSV, and deletes the CSV.
2. `compress_checkpoints(...)` bundles `checkpoints_<tag>_s<seed>/` into a single `checkpoints_<tag>_s<seed>.tar.xz` (stdlib LZMA, no new runtime dependency) and deletes the source dir.

Both steps round-trip losslessly modulo the documented float64→float32 / int64→int32 downcast in the parquet writer. Both stream end-to-end — `compress_logs` reads the source CSV in 250k-row chunks (configurable via `chunksize=`), so peak heap stays well under 1 GB even on a 5 GB year-log; `compress_checkpoints` uses `tarfile`'s incremental writer. Safe on Azure ML's standard D16ds_v5 (64 GB RAM).

Behaviour is controlled by a new `logging.compress_on_finish` block in YAML (all defaults `true`):

```yaml
logging:
  compress_on_finish:
    logs: true
    checkpoints: true
    delete_csv: true
    delete_checkpoint_dir: true
```

### Decompression workflow
Symmetric helper plus `evaluate.py` integration so users never have to drop to a shell:

- `decompress_checkpoints(archive)` extracts a `checkpoints_*.tar.xz` back to the original directory layout. Non-destructive by default; pass `delete_archive=True` to reclaim the space. Uses `tarfile.data_filter` on Py 3.12+ to mitigate CVE-2007-4559-family path traversal.
- `scripts/evaluate.py --checkpoint path/to/checkpoints_<tag>_s<seed>.tar.xz` now works directly — the archive is extracted on demand before agent weights are loaded.
- Equivalent shell one-liner: `tar -xJf checkpoints_<tag>_s<seed>.tar.xz`.

### `scripts/compress_results.py` — migrate existing data
Run once to migrate the 20 GB of existing CSV logs and 2.5 GB of checkpoint dirs to their compressed form. Walks any directory and applies the same compression as the training-end hook; supports `--dry-run`, `--keep-source`, `--logs-only`, `--checkpoints-only`. Idempotent — re-running skips runs whose archives already exist.

```bash
python scripts/compress_results.py results --dry-run
python scripts/compress_results.py results
```

### Notebook migration
All 6 notebooks that read training/year/Q-learning logs are migrated:

- `Bots-Only Baseline`, `Data Science Analysis`, `Default RQ Analysis`, `Full Run & Analysis`, `Q-Learning Baseline`, `Sweep Analysis`
- 15 `pd.read_csv(...)` calls rewritten to `load_run_csv(...)`
- 6 `glob.glob('…*.csv')` discovery patterns rewritten to `glob_run_logs(...)` (incl. `recursive=True` form)
- Import line added next to the existing pandas import in each notebook
- `Episode Viewer` is unchanged — verified it does not read any log CSV (it runs a live in-memory env rollout via `ETSEnvironment.step_*` and reads the env's in-memory `year_logs` dict)

### Plumbing
- Version 8.6.3 → **8.6.4** in `pyproject.toml`, `configs/default.yaml`, with a `[8.6.4]` entry in `docs/changelog.md`.
- `pyarrow>=15.0.0` added to `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`, `notebooks/requirements-notebooks.txt`. Checkpoint compression uses stdlib `tarfile` (LZMA) — no new runtime dependency.
- `tests/test_run_data.py` — 36 tests (round-trip, dtype downcast, cache reuse, mtime-invalidation, force-rebuild, column projection incl. unknown-column tolerance, missing-files, CSV-delete fallback, empty-CSV, parquet-direct load, idempotent `cache_path_for`, four `glob_run_logs` cases, three `compress_logs` cases including a 200k-row chunked-streaming round-trip, four `compress_checkpoints` cases, three `decompress_checkpoints` cases).
- `tests/test_training_smoke.py` — adds `test_compress_on_finish_hook` running a real 5-episode training and asserting the CSVs are gone and the parquet + `tar.xz` artefacts are on disk. Existing smoke test opts out of compression so it can keep asserting on the live CSV.
- `docs/run_data_cache.md` — usage, end-of-run config block, memory-profile notes, decompression walkthrough, migration walkthrough, disk-space sketch.

### Disk footprint impact
| Artefact | Source | Compressed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `year_log_*.csv` | ~5 GB | ~0.5–1.0 GB parquet |
| `training_log_*.csv` | ~30 MB | ~5–10 MB parquet |
| `checkpoints_*/` (170 files) | ~2.5 GB | ~0.5–1.5 GB tar.xz |

author: fiveapplesonthetable
body:
Two commits, layered:

## 1. `tp: scope critical-path stack work per-query, drop module-load materialisations`

`sched.thread_executing_span_with_slice` previously eagerly built four whole-trace tables at module load (`_critical_path_all`, `_span_thread_state_slice`, `_critical_path_thread_state_slice_raw`, `_critical_path_thread_state_slice`) plus the `_self_and_critical_path_sp` SPAN_JOIN. On a 17 MB Android trace this was ~95 s of `INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE` cost — wasted work, since every consumer already passes a `(root_utid, ts, dur)` window.

Drops the four materialised tables and the SPAN_JOIN. New helper `_critical_path_relevant_spans(root_utid, ts, dur)` computes `_self_and_critical_path_sp WHERE root_utid = … AND dur > 0` lazily, restricted to the input window:

- Walk runs only over wakeup nodes for `root_utid` overlapping `[ts, ts+dur]` via `_critical_path_by_roots!(_intervals_to_roots!(...))`.
- The two SPAN_LEFT_JOIN virtual tables are queried with `WHERE utid = …` / `WHERE utid IN (…)` so partition push-down kicks in. (`JOIN … USING (utid)` did *not* push down — ~4× slower in microbenchmarks.)
- The two inner intersections are open-coded `JOIN … ON overlap`. `_interval_intersect!` was tried — its join-back to recover columns evaluates each input twice, and on whole-trace inputs that path measured ~40× slower than open-coded JOIN even with MATERIALIZED CTEs.

Bit-identical output: all 23 `TablesSched` diff tests pass with no expectation changes.

| stage                    | before | after |
|--------------------------|-------:|------:|
| module load              | ~95 s  | ~12 s |
| narrow stack call        | 0.3 s  | 1.3 s |
| whole-trace stack call   | 0.3 s  | 2.4 s |

Single-click UI workflow: 95.3 s → 1.6 s end-to-end (~60×).

## 2. `tp+ui: replace synthetic CP stack with typed-column context + pprof`

The previous CP "stack" pipeline emitted synthetic slice-track strings (`'process_name: …'`, `'thread_name: …'`) that callers had to parse, fragmented identical chains by accidental columns (CPU, io_wait), and wedged a flame graph through a flat slice track. This commit replaces it with three purpose-built helpers and migrates the UI plugin onto them.

In `sched.thread_executing_span_with_slice`:

- **`_critical_path_context(root_utid, ts, dur)`** — wide-row table, one row per CP interval. Both sides expanded as typed columns: `self_*` (state, blocked_function, slice id/name/depth) and `blocker_*` (utid, thread+process name, state, function, slice id/name/depth, cpu).
- **`_critical_path_self_slice_stack` / `_critical_path_blocker_slice_stack`** — `(ts, dur, slice_id, slice_name, stack_depth)` rows for the ancestor stack on either side at every interval. `stack_depth` is in the original (un-flattened) slice tree, so consumers render root → leaf without re-deriving.
- **`_critical_path_pprof(graph_title, root_utid, ts, dur, enable_blocker_process, enable_blocker_thread, enable_blocker_slice_stack, enable_self_function)`** — `experimental_profile` aggregator. Frames are typed strings so identical paths land on the same leaf. Self-time is computed via `dur - lead(dur)` per (ts), so non-leaf frames contribute 0 — no double counting.

In `dev.perfetto.CriticalPath`, the `Critical path` command now adds two debug-slice tracks: `<thread> ◀ blocker` (chain hop + blocker leaf slice + state, with the blocker's `utid` so the track inherits its colour) and `<thread> ◀ wait reason` (root's own state + blocked_function + active slice). The synthetic-stack track and old `Critical path pprof` graph helper are gone.

Removes the now-unreachable `_thread_executing_span_critical_path_stack`, `_critical_path_stack`, and `_thread_executing_span_critical_path_graph` plus their tests (-681 lines of stdlib SQL, -2 obsolete tests). Lite path (`_thread_executing_span_critical_path`) is unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] All `TablesSched` diff tests green (23 tests; 4 new for context/stacks/pprof, 2 old removed)
- [x] End-to-end UI verification with PerfettoCpDemo trace; both new tracks render and tell the chain story
- [x] `_critical_path_pprof` returns valid `experimental_profile` bytes

author: jacksteroo
body:
## Summary

Implements the persistence half of [Epic 01: Trace Substrate](https://github.com/jacksteroo/Pepper/issues/17). Materializes the schema landed by [#84](https://github.com/jacksteroo/Pepper/pull/84) into a Postgres table, an append-only repository, and the role/grant scaffolding ADR-0005 mandates.

- `agent/traces/models.py` — SQLAlchemy `TraceRow` mirroring the `Trace` dataclass field-for-field. Heavy columns (`embedding`, `assembled_context`, `tools_called`) use `deferred()` per `docs/trace-schema.md` §"Read patterns" so list-view callers don't pay the jsonb/vector load cost.
- `agent/traces/migration.py` — idempotent post-`create_all` SQL: partial HNSW index `WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL`, GIN `jsonb_path_ops` on `tools_called`, and the three roles (`pepper_traces_writer` / `pepper_traces_compactor` / `pepper_traces_reader`) with the ADR-0005 grants. Compactor receives per-column `UPDATE` on `(embedding, embedding_model_version, tier, user_reaction)`; writer is `INSERT`-only; reader is `SELECT`-only. `DELETE` is never granted. The owner-bypass limitation (the application connects as the table owner today) is documented in the module's top docstring as an advisory caveat — the repository is the operative enforcement until per-role connection routing lands as a follow-up.
- `agent/traces/repository.py` — `TraceRepository` exposes exactly seven public methods: `append`, `get_by_id`, `query`, `find_similar`, plus the three carve-outs `set_embedding`, `advance_tier`, `set_user_reaction`. No `update*`, no `delete*` (forbidden-prefix scan asserts this in tests). `query()` uses composite cursor `(created_at, trace_id)` for pagination stability across `created_at` ties, and `with_payload` is opt-in so list-view callers can avoid loading the heavy columns. `advance_tier` is forward-only with same-tier no-op for nightly job idempotency. `set_user_reaction` validates the payload shape against the keys documented in `docs/trace-schema.md`.
- `agent/db.py` — wires `apply_traces_migration` into `init_db` after `create_all`, with a side-effect import to ensure the model is registered with `Base.metadata`.
- `agent/traces/schema.py` — `__post_init__` now validates `trace_id` is UUID-shaped at the contract boundary.
- `docs/adr/0005-trace-schema.md` — §"Postgres roles & grants" lists `user_reaction` in the compactor carve-out so the grants section matches §Mutability.

Closes #20.

## Test plan

- [x] `.venv/bin/python -m pytest agent/tests/test_traces_*.py -v` — 53/53 pass.
- [x] `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check agent/traces/ agent/tests/test_traces_*.py agent/db.py` clean.
- [x] Full repo suite: 652 passing; 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (`test_router_backfill.py::test_backfill_skips_duplicate_rows`) reproducible on `main` without this PR.

## Acceptance criteria for #20

- [x] Migration runs clean on a fresh `pepper_dev` DB (idempotent SQL; covered by content tests).
- [x] Round-trip `append() → get_by_id()` exact equality (refresh after flush so server-side defaults are reflected).
- [x] `traces_repository.update(...)` does not exist (`hasattr` asserted).
- [x] Writer role lacks `UPDATE` / `DELETE` on the table (asserted via SQL content introspection).
- [x] `agent/traces/repository.py` exposes only `append`, `get_by_id`, `query`, plus the three documented carve-outs.

## What's deferred

- Per-role connection pools — currently `CURRENT_USER` inherits writer + compactor and the role enforcement is advisory.
- Real-DB integration test for HNSW nearest-neighbor against synthetic data — content tests cover the migration SQL; behavioral tests against a live Postgres are out of scope for this PR.

author: yahonda
body:
## Summary

Add a regression spec confirming that Rails' `RestartParentTransaction` (rails/rails#44526) works correctly on Oracle. **No production code changes.**

The spec asserts:

- An immediately-nested `transaction(requires_new: true)` inside an outer `transaction do ... end`, with `raise ActiveRecord::Rollback` in the inner block and a subsequent DML in the outer block, yields:
  - The inner row did **not** persist (rollback succeeded).
  - The outer row **did** persist after the inner rollback (the parent transaction stayed alive across the restart).
  - **No `SAVEPOINT` SQL** was logged — i.e. Rails selected `RestartParentTransaction` over `SavepointTransaction`.

## Why no production code change (= why not override `supports_restart_db_transaction?`)

Rails picks `RestartParentTransaction` whenever the parent is `restartable?` (joinable && !dirty), **independent of `supports_restart_db_transaction?`**. The capability flag only switches the *implementation* of the restart:

- `true` → `connection.restart_db_transaction` (one optimized call)
- `false` → `connection.rollback_db_transaction` + `parent.materialize!` (the default fallback)

For Oracle, the fallback path already does the right thing:

- It issues a single `ROLLBACK`.
- `materialize!` re-applies the parent's isolation level by calling `begin_isolated_db_transaction(isolation_level)` again, re-issuing `SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL ...`.

Overriding `supports_restart_db_transaction?` to `true` was explored in #2525 — that approach saves only two local `setAutoCommit()` calls per restart (no DB round-trip on JDBC or OCI8), but in exchange the adapter must thread an `@transaction_isolation` instance variable through `begin_db_transaction`, `begin_isolated_db_transaction`, `commit_db_transaction`, `exec_rollback_db_transaction`, and `exec_restart_db_transaction` so the restart can re-issue `SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL` (Oracle's bare `ROLLBACK` drops it; Postgres uses `ROLLBACK AND CHAIN` to preserve it).

**The added complexity is not justified by the marginal saving.** This PR takes the simpler route: rely on Rails' fallback, which is correct as-is for Oracle, and add a regression spec so the behavior stays guaranteed.

## Test plan

- [x] New spec passes locally against Oracle Database 23ai Free.
- [x] Full rspec suite green locally (no regressions).
- [x] `bundle exec rubocop` clean.
- [ ] CI green.

Closes #2270.

(Supersedes #2525.)

author: jcfs
body:
The Jira and Linear integrations had zero end-to-end coverage and no way to drive them deterministically without hitting real Atlassian / Linear APIs. This adds in-memory mock backends gated behind `KANDEV_MOCK_{JIRA,LINEAR}=true`, mock-control HTTP routes, e2e helpers, page objects, and four Playwright spec files covering settings flows and import popovers — so future changes to either integration's UI fail loudly instead of silently regressing.

## Important Changes

- Backend `MockClient` + `MockController` for jira and linear, mirroring the existing GitHub mock pattern. `Provide` branches on the env var; `RegisterMockRoutes` mounts `/api/v1/{jira,linear}/mock/*` only in mock mode.
- `ValidatedPopover.TriggerButton` now spreads `...rest` onto the inner Button — it was silently dropping the `onClick` handler radix's Slot injects via `PopoverTrigger asChild`, so the popover never opened under any synthetic-click path. Real users were unaffected because the same button has a tooltip-trigger sibling that masked the issue in casual testing.
- `e2e/fixtures/test-base.ts` integration cleanup is now an `auto: true` fixture instead of a top-level `test.beforeEach`, because Playwright only fires file-scoped beforeEach hooks for tests defined in the same file as the hook — the imported `test` object's hooks were skipped for cross-spec tests.

## Validation

- `make -C apps/backend fmt lint test`
- `cd apps && pnpm --filter @kandev/web lint`
- `cd apps && pnpm --filter @kandev/web test` (vitest, 890 unit tests)
- `cd apps/web && npx playwright test --config e2e/playwright.config.ts e2e/tests/integrations/` (16/16 pass)
- Smoke-checked existing `e2e/tests/task/create-task.spec.ts` still passes after the test-base fixture rework.

## Possible Improvements

Low risk. The integration cleanup auto-fixture runs DELETE + mock-reset for every test in the suite — adds ~5–10ms per test, immaterial against the existing 60s test timeout. If a worker without the mock binary somehow runs (none today), the `.catch(() => undefined)` swallows the failure rather than leaking.

## Checklist

- [ ] I have performed a self-review of my code.
- [ ] I have manually tested my changes and they work as expected.
- [ ] My changes have tests that cover the new functionality and edge cases.
- [ ] If my change touches UI files (`apps/web/`), I have added or updated Playwright e2e tests in `apps/web/e2e/` and verified them with `make test-e2e`.
