body:
## Summary

Five issues from end-to-end smoke testing the v3.4 researcher refactor with \`--preset solo\` real Claude subprocess. Each fix landed against a specific stack-trace or transcript observability finding — all documented in \`CHANGELOG.md\`.

## The five RCAs

1. **EISDIR on researcher spawn** — \`ACTOR_TO_SANDWICH\` was missing the \`researcher\` entry → \`baseSandwichPath = ''\` → \`resolve(repoRoot, '') = repoRoot\` (directory) → \`readFile\` EISDIR. Fix: added \`researcher: 'agents/researcher.md'\`.

2. **per_spawn_timeout 5min too tight** — Claude wake alone takes ~3:30 for the 15KB sandwich. Bumped default to 10min. Added \`--per-spawn-timeout <ms>\` CLI flag for override.

3. **\`--root\` was required from non-repo cwd** — Bagelcode reviewer expectation: clone → npm install → \`crumb run\` from any cwd. Added \`inferRepoRoot()\` that resolves from \`import.meta.url\` and walks up to \`AGENTS.md\` + \`agents/\`.

4. **Chain drain race** — coordinator watchdog's \`processing.finally(() => finish())\` attached to a snapshot of the chain. Long planner spawn (7min) caused \`finish()\` to fire right after planner returned, before queued \`handoff.requested(researcher) → dispatch(spawn researcher)\` ran. Observed: session 01KQMFWA ended at agent.stop+7ms with 0 researcher events. Fix: \`pendingItems\` counter; watchdog requires \`pendingItems === 0\` AND idle to call \`finish\`.

5. **Fatal handler hid stack traces** — printed only \`err.message\`. Added \`err.stack\` so future RCA gets full traces without re-running.

## Bonus: README quickstart simplified

§B (mock) + §C (real) now use \`crumb run\` directly (after one-time \`npm install && npm run build && npm link\`), no more \`npx tsx src/index.ts ...\`. §C example walks the full submission flow (\`init --pin → run --preset solo → release --as v1 → copy-artifacts v1 --to ./demo\`).

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run typecheck\` clean
- [x] \`npm run lint\` clean (per main; package-lock + mcp-server changes from parallel sessions intentionally NOT included)
- [x] Mock e2e from /tmp cwd: \`auto-detect\` resolves \`repo=/Users/mango/workspace/crumb\`, score_history=1 PASS
- [ ] Real subprocess full cycle (planner → researcher → planner phase B → builder → qa → verifier) post-merge

Two rounds of QA staging follow-ups bundled into a single PR. 9 issues from the round-1 (10-subagent) sweep + the round-2 auth/wizard sweep, scoped to citizen-pwa.

**Round 1 (commit 013e8b5)** — 4 issues, 3 source files:
- Offline shell: precache `/`, `/index.html`, manifest, icons; navigation fallback to cached `/index.html`; cache version `v1` → `v2` (`apps/citizen-pwa/public/sw.js`)
- Settings WCAG-AA contrast: 6× `text-[#768081]` → `text-surface-600`, 1× `text-[#a3adae]` → `text-surface-500` (`SettingsPage.tsx`)
- Settings `<main id="main-content">` landmark (same file)
- Wizard Step 2 silent submit: bottom action region always rendered with `role="status"` hint until a location method is picked (`Step2WhoWhere.tsx`)

**Round 2 (commit cdcf72b)** — 5 real bugs, 6 files (4 modified + 2 new):
- RegisterPage phone input a11y: `id`/`name`/`autoComplete="tel"` + real `<label htmlFor>`
- Phone preservation Login ↔ Register via `sessionStorage["bantayog.last-phone"]` + `useState` lazy initializer
- Step 1 Skip-photo silent submit: `reportType` defaults to `''` instead of seeded `'flood'`; `handleNext` validates with inline `role="alert"`; type buttons clear the error
- Wizard resumability: new `wizard-snapshot` service (localforage, 24h TTL, distinct from `draft-store`); `WizardContainer` loads on mount, saves on every step/formData change, clears on submit success and Step-1 back-to-home; `Step1Evidence` accepts `initialReportType` prop
- Photos intentionally not persisted in the snapshot (per-keystroke blob writes would bloat IDB; user re-attaches if needed)

## Booked, NOT in this PR (documented in `docs/progress.md`)

- **A-5 RegisterPage architecture** — `linkWithPhoneNumber` requires `currentUser` but the codebase has no `signInAnonymously` upstream. Fresh users hitting `/register` directly get "Not signed in" with no recovery. Design decision needed (link vs. fresh sign-in vs. anon-then-link).
- **Step 2 back-from-Step-3 field loss** — `Step2WhoWhere` mounts fresh on back navigation; needs `initialValues` props.

body:
## Summary

Adds AWS::KMS::ReplicaKey to the CFN provisioner. Looks up the primary multi-region key by ARN, clones the relevant fields, and inserts a replica with primary_region set so DescribeKey reports MultiRegionKeyType=REPLICA.

Since fakecloud is single-region, the replica gets a distinct 'mrk-replica-' id rather than colliding with the primary id (real AWS reuses the same id across regions, but fakecloud keys by id within one region).

Updates helpers::key_metadata_json so MultiRegionKeyType is computed from the stored primary_region pointer rather than always returning 'PRIMARY'. The PrimaryKey field of the multi-region configuration now points back at the primary's region/arn for replicas.

Closes BB14 of the parity-gap plan.

author: rymsha
body:
Part of #11991.

Audited `modules/lib/lib-auth/` against the Java handlers and TypeScript types. The Java handler is the runtime truth; this PR only updates JSDoc and JSDoc-only wording in `auth.ts`. No Java behavior or TS signatures are changed.

## Findings fixed

- **`getUser`** — said "returns *undefined*" when not logged in; Java returns `null`. Also updated `@returns {User}` to `@returns {User | null}` (TS signature is already `User | null`).
- **`createUser`** — was missing `@returns {User}`.
- **`createGroup`** — was missing `@returns {Group}`; the description for `params.description` was the broken "`as principal description .`" — replaced with `Group description.`.
- **`createRole`** — was missing `@param {object} params JSON parameters.`, missing `@returns {Role}`, and had the same broken `params.description` text — replaced with `Role description.`.
- **`modifyUser`** — `@returns {User}` had a stray double-space typo and dropped the `null` case; tightened to `@returns {User | null}` and cleaned the wording.
- **`modifyGroup` / `modifyRole`** — same null-case fix applied to `@returns`.
- **`addMembers`** — description said "Adds members to a principal (user or role)"; you don't add members to a user. The `principalKey` parameter is typed `GroupKey | RoleKey` in TS — corrected to "(group or role)".
- **`removeMembers`** — same "user or role" wording fix as `addMembers`. Also `@param {string} members` was wrong: `members` is an array (`string[]` / `(UserKey | GroupKey)[]`).
- **`findUsers`** — `params.count` comment said "Number of contents to fetch" (stale copy from `lib-content`) — corrected to "Number of users to fetch".

## Verification

- `./gradlew :lib:lib-auth:test` — green (TypeScript declarations regenerate as part of the build).
- No `integrationTest` source set in `lib-auth` and no `itest-lib-auth` module.

body:
## Summary
- skip `pendingIndexedRootRunsLocked` when buffered update planning can use the lazy primary-run index directly
- add a regression test covering many pending indexed flush units with an existing primary-run index
- add a focused microbenchmark for the direct indexed buffered-read path

## Why
A fresh #1159 profile on current `main` showed `collections.pendingIndexedRootRunsLocked` allocating ~568 MB in the two-index BSON update benchmark. The slice was built even though `domain.primaryRunIndex` was present and the fallback run scan was not used.

## Benchmarks / profiles
Baseline current main command:
```bash
PROFILE_DIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/gomap_1159_publish_profile_XXXXXX)
MONGO_GATEWAY_PROFILE_BENCH_UPDATE_DOCUMENTS=200000 \
MONGO_GATEWAY_PROFILE_BENCH_BATCH_SIZE=2000 \
MONGO_GATEWAY_PROFILE_BENCH_WRITERS=8 \
MONGO_GATEWAY_PROFILE_BENCH_BUFFERED_INDEXED_ASYNC_FLUSH=true \
MONGO_GATEWAY_PROFILE_BENCH_BUFFERED_INDEXED_ASYNC_FLUSH_MAX_QUEUED_UNITS=4 \
go test ./cmd/mongo_gateway_bench \
  -run '^$' \
  -bench '^BenchmarkDirectCollectionConcurrentUpdateBSONIndexes2$' \
  -benchtime=10s \
  -benchmem \
  -count=1 \
  -cpuprofile "$PROFILE_DIR/cpu.pprof" \
  -memprofile "$PROFILE_DIR/mem.pprof"
```

Baseline current main:
- `934137` iterations, `11346 ns/op`, `88138 docs/sec`, `1266 B/op`, `7 allocs/op`
- `pendingIndexedRootRunsLocked`: `568.27 MB` flat allocation, `7.52%` of alloc_space

After this PR, same command:
- `949586` iterations, `11938 ns/op`, `83766 docs/sec`, `1257 B/op`, `7 allocs/op`
- `pendingIndexedRootRunsLocked`: no longer appears in alloc_space profile (`go tool pprof -alloc_space -list pendingIndexedRootRunsLocked` reports no match)

Focused microbenchmark:
```bash
go test ./TreeDB/collections -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkSnapshotUpdateBatchBufferedReadPrimaryRunIndexPendingUnits$' -benchmem -count=5
```

Results:

- `412.4 ns/op`, `48 B/op`, `2 allocs/op`

author: andrew-adamson
body:
## Summary

Fixes #558.
Fixes #559.

This PR replaces index/path-derived AC/Sub-AC ownership with deterministic opaque execution-scoped node identities. New executions now use `execution_node_v1` metadata with stable `node_id` values generated from `execution_id + path`, while preserving legacy index metadata for backwards compatibility.

This fixes incorrect Sub-AC ownership/projection in recursive decomposition and aligns monitoring, runtime resume, cancellation, and event updates around the same canonical node model.

## Problem

Recursive Sub-AC execution previously relied on synthetic or legacy AC indexes for ownership. That created ambiguity once decomposition went deeper than one level:

- Sub-ACs could appear under the wrong parent in monitoring/HUD/TUI projections.
- Runtime identity and monitoring identity could diverge.
- `ac_index` was overloaded as both a scheduler/display concept and an ownership key.
- Deep recursive paths made path-like IDs brittle and hard to scale.
- Existing persisted sessions still contain legacy `ac_0`, `sub_ac_0_0`, or temporary one-based identifiers.

## Solution

Introduce opaque, deterministic execution-scoped node identity:

```json
{
  "identity_model": "execution_node_v1",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "execution_id": "exec_abc123",
  "node_id": "node_7YK4Q2J9F6",
  "parent_node_id": "node_9Q5H1P8K2A",
  "root_ac_index": 0,
  "root_ac_number": 1,
  "path": [0, 2, 1],
  "display_path": "1.3.2",
  "depth": 2,
  "ordinal": 1,
  "node_kind": "sub_ac"
}
```

Key behavior:

- `node_id` is now the canonical key for joins, runtime handles, resume cache, cancellation, and node update events.
- `parent_node_id` defines tree structure.
- `path` and `display_path` are only for ordering and UI labels.
- `ac_index`, `parent_ac_index`, and `sub_ac_index` remain only as legacy compatibility metadata.
- Runtime scopes for node-aware executions now use the opaque node identity.
- Resume lookup checks canonical node scope first, then known legacy scope aliases.

## Compatibility

This PR preserves old sessions and intermediate branch states by emitting and accepting transitional metadata:

- `legacy_node_id`
- `legacy_parent_node_id`
- `legacy_node_aliases`
- `legacy_parent_node_aliases`
- `legacy_session_scope_id`
- `legacy_session_scope_ids`
- `legacy_session_state_path`
- `legacy_session_state_paths`

That means new executions use the long-term opaque model, while old persisted events using `ac_0`, `sub_ac_0_0`, or the temporary one-based `ac_1` style can still be projected or resumed.

## Implementation Notes

Changed areas:

- `execution_runtime_scope.py`
  Defines opaque execution-scoped node IDs, legacy aliases, node metadata, and compatibility runtime scopes.

- `parallel_executor.py`
  Uses node identity for runtime ownership, emits node metadata on runtime/subtask events, and probes legacy scopes during resume.

- `adapter.py`
  Persists the new node/legacy metadata fields through runtime handles.

- `events.py`
  Updates runtime event documentation to reflect opaque IDs.

- Tests
  Adds coverage for opaque node generation, legacy aliases, legacy resume fallback, recursive Sub-AC ownership, deterministic event ordering, and subscription polling stability.

## Testing

Passed locally:

```bash
uv run --python 3.12 ruff check src/ tests/
uv run --python 3.12 ruff format --check src/ tests/
uv run --python 3.12 mypy src/ouroboros
```

Targeted branch-relevant suite:

```bash
uv run --python 3.12 pytest tests/unit/orchestrator/test_execution_runtime_scope.py tests/unit/orchestrator/test_parallel_executor.py tests/unit/orchestrator/test_runner.py tests/unit/orchestrator/test_session.py tests/unit/orchestrator/test_parallel_executor_recursive_depth.py tests/unit/mcp/tools/test_ac_tree_hud_handler.py tests/unit/tui/test_events.py tests/unit/tui/test_app.py -q
uv run --python 3.13 pytest tests/unit/orchestrator/test_execution_runtime_scope.py tests/unit/orchestrator/test_parallel_executor.py tests/unit/orchestrator/test_runner.py tests/unit/orchestrator/test_session.py tests/unit/orchestrator/test_parallel_executor_recursive_depth.py tests/unit/mcp/tools/test_ac_tree_hud_handler.py tests/unit/tui/test_events.py tests/unit/tui/test_app.py -q
uv run --python 3.14 pytest tests/unit/orchestrator/test_execution_runtime_scope.py tests/unit/orchestrator/test_parallel_executor.py tests/unit/orchestrator/test_runner.py tests/unit/orchestrator/test_session.py tests/unit/orchestrator/test_parallel_executor_recursive_depth.py tests/unit/mcp/tools/test_ac_tree_hud_handler.py tests/unit/tui/test_events.py tests/unit/tui/test_app.py -q
```

Result for each Python version:

```text
297 passed, 1 skipped
```

TypeScript plugin:

```bash
bunx tsc --noEmit
```

Passed.

## Local CI Caveat

Full upstream Linux CI could not be fully reproduced on this Windows machine:

- Native Windows full pytest hits unrelated platform assumptions around path separators, command execution, and file locking.
- Native Windows `bun test` fails POSIX path expectations when tests mock Linux/Darwin.
- WSL command execution was killed immediately.
- Docker is installed but the Linux engine was not running.

The branch-specific Python suite passes across the same Python versions as upstream, and full-tree lint/format/mypy pass.

## Summary

Per-org Slack manifest (YAML) + Teams app `.zip` package generators with an operator-gated download endpoint and a "Generate manifest for IT" button on disconnected Slack/Teams tiles. Implements SPEC § 3.4 (Multi-tenant manifest generation).

- `lib/connectors/manifests/slack.ts` — YAML manifest, bot scopes sourced from `providers.ts`, slash commands sourced from C-1B's parser, per-org `display_information.name`/`bot_user.display_name`/`oauth_config.redirect_urls`/`event_subscriptions.request_url`
- `lib/connectors/manifests/teams.ts` — Teams app schema 1.16+ `manifest.json` + 192×192 color + 32×32 outline PNG placeholders packaged via JSZip; deterministic UUID per org so re-downloads are idempotent
- `app/api/connectors/[type]/manifest/route.ts` — `GET ?org_id={org}`, operator-gated, `slack`→YAML, `teams`→zip, `hubspot`→404
- `ConnectorsView` + `ConnectorTile` — adds `tertiaryAction` prop; UI surfaces the manifest download on disconnected Slack/Teams tiles only

Adds `jszip@3.10.1` and `js-yaml@4.1.1` (+ `@types/js-yaml`). Combined transitive footprint is small; Vercel function bundle remains far under the 50MB Lambda limit.

## SECURITY REVIEW CHECKLIST

- [x] Manifest endpoint operator-gated (non-operators get 403). `app/api/connectors/[type]/manifest/route.ts` calls `isOperatorRequest(req)` first and short-circuits with `403 forbidden` when false.
- [x] Generated manifests don't leak `customer_org_id` beyond the requesting org. `org_id` is parsed from the query string, validated against `[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}`, and embedded only into the requested tenant's manifest body. The endpoint is read-only — there is no DB lookup that could return another tenant's row.
- [x] Slack signing secret + Teams JWT keys NOT included in manifest body. The Slack manifest only emits public scope names and request URLs; the signing secret stays in `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET`. The Teams manifest only emits the public bot ID (read from `TEAMS_BOT_ID`); `TEAMS_CLIENT_SECRET` and `TEAMS_BOT_PASSWORD` never appear in the body. Test `manifest-slack.test.ts > 'does not leak the slack signing secret'` and `manifest-teams.test.ts > 'does not leak teams client secret'` assert this.
- [x] Generated icons / brand assets safe. Icons are byte-perfect placeholder PNGs constructed locally from `node:zlib` deflate. No SVG, no foreign-content, no embedded JS. Only the PNG signature, IHDR, IDAT, IEND chunks.

# Summary

- Added the `KvStoreService` proto schema and a buf config to lint it
- Wired `protoc` + `grpc_cpp_plugin` into the CMake build, emitting generated code into a separate `kv_proto` library
- Installed gRPC and Protobuf packages on the Linux CI runners

## Rationale

- Keeping the generated code in its own library means the project's `-Werror` policy doesn't trip on protobuf-generated warnings
- Only `find_package(gRPC CONFIG REQUIRED)` is called explicitly – it pulls Protobuf in transitively, which avoids a platform mismatch where macOS Homebrew ships `protobuf-config.cmake` but Ubuntu's apt packages only support the legacy `FindProtobuf` module
- Versioned package layout (`kv.v1` -> `proto/kv/v1/kv.proto`) so adding a v2 later doesn't require restructuring

author: jesseblueberry
body:
### Motivation
- Improve landing-page startup performance on slow connections by allowing the app to skip avatar/expression image loading and open a text-first grid immediately.
- Provide a user-control to enable a non-blocking "slow connection" mode so preloading of chat assets does not delay UI render.

### Description
- Introduce `useSlowConnectionMode` and `startupFastTrackRequested` flags in `LandingPage` to control non-blocking startup and fast-track rendering when requested.
- Change startup flow so when slow mode is active the code uses `Promise.allSettled` for `card.load()` (does not block render) and fast-tracks the card grid rendering early by short-circuiting the await path using `startupFastTrackRequested`.
- Update card rendering to honor a new `settings.loadAvatars` flag and render a styled placeholder when `loadAvatars === false` instead of loading images, and keep `showExpression` handling for expressions otherwise (`Card.js`).
- Add a "Use Slow Connection Mode" button to the startup UI and rename/replace the previous skip-thumbnails control, plus cleanup and DOM refresh logic in `renderContent` to avoid duplicate wrapper/menu nodes (`LandingPage.js`).
- Add CSS for avatar placeholders in `style.css` to visually indicate text-first cards when avatars are skipped.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for these changes.

author: hyperpolymath
body:
Cargo `--lib --tests` and `cargo clippy --lib --tests` now run clean (0
warnings, 0 errors). 1460 unit + integration tests pass.

Real bugs found and fixed:

* `provers::mod::from_str`: `"prob"` alias was double-claimed. Line 525
  routes it to `ProverKind::ProB` (B-method model checker); a later arm
  also tried to claim it for `ProverKind::ProbabilisticTypeChecker`
  (unreachable). Removed the dead alias — `prob-types` and
  `probabilistic` still reach the type-checker.
* `gnn::fallback_monitor::record_fallback`: comment claimed
  "exponential moving average" with an unused `ema_weight = 0.2` local,
  but the formula is a cumulative arithmetic mean (and tests assert
  cumulative-mean values). Updated the comment to reflect actual
  behaviour and dropped the dead variable; SLA semantics unchanged.
* `dispatch::cross_check_dispatch`: the cross-checker filter held the
  `health_status` `MutexGuard` across an `await` (clippy
  `await_holding_lock`). Restructured into an explicit scope so the
  guard is released before any await.
* GraphQL workspace member did not compile: `cargo check -p
  echidna-graphql` reported 28 missing `ProverKind` variants. Synced
  `schema.rs` enum + `core_to_gql` + `gql_to_core`, `resolvers.rs`
  `ProverKindExt::{from_core,to_core}`, and `ffi_wrapper.rs` ordinals
  113-140 with the core enum. (Mizar/MizAR are intentionally distinct.)

Compliance fix:

* `deno.json` license was `MIT OR AGPL-3.0-or-later` — project policy
  per CLAUDE.md is `PMPL-1.0-or-later` (explicitly "not AGPL").

Diagnostics fields preserved as ML acronyms:

* `ModelHealth.{last_validation_nDCG, last_validation_MRR,
  nDCG_meets_threshold}` and `GnnTrainingMetrics.{nDCG, MRR}` now
  carry an `#[allow(non_snake_case)]` with a comment explaining that
  these field names match the JSON keys emitted by the Julia training
  pipeline (`src/julia/train_and_evaluate.jl`). Renaming would have
  silently broken the cross-language contract.

Resilience accessors:

* Exposed `CircuitBreaker::name(&self) -> &str` and
  `Bulkhead::config(&self) -> &BulkheadConfig` so the previously
  dead-but-stored fields are usable for diagnostics output.

Remaining clippy items (mechanical): unused imports, doc list
indentation, a few `field_reassign_with_default` cases (kept as-is
with `#[allow(...)]` where the alternative is uglier), and type
aliases for two complex closure-box types.

Out of scope (left untouched): pre-existing `cargo fmt` drift across
~820 files, `cargo test --workspace` requires `protoc` (gRPC build),
docs/* license-string drift in historical release notes, ROADMAP-
acknowledged ReScript→AffineScript migration.

author: haritsrhn
body:
## Summary

- **CheckRole middleware** (`app/Http/Middleware/CheckRole.php`): accepts variadic role slugs via route definition, grants access if user holds at least one, returns 403 JSON in Bahasa Indonesia otherwise
- **CheckPermission middleware** (`app/Http/Middleware/CheckPermission.php`): validates a single permission slug; automatically narrows the check to `active_entity_id` when set by EntityScope
- **EntityScope middleware** (`app/Http/Middleware/EntityScope.php`): resolves active entity from `?entity_id` query param (holding_admin / super_admin only) or primary employment; blocks cross-entity access for entity_admin; injects `active_entity_id` into request attributes for downstream consumers
- **Middleware aliases** registered in `bootstrap/app.php` (`role`, `permission`, `entity.scope`) using Laravel 13's fluent API — no Kernel.php
- **ApiResponse trait** (`app/Http/Resources/ApiResponse.php`): `success()` and `error()` helpers that produce consistent `{ data, message, status }` envelopes
- **Base Controller** updated to expose `success()` / `error()` helpers on all concrete controllers
- **6 stub controllers** (Entity, Employee, Attendance, Leave, Payroll, Location) — all methods return `501 Coming soon` so routes resolve without errors
- **routes/api.php** expanded with 30 MVP routes across 6 resource groups, each guarded with the correct combination of `auth:sanctum`, `entity.scope`, `role:…`, and `permission:…`

## Security design decisions

- `entity_admin` attempting `?entity_id=<other>` → immediate 403 (no DB query leaks)
- `super_admin` is exempt from primary-employment requirement in EntityScope (global scope)
- Attendance routes intentionally omit `entity.scope` at the group level — employees are mobile; the controller enforces entity isolation via the employment record on clock events
- `/employees/import` is declared before `/{user}` to prevent Laravel routing the literal string "import" as a user ID

## Acceptance criteria

| Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|
| No token | 401 (Sanctum) |
| Valid token, wrong role | 403 `{"message":"Anda tidak memiliki akses…","status":403}` |
| entity_admin with `?entity_id` of another entity | 403 |
| super_admin with any `?entity_id` | 200 (passes through) |
| All response bodies | `{"data":…,"message":…,"status":…}` |

## Files created / modified

| File | Action |
|---|---|
| `backend/app/Http/Middleware/CheckRole.php` | Created |
| `backend/app/Http/Middleware/CheckPermission.php` | Created |
| `backend/app/Http/Middleware/EntityScope.php` | Created |
| `backend/app/Http/Resources/ApiResponse.php` | Created |
| `backend/app/Http/Controllers/EntityController.php` | Created (stub) |
| `backend/app/Http/Controllers/EmployeeController.php` | Created (stub) |
| `backend/app/Http/Controllers/AttendanceController.php` | Created (stub) |
| `backend/app/Http/Controllers/LeaveController.php` | Created (stub) |
| `backend/app/Http/Controllers/PayrollController.php` | Created (stub) |
| `backend/app/Http/Controllers/LocationController.php` | Created (stub) |
| `backend/app/Http/Controllers/Controller.php` | Modified |

| `backend/routes/api.php` | Modified |

author: senamakel
body:
Follow-up to #1100 / #1102. Both prior fixes left the cleanup wired through a bash `trap`. The most recent staging run still exits 1 right after a successful symbol upload:

\`\`\`
[INFO] Successfully uploaded symbols for openhuman@0.53.9+dc4f91a151ca
scripts/upload_sentry_symbols.sh: line 247: tmp_dir: unbound variable
[INFO] === Upload complete ===
Error: Process completed with exit code 1
\`\`\`

## Root cause

Bash traps are **globally scoped**, not function-scoped. A `trap '... \$tmp_dir ...' RETURN` defined inside `ensure_sentry_cli` fires on EVERY subsequent function return — including `main`'s at end-of-script. By that point `local tmp_dir` is gone and \`set -u\` errors out. EXIT has the same scoping problem; there is no clean way to limit a bash trap to one function's lifetime.

## Fix

Drop the trap entirely.

- `mv` already empties `tmp_dir` on the success path; the function ends with an explicit `rm -rf "$tmp_dir"` to remove the now-empty directory.
- Each early-exit branch (download fail, empty file, HTML page, install-dir unwritable) gets an inline `rm -rf "$tmp_dir"` before its `exit 1`.

Worst case if `set -e` triggers between `mktemp` and the next inline cleanup, `/tmp` leaks one directory until the OS sweeps it.

## Test plan

- [ ] Re-trigger **Release (Staging)** and confirm the `Upload Tauri shell debug symbols` step exits 0 cleanly after \"Successfully uploaded symbols\".
- [ ] Confirm no `tmp_dir: unbound variable` regression appears anywhere in subsequent runs.

* **Chores**
  * Improved internal cleanup handling in the Sentry symbols upload script to prevent temporary file accumulation.

author: copilot
body:
On H1, the EMA5–EMA89 spread in an active TM-phase trend routinely exceeds 60–120 pips. With `EmaFanMaxTotalPips = 25.0` (an M1/M5-calibrated value), the filter fires on virtually every bar, returning `TS=0` before PSAR or DPI are ever evaluated — silently killing valid pullback-recovery entries.

DPI already covers this use case: a yellow histogram signals recovery after an overextended pullback, making the fan filter redundant.

## Change

`SEA_Presets.mqh` — `PRESET_RRM_ORG` block only:

```mql5
// Before
cfg.EmaFanFilterEnabled = true;
cfg.EmaFanMaxTotalPips  = 25.0;

// After
cfg.EmaFanFilterEnabled = false;
cfg.EmaFanMaxTotalPips  = 25.0;   // value retained for reference, filter is off
```

`PRESET_RRM` and all other blocks are untouched.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


## Problem

In `SEA_Presets.mqh`, `PRESET_RRM_ORG` has the `EmaFanFilter` enabled with `EmaFanMaxTotalPips = 25.0`. This threshold was calibrated for M1/M5. On H1 EURUSD in an active TM-phase trend, the EMA5 vs EMA89 spread routinely exceeds 60–120 pips, and the gap continues expanding while the trend is healthy. This means the filter fires on virtually every bar during a valid H1 trend, returning TS=0 before PSAR or DPI are ever evaluated.

The EMA fan gap condition is already covered by DPI: when the DPI histogram turns yellow it signals the recovery moment after an overextended pullback. The fan filter is therefore redundant and destructive in this preset.

## Fix

In `SEA_Presets.mqh`, inside the `PRESET_RRM_ORG` block only, change:

```
// Before:
cfg.EmaFanFilterEnabled   = true;
cfg.EmaFanMaxTotalPips    = 25.0;

// After:
cfg.EmaFanFilterEnabled   = false;
cfg.EmaFanMaxTotalPips    = 25.0;   // value retained for reference, filter is off
```

**Do NOT change anything else.** CandleBody settings, DPI settings, PSAR settings and all other preset blocks remain completely untouched.

## File to change

`SEA_Presets.mqh` — `PRESET_RRM_ORG` block only.


The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

Assistant: Now I have the full picture. The decoded content confirms: **`PRESET_RRM_ORG` also sets `EmaFanFilterEnabled = true` and `EmaFanMaxTotalPips = 25.0`** — same wrong value. This is confirmed directly from the code.

Your three points are all valid and actionable. Here's a precise diagnosis:

---

## 1. The EMA Fan Filter — Wrong Concept for This EA, Wrong Value for H1

The code in `PRESET_RRM_ORG`:
```mql5 name=SEA_Presets.mqh url=https://github.com/msmaciej/RRM_SEA/blob/main/SEA_Presets.mqh
cfg.EmaFanFilterEnabled   = true;
cfg.EmaFanMaxTotalPips    = 25.0;   // ← M1/M5 calibrated, fires constantly on H1
```

**You are right on two levels:**

- **Concept is wrong:** This entire filter is pip-based — exactly what you've deactivated everywhere else in the EA. Your EA uses dynamic SL (swing + cushion), not fixed pips, for the same reason pips are instrument/TF-agnostic. The EMA fan filter contradicts that philosophy entirely.

- **Value is wrong for H1:** Even its own comment says `M15/H1: consider 40–60 pips`. But it hardcodes `25.0` for all presets including `PRESET_RRM_ORG`.

**Your instinct is correct:** The fan overextension concept is valid (avoid chasing spike candles), but it belongs in the **CandleBody filter**, which you already have locked ON in `PRESET_RRM_ORG`:

```mql5 name=SEA_Presets.mqh url=https://github.com/msmaciej/RRM_SEA/blob/main/SEA_Presets.mqh
cfg.Ind_CandleBody_Enabled = true;
cfg.CandleBody_AvgPeriod   = 15;
cfg.CandleBody_MaxMult     = 3.5;      // blocks if candle > 3.5× avg body
cfg.CandleBody_CheckBars   = 2;        // checks 2 bars (H1+)
cfg.CandleBody_RequireDirection = true;
```

The CandleBody filter already blocks spike/overextension candles in a **TF-adaptive, pip-free way** — exactly as you described.

---

## 2. What This Means for Your Missed Trades

On the H1 EURUSD chart, during the April 2026 trending run you circled:
- EMA5–EMA89 gap routinely exceeds 25 pips while still expanding
- **Every single bar in an active trend will fire `EMA_OVEREXT`** and return `TS=0`
- The CandleBody filter never gets a chance to run

This is why **clusters of valid pullback entries are silently killed** — not because they fail the RRM structural checks (Phase/Layer/Recovery/BarClose/PSAR/DPI), but because a secondary pip filter that shouldn't exist for this preset fires first.

---

## Fix — Two Clear Actions

**1. Remove the EMA Fan Filter from `PRESET_RRM_ORG` (and `PRESET_RRM`):**
```mql5 name=SEA_Presets.mqh
// In PRESET_RRM_ORG block — change to:
cfg.EmaFanFilterEnabled   = false;   // CandleBody handles spike protection
cfg.EmaFanMaxTotalPips    = 0.0;
```

**2. Decide the long-term fate of `EmaFanMaxTotalPips` globally:** Since the CandleBody filter covers the same use case without pip hardcoding, the EMA fan filter is redundant and inconsistent with EA design. Either remove it entirely from the codebase or keep it only as an opt-in `PRESET_CUSTOM` tool with `false` as default everywhere else.

The missed trades in your screenshot are almost certainly all `EMA_OVEREXT` rejections. Enable `DebugFlow=true` in the next test run and you'll see it confirmed in the Journal for every red-line bar.

User: EMA Fan Filter should be removed entirely from the code, not  only from specific PRESETs. Additionally: screenshot and marked manually potential trades do not refer at all Fan Filter. These marked TS=1 show where TS=1 should be evaluated, if not on specific bars, then perhaps bar or two later. Instead we do not see any trades there

## Summary

Mirrors xradar's [`open_nexradlevel2_datatree(list_of_bytes)`](https://docs.openradarscience.org/projects/xradar/en/stable/notebooks/nexrad_read_chunks.html) API for NOAA's live `unidata-nexrad-level2-chunks` S3 bucket. Each volume in that bucket is split into many small files (`S` + `I00..In` + `E`) that arrive seconds after each scan, vs. minutes for the assembled `noaa-nexrad-level2` archive.

## API

* `radish.read_nexrad_chunks(list[bytes]) -> VolumeData` — low-level Rust pipeline
* `radish.open_nexrad_chunks_datatree(list[bytes | path]) -> xarray.DataTree` — one-liner for the xarray side
* Rust: `NexradBackend::read_chunks_volume(Vec<Vec<u8>>) -> VolumeData`

## How it works

Concatenating `[S, I00, ..., E]` reconstitutes a complete Archive II buffer byte-for-byte (volume header from `S`, then the LDM record stream across all chunks), so we hand it to the same decoder used by `read_nexrad`. A truncated volume (no `E`, or only the first few `I` chunks) decodes whatever rays survive — incomplete trailing sweeps come through with fewer rays than the VCP would normally produce. That matches xradar's `incomplete_sweep="drop"` default; an explicit `"pad"` mode is deferred.

## Live demo

Added `python/examples/read_chunks.ipynb` — 18 cells walking through the workflow end-to-end against the live S3 bucket via `fsspec` + `s3fs`. Sample run on KLOT volume 758 (VCP-35 clear-air, 55 chunks, ~3 MB):

* radish 0.658 s, xradar 1.513 s → **2.30× speedup**
* 16/16 root MSG_2/MSG_5 attrs match xradar verbatim
* 12 sweeps × 9 per-sweep attrs = **108 pairs, 0 mismatches**
* Partial volume of 18/55 chunks decodes 3 sweeps (incomplete-volume path works)

## Tests

* Rust unit: `concat_chunks` byte-for-byte preservation, empty-list edge case
* Rust integration (gated on `RADISH_NEXRAD_FIXTURE`): split a full file in thirds, decode via chunks API, assert metadata + nexrad attrs match the path-based read
* Python: 4-way byte-split round-trip, `open_nexrad_chunks_datatree` accepts `bytes` and path inputs, output equal to engine-based read on the same fixture

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --all-features`
- [x] `pytest python/tests/` against KLOT fixture — 14 pass (3 new chunks tests)
- [x] `ruff check`, `black --check`, `mypy` clean
- [x] Notebook executes end-to-end against live S3 in <30 s
- [ ] CI green on push

## Summary

The Pipeline DAG drew two **edges that don't exist in the reducer**:
- `verifier → coordinator → builder-fallback` — coordinator is host-inline; reducer spawns fallback directly on FAIL+breaker_OPEN (`src/reducer/index.ts:300`)
- `verifier → validator` as a routing edge — it's actually a conditional anti-deception side-effect (`src/reducer/index.ts:226`), not a handoff

Now every edge is grounded against a specific reducer line. **6 edge type vocabulary** encodes the full routing flow:

| Type | Color/Style | Routes |
|---|---|---|
| `handoff`   | indigo solid | 8 standard reducer-driven spawns |
| `rollback`  | amber dashed (curves up) | `verifier → planner-lead` (FAIL+breaker_CLOSED, line 309) |
| `fallback`  | red dashed (curves down) | `verifier → builder-fallback` (FAIL+breaker_OPEN, line 300) |
| `terminal`  | green solid | `verifier → done` (PASS, line 288) |
| `audit`     | pink dotted | `verifier ⇢ validator` (anti-deception violations only, line 226) |
| `intervene` | gray dotted | `user ⇢ {planner, builder, verifier}` (`user.veto` line 322 + `user.intervene(goto=X)` line 396) |

Adds **`done` terminal node** (lime + glow on any `kind=done`). **Phase A·B / C / D** background zones, palette aligned to `skills/mermaid-diagrams/SKILL.md`.

`WEAVE_TARGET` expanded: `step.research → planner-lead` resume (line 546). New `weaveTargetForVerdict()` branches ripple by verdict (PASS→done, FAIL+(builder-error≥3)→fallback, FAIL→planner). `edgePath()` curves rollback up-and-over and fallback down-and-under to avoid main-flow overlap.

author: patebry
body:
## Summary

- Adds `TXRVDenseNet121NIHBackbone` — a `BackbonePort` implementation backed by torchxrayvision's NIH-pretrained DenseNet121. Produces 1024-dim penultimate features and unlocks a +0.054 macro-AUROC lift over the ResNet50/ImageNet baseline (0.643 -> 0.697 on n=4998 in the embedding ablation, identical downstream pipeline, zero model training).
- Lifts the proven ad-hoc adapter from `/tmp/txrv_embed_ablation/run.py` into the v1 surface with TDD discipline, strict types, contract test subclass, factory variant smoke test, and a `pyproject` extras update.
- The factory wiring (`build_publication_runner_v1(backbone="txrv-densenet121")`) shipped on the parallel LR-head PR; this PR provides the adapter the kwarg references, plus the smoke test that exercises that path end-to-end.

## Quality gates

| gate | result |
| ---- | ------ |
| `pytest tests/` (default) | 459 passed, 62 deselected in 3.59s |
| `pytest tests/ -m torch` | 60 passed, 461 deselected in 55.86s |
| `pytest tests/ -m smoke` | 8 passed, 513 deselected in 39.87s |
| `pytest tests/harness/unit/test_txrv_backbone.py -m torch` (TDD) | 14 passed in 3.42s |
| `pytest tests/harness/contract/test_backbone_contract.py -m torch` | 18 passed, 13 deselected in 6.81s |
| `ruff check harness/ tests/harness/` | clean |
| `mypy --strict harness/` | clean (48 source files) |
| `mypy --strict tests/harness/` | clean (34 source files) |

## TDD evidence

- **RED**: `pytest tests/harness/unit/test_txrv_backbone.py -m torch` → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'harness.adapters.torch.txrv_backbone'` (collection error before implementation landed).
- **GREEN**: same command after `harness/adapters/torch/txrv_backbone.py` was added → `14 passed in 3.42s`.

## Built by

1 subagent, single-wave TDD implementation.
- Wave 1: read `BackbonePort`, existing torchvision adapter, `/tmp/txrv_embed_ablation/run.py`, and the existing contract / unit-test patterns.
- Wave 2: write failing unit tests + contract subclass + smoke test (RED). Implement adapter + `__init__.py` re-export + pyproject extras + mypy override (GREEN). Three iterations on mypy strict (`Tensor` not callable on `model.features`; resolved by capturing `features` before narrowing `_model` to `nn.Module`).

## Implementation notes

- Eval-only: `model.eval()` once at construction; `extract` runs in `torch.no_grad()`; classifier head replaced with `nn.Identity`. Drives `model.features -> F.relu -> adaptive_avg_pool2d -> flatten` directly so features match what TXRV's pretrained classifier consumes.
- MPS-safe chunking at default `chunk_size=32`. The ad-hoc agent had to add this to avoid MPSGraph INT_MAX activations on whole-split forwards; the chunk_size is exposed as a constructor kwarg so unit tests exercise the loop with tiny tensors.
- Determinism: `torch.manual_seed(seed)` inside `__init__`, never globally. Mirrors the documented v1 deviation in the existing torchvision adapter.
- Identifier: `"txrv-densenet121-res224-nih"`. Distinct from any torchvision identifier so a `CachedBackbone` wrapping this instance shards into its own subdirectory (no stale-feature footgun when callers swap variants).
- `[experiment]` extras: `torchxrayvision>=1.3,<2`. mypy `ignore_missing_imports` extended to cover `torchxrayvision.*` (no type stubs ship with the library).

## Caveats

- TXRV NIH weights were trained on the full NIH-14 corpus including any rows used for evaluation here. Absolute AUROC is optimistically biased; only the **delta** vs ImageNet baselines is paper-defensible. Document this in any model card / paper writeup that uses this adapter.
- The factory `build_publication_runner_v1(backbone="...")` kwarg defaults to `"resnet50"`. Default flip is deferred so existing Step 3 baseline numbers remain reproducible without an opt-in.

## Test plan

- [x] Reproducible install: `.venv/bin/pip install torchxrayvision` already shipped from yesterday's experiment.
- [x] Default suite passes (`pytest tests/`): 459 passed in 3.59s.
- [x] Torch suite passes (`pytest tests/ -m torch`): 60 passed in 55.86s.
- [x] Smoke suite passes (`pytest tests/ -m smoke`): 8 passed in 39.87s.
- [x] Lint (`ruff check`) clean.
- [x] Type (`mypy --strict`) clean on harness/ and tests/harness/.
- [x] Real `densenet121-res224-nih` weights loaded and forward-pass exercised by both unit and contract tests.

## Out of scope

- Default flip from `resnet50` to `txrv-densenet121` in the factory.
- `RadImageNetResNet50Backbone` variant (already documented as v1.1+ in ARCHITECTURE.md §13.5).
- `ARCHITECTURE.md §13` update documenting this third torch backbone — left for a follow-up doc PR so this PR stays adapter-scoped.

author: zetermordio
body:
## Summary

Tenor is one of gifgrep's two search providers, and Google has announced the Tenor API will be fully decommissioned on June 30, 2026. This moves the Tenor-backed search path to Klipy, while keeping `--source tenor` working as a compatibility alias.

## Why

`auto` currently falls back to Tenor when `GIPHY_API_KEY` is not set, so default search will break for users without Giphy credentials once Tenor shuts down.

Klipy documents a Tenor migration path using `api.klipy.com` and a Klipy API key:
https://docs.klipy.com/migrate-from-tenor.md

Klipy also describes the team as including ex-Tenor founder, leadership, and tech team members:
https://www.linkedin.com/company/klipyco

## Changes

- Add Klipy v2 search via `https://api.klipy.com/v2/search`
- Add `--source klipy`
- Keep `--source tenor` as an alias resolving to Klipy
- Update `auto` fallback to Klipy when Giphy is not configured
- Replace `TENOR_API_KEY` docs/help with `KLIPY_API_KEY`
- Keep Giphy behavior unchanged
- Add Klipy attribution in the TUI
- Update mocks and regression tests

## Validation

- `make test`
- `make lint`
- `go test -race ./...`
- `go build ./...`
- Live smoke with `KLIPY_API_KEY` for both `--source klipy` and the `--source tenor` alias

author: leftibot
body:
Automated fix by @leftibot.

### What changed

> Fix #612: Allow fun<Signature>(&overloaded) for overload disambiguation
> The cheatsheet's "preferred" syntax for binding overloaded free functions,
> fun<Ret(Args...)>(&overloaded), only worked on MSVC because the existing
> fun<T>(T&&) overload sets T to a function type when called explicitly,
> which produces a function rvalue-reference parameter that does not match
> a function pointer argument. Standards-conforming compilers (clang, GCC
> in some modes) correctly rejected it.
> Added two new fun overloads, parameterized on the explicitly-supplied
> function-type Signature and using std::type_identity_t to keep that
> parameter non-deducible, so they only participate in overload resolution
> when Signature is given explicitly. One accepts a free function pointer,
> the other a pointer-to-member, enabling both fun<Ret(Args...)>(&free_fn)
> and fun<Ret(Args...) cv>(&Class::method) to disambiguate overloads
> without resorting to static_cast.

### Files
```
 .../chaiscript/dispatchkit/register_function.hpp   | 37 ++++++++++++
 unittests/compiled_tests.cpp                       | 68 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 2 files changed, 105 insertions(+)
```

Closes #612

_Triggered by @lefticus._

## Summary

Centralises real beer-label photos used to manually exercise the \`POST /scan\` endpoint end-to-end. Until a YOLO checkpoint is trained and the live mobile barcode scanner ships (issue #803, PR2.5a chantier), hand-captured photos are the only way to validate the full ML pipeline (\`infer\` -> \`ocr\` -> \`extract\` -> \`recommender\`) on real-world input.

## Changes

| File | Status | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| \`scan-photos/.gitignore\` | NEW (committed) | Exclude every file in the folder except the 3 anchor files |
| \`scan-photos/README.md\` | NEW (committed) | Purpose, naming convention, workflow, OS notes (HEIC), retention policy |
| \`scan-photos/findings.md\` | NEW (committed) | Append-only test session log |

Photo files (jpg/png/heic/webp) are intentionally **not committed**: heavy, personal, low repository value. The folder structure + README + findings log stay under version control so the folder is self-documenting and the test history persists across machines.

## Naming convention (suggested)

\`\`\`
YYYY-MM-DD_<beer-slug>_<face>.jpg
\`\`\`

Examples: \`2026-05-02_pelforth-brune_front.jpg\`, \`2026-05-02_chouffe-blonde_back.jpg\`, \`2026-05-02_unknown-craft-no-name.jpg\`.

## .gitignore pattern

The folder uses a local \`.gitignore\` rather than adding to the package-level \`.gitignore\` so the rules are co-located with the data they govern (more discoverable for future contributors):

\`\`\`gitignore
*
!.gitignore
!README.md
!findings.md
\`\`\`

Verified manually: a \`fake-photo.jpg\` dropped in the folder is correctly ignored, while the 3 anchor files stay tracked.

## Why now

Manual /scan validation is needed **before** committing time to PR2.5a (live barcode mobile scanner). The first session today (2026-05-02) immediately surfaced an OCR pipeline bug (paragraph=True silently dropped all results on dispersed-text labels) — fixed in PR coming next.

- [x] README documents the workflow + naming + OS notes

- [x] No \`Any\`, no inline styles introduced

body:
# Hypothesis: Surface-decoder-only FiLM normal conditioning for wsy/wsz (Wave 14 reassignment R2)

**Reassignment context**: This is a reassignment of closed PR #441, which expired its 30-min ACK deadline. The hypothesis is unchanged. **Strict 30-min ACK deadline applies — post your W&B run ID within 30 minutes of receiving this PR or it will be closed and the work permanently reassigned to another student.**

## Why this hypothesis

The current best baseline (alphonse PR #174, val_abupt = 6.9549%) is bottlenecked by wall-shear axes:
- wsy = 8.7345% (target 3.65% — **5.08pp gap**)
- wsz = 10.5766% (target 3.63% — **6.95pp gap**)

The previous FiLM-every-block experiment (gilbert PR #346) **falsified trunk-level normal conditioning**: ep10 abupt looked OK (8.86%) but wsy/wsz were ~2pp WORSE than baseline. Diagnosis: FiLM applied across every block in the shared trunk diluted volume-pressure capacity into surface-only conditioning, hurting overall axis balance.

**This experiment isolates the conditioning to the surface decoder only**, leaving the shared trunk untouched. Hypothesis: surface normals are physically meaningful for wall-shear prediction (shear is tangential to the surface), but the conditioning signal needs to be applied where surface features are read out — not in the shared backbone.

## Implementation

Add a `--film-surface-decoder` flag. When enabled:

1. **Conditioning input**: Surface normal vector at each point (3-dim). Surface normals are already computed and available in the surface batch.
2. **FiLM generator MLP**: `Linear(3 → 64) → GELU → Linear(64 → 2 * hidden_dim)`, output split into `gamma` and `beta`. **Initialize the output Linear's weights and biases to zero** so γ=0, β=0 at init → identity FiLM (gamma=1+0, beta=0). This gives a clean ablation: at step 0 the network is identical to the baseline.
3. **Where to apply**: Inside the surface decoder MLP only. The DrivAerML model has a separate surface decoder head — apply FiLM after each linear+activation in that head: `h = h * (1 + gamma) + beta`. **Do NOT touch the shared trunk or the volume decoder.** Volume pressure prediction must be unchanged.
4. **No FiLM in volume decoder**: This is the critical contrast vs. PR #346.

## Reproduce command

```bash
cd target/ && torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=4 train.py \
  --model-layers 5 \
  --model-hidden-dim 256 \
  --model-heads 4 \
  --fourier-pe \
  --no-use-ema \
  --lr 3e-4 \
  --lr-cosine-t-max 50 \
  --no-compile-model \
  --film-surface-decoder \
  --agent gilbert \
  --wandb-group bengio-wave14 \
  --wandb-name gilbert-surface-dec-film-normal-r2-5l256d-tmax50
```

## Gate schedule (kill if NOT below)

| Epoch | val_abupt kill threshold |
|-------|--------------------------|
| ep5   | < 13.0%                  |
| ep10  | < 10.0%                  |
| ep15  | < 8.9%                   |
| ep30  | < 7.5%                   |
| ep50  | must beat 6.9549%        |

**Critical reporting requirement**: At each gate, report `val_primary/wall_shear_y_rel_l2_pct` and `val_primary/wall_shear_z_rel_l2_pct` separately. The hypothesis succeeds only if wsy/wsz improve materially vs the alphonse PR #174 baseline (wsy 8.7345%, wsz 10.5766%) — even if abupt is similar, a clear binding-axis improvement at zero cost to vol_p (must remain ≤ 4.5%) is mergeable.

## Hard constraints

- `--no-compile-model`: Mandatory (PyTorch 2.x Inductor crash at validation)
- `--fourier-pe`: Mandatory (n_params confirms FourierEmbed presence — comparability)
- Correct grad-clip flag if you tweak it: `--grad-clip-norm` (NOT `--grad-clip`)
- Volume decoder must remain identical to baseline — verify via grad flow if uncertain
- Epochs hard cap: `SENPAI_MAX_EPOCHS`; wall-clock: `SENPAI_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`

## Baseline metrics (alphonse PR #174, run vu4jsiic)

| Metric | val |
|--------|-----|
| val_primary/abupt_axis_mean_rel_l2_pct | **6.9549** |
| val_primary/surface_pressure_rel_l2_pct | 4.5644 |
| val_primary/volume_pressure_rel_l2_pct | 3.9361 ✓ |
| val_primary/wall_shear_y_rel_l2_pct | 8.7345 |
| val_primary/wall_shear_z_rel_l2_pct | 10.5766 |

## ACK requirement (HARD)

Post a comment on this PR within **30 minutes** of receipt with:

author: guillaumelaurin
body:
## Description

**What.** Ports `cest::hotpatch` to Windows on x86_64 and ARM64, and exposes two
new CMake facets — `Cest::Mock` and `Cest::MockStrict` — that propagate the
build flags hot-patching needs so consumers don't have to discover and apply
them manually. Adds a `hotpatchMethod()` overload for non-virtual member
functions, a `CEST_MOCKABLE` annotation macro, and end-to-end tests for both
facets.

**Why.** Hot-patching previously threw an explicit `runtime_error` on Windows
and forced POSIX users to set `-fno-inline` themselves. Both were friction
points called out in the original module header and in ROADMAP item 3.1. With
this change, a user adds `Cest::Mock` to their `target_link_libraries` and
hot-patching works on Linux, macOS, and Windows with no further configuration.

**Implementation summary.**

- Memory protection is now dispatched between `mprotect` (POSIX) and
  `VirtualProtect` (Windows). The Windows path uses `PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE`
  during the patch and restores the previous protection from
  `lpflOldProtect`. Page alignment is handled by Windows itself, so no manual
  rounding is needed on that path.
- Instruction encodings are unchanged. `movabs rax, imm64; jmp rax` (12 bytes)
  on x86_64 and `ldr x16, #8; br x16; <addr>` (16 bytes) on AArch64 are
  identical between POSIX and Windows. The arch-specific blocks were lifted
  out of the POSIX `#if` so both platforms share them.
- `FlushInstructionCache(GetCurrentProcess(), addr, size)` is called
  unconditionally on Windows, including on x86/x64. Microsoft's contract
  requires it even where the i-cache is coherent with the d-cache on the
  same core, because other threads may have prefetched the old bytes.
- `hotpatchMethod()` was added for non-virtual member functions. It extracts
  the code address from a member pointer via `memcpy` (Itanium ABI on
  GCC/Clang, single-inheritance MSVC representation) and routes through the
  existing `hotpatch` machinery. Const-qualified overload provided.

**CMake-side changes.** Two new `INTERFACE` libraries are exported alongside
the existing `Cest::Cest`:

- `Cest::Mock` — link this and hot-patching just works. Propagates
  `/guard:cf-` + `/GUARD:NO` (CFG off), `/INCREMENTAL:NO` (no ILT thunk), and
  `/Ob0` (MSVC) or `-fno-inline -fno-inline-functions` (GCC/Clang). No
  annotations required on user code; trade-off is loss of inlining in the
  test binary.
- `Cest::MockStrict` — same CFG and incremental linking flags, but inlining
  stays enabled. Users must annotate hot-patchable functions with
  `CEST_MOCKABLE` (defined in `<cest/macros/attributes.hpp>`, expands to
  `__declspec(noinline)` on MSVC and `__attribute__((noinline))` elsewhere).

Both facets transitively link `Cest::Cest`, so consumers do not need to list
the core target a second time.

The MSVC-specific glue lives in a new `cmake/Modules/CestMockCommon.cmake`
helper. Install/export rules in `CestDeployment.cmake` were extended to ship
the two new facets, and both `CestConfig.cmake.in` and
`CestBuildTreeConfig.cmake.in` were updated to apply
`MAP_IMPORTED_CONFIG_<CONFIG>` to all three exported targets via a
`foreach`/`if(TARGET ...)` loop.

**Known cosmetic warning.** When `STRICT_MODE` is on, MSVC emits warning
D9025 (`overriding '/guard:cf' with '/guard:cf-'`) at compile time. This is
intentional and documented in the README; the warning is a command-line
driver warning that cannot be suppressed via `/wd9025` or `/WX`. The build
itself succeeds.

## Kind of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] Build / CI / tooling (CMake, GitHub Actions, repo configuration)
- [x] Documentation only (README, ROADMAP, comments, contributing docs)

## GitHub issues

#14 

Closes #3.1 (Windows hot-patch port from ROADMAP).

Related to ROADMAP item 3.2 (`VTableGuard` for per-instance virtual mocking),
which is not implemented in this PR but is now unblocked by the shared arch
encoding refactor.

## Tests

Two new test binaries exercise the feature end-to-end and double as usage
examples for the README:

- `tests/test_hotpatch.cpp` (links `Cest::Mock`) — covers free-function
  patching with primitive and pointer return types, multiple independent
  patches, explicit `restore()` calls and idempotency, `HotpatchGuard` move
  semantics, nested patches on the same function (last-write-wins), and
  `hotpatchMethod` on both mutating and `const`-qualified non-virtual
  methods.
- `tests/test_strict_hotpatch.cpp` (links `Cest::MockStrict`) — same
  coverage shape, but every target function is annotated with
  `CEST_MOCKABLE`. Validates that the strict facet does not disable
  inlining globally and that `CEST_MOCKABLE` is sufficient on its own.

Both binaries are wired into CTest and run on every CI configuration. The
existing `test_mock.cpp` (Tier A `MockFn`) was left unchanged and continues
to pass.

body:
Adds full time entry CRUD per #7, reimplemented from current `main` per the maintainer's "fresh PR from current main with tests against the post-1.1.0 handler structure" note when closing #12 (and equivalent guidance closing #8).

> [!NOTE]
> **Tracking #36, depends on #37.** Same coordination story as #37 (tag CRUD): authored against current `main`. The request 200/empty-body fix is cherry-picked from #37 because tag DELETE and time entry DELETE share the same Toggl response shape — patch-id collision will let the duplicate commit drop cleanly when either PR rebases. Happy to rebase against post-#36/#37 `main` and add handler tests using the new `tests/mcp-server.test.ts` pattern, or merge in any order — your call.

## What's added

Three MCP tools that complete the time entry CRUD surface, plus a small extension to `toggl_start_timer`:

- `toggl_create_time_entry` — `POST /workspaces/{wid}/time_entries`. Required: `start`. Optional: `stop`, `duration`, `description`, `project_id`, `task_id`, `tags`, `tag_ids`, `billable`. Fills the create gap for retroactively logging past work — `toggl_start_timer` only creates running timers.
- `toggl_update_time_entry` — `PUT /workspaces/{wid}/time_entries/{tid}`. All fields optional except `entry_id`; only fields the caller passed are sent, so `{ project_id: 50 }` doesn't clobber description.
- `toggl_delete_time_entry` — `DELETE /workspaces/{wid}/time_entries/{tid}`.
- `toggl_start_timer` — gains optional `billable` parameter for parity.

All three new tools resolve workspace via `resolveWorkspaceForTool`, return via `jsonResponse`, and hydrate response entries via `cache.hydrateTimeEntries`. Errors flow through the central catch with `errorPayload(error)`. No new cache invalidation — time entries aren't cached as a collection.

## Includes a small `request()` fix (cherry-picked from #37)

`toggl_delete_time_entry` hits the same Toggl 200/`content-length: 0` shape as tag DELETE. The existing `request()` short-circuited only on 204 and called `response.json()` on the empty body, throwing and triggering a misleading retry that surfaced as a bogus 404. The cherry-picked fix from #37 treats 200/empty-body the same as 204. Behavior unchanged for non-empty success responses.

## Resolves prior closed work

- **#7** (open, @YoungR25): explicit feature request for `toggl_update_time_entry` with project/task/description/tags/billable. Implemented.
- **#8** (closed, @rocketworm): billable on `start_timer` + update_entry tool. Maintainer's closing note: *"rewrite from current main if billable/update-entry support is still wanted."* Reimplemented from current `main`; original author credited via `Co-Authored-By`.
- **#12** (closed, @arndjan): create + delete time entry tools. Maintainer's closing note: *"fresh PR from current main with tests against the post-1.1.0 handler structure."* Reimplemented from current `main`; original author credited via `Co-Authored-By`.

Both contributors' branches were too far behind to cherry-pick cleanly (pre-1.1.0). Their work informed the design but the implementation here is fresh against current `main` patterns: `WorkspaceResolutionError`, `jsonResponse`, `errorPayload`, `resolveWorkspaceForTool`, `cache.hydrateTimeEntries`.

## Plan-tier billable note

A small UX hint: the `billable` parameter description on all three tools that accept it now mentions that some Toggl plans (Free) silently set entry-level billable to `false` even when the project itself is billable. Agents can check the response to detect the discrepancy rather than assuming the flag applied. Verified live during smoke testing — the Toggl API accepts the flag and returns 200, but the response shows `billable: false` on Free workspaces.

## Commits

Three commits:

1. `fix(api): handle Toggl 200/empty-body responses` — cherry-picked from #37
2. `feat: add time entry CRUD tools and billable on start_timer` — Co-Authored-By: Andreas Wurm, Arnd Jan Gulmans
3. `docs: note plan-tier billable behavior in tool schemas`

## Verification

- `npm test` — 36/36 passing (5 new API-level tests: POST/PUT/DELETE shape, billable-passthrough, 4xx no-retry)
- `npm run build` — clean
- `npm run lint` — no new warnings
- Smoke-tested end-to-end against a real Toggl workspace: `create` with billable → `list` (verify visible) → `update` (assign project, hydrate via cache) → `delete` → verify cleanup. The empty-body fix is verified live; delete returns clean `success: true`, no false 404.

## Coverage with #36's proposed thresholds

Same approach as #37 — every metric improves over `main`; further gain available via handler tests once `createTogglServer` lands.

## Scope

Time entry CRUD only. No project/client write tools, no SDK upgrade.

author: mosnin
body:
### Motivation

- Harden the agent trigger and callback paths so Modal failures never leave jobs indefinitely queued. 
- Support an alternative callback header and protect against misconfigured Modal runtime settings and redirects. 
- Improve reliability of Modal client behavior (retries, redirects, timeouts) and enforce sane limits when syncing tasks. 

### Description

- `POST /api/agent/trigger` now validates `jobId`, `convexUserId`, and `intent`, requires both `MODAL_AGENT_URL` and `MODAL_AGENT_SECRET`, awaits Modal `/run` with a 15s timeout, and fails the Convex job if Modal returns non-2xx or the request times out. 
- Callback routes under `app/api/agent/*` (`progress`, `complete`, `fail`, `sync-tasks`, `data`) accept the secret via either `Authorization: Bearer {secret}` or `X-Modal-Secret` and return proper errors on authorization or write failures; `sync-tasks` now returns HTTP 500 on Convex write failures and logs the error. 
- `modal_agent/client.py` now includes `X-Modal-Secret` in headers, refuses to run without a secret, disables automatic follow-redirects and surfaces redirects as errors (with guidance to set `APP_URL` to the canonical host), and uses non-redirecting requests for all callback calls. 
- `modal_agent/orchestrator.py` enforces a documented max of 50 tasks when syncing to the app to avoid huge writes. 
- `modal_agent/types.py` switches `connectedPlatforms` to a `Field(default_factory=list)` to avoid shared mutable defaults. 
- `modal_agent/app.py` and `requirements.txt` updated to align package names/versions (`composio-openai`, `composio-openai-agents`, etc.). 
- UI pages (`app/(dashboard)/agent/page.tsx` and `app/(dashboard)/today/page.tsx`) now await the `/api/agent/trigger` response and surface failures via console logs; they also handle non-OK HTTP responses from the trigger route. 
- Documentation (`docs/agent-harness.md`) updated to reflect behavioral and security changes and added reliability notes about redirects, required packages, and task limits. 

### Testing

- Ran TypeScript typecheck and Next.js app build locally and the build completed without type errors. 
- Exercised the `/api/agent/trigger` and callback routes locally against a Modal dev instance and confirmed that non-2xx responses and timeouts mark jobs failed; these checks succeeded. 
- Ran the Modal client end-to-end with a local Modal container to validate callback headers, redirect detection, and task sync truncation; these validation runs succeeded.

body: ## Objetivo Adicionar uma API local na VPS para integrar ChatGPT (Actions/MCP) ao copiloto operacional, mantendo o modelo de segurança por aprovação explícita e allowlist de comandos, além de ampliar o report diário para leitura detalhada de performance por desfecho e diagnóstico fast-vs-slow. ## O que foi incluído - Novo módulo `ops/ai_copilot_api.py` com servidor HTTP (`ThreadingHTTPServer`) e endpoints: - `GET /health` - `GET /diag?minutes=30` - `GET /pending` - `GET /history?limit=30` - `POST /approve` - `POST /reject` - `POST /query` (shell read-only com allowlist) - `POST /sql` (SQL read-only `SELECT/WITH`) - Reaproveitamento do motor já existente de diagnóstico/propostas e fila de ações pendentes. - Autenticação via bearer token (`OPS_AI_API_TOKEN`) para todos os endpoints sensíveis. - Modo opcional sem token apenas para laboratório (`OPS_AI_API_ALLOW_NO_TOKEN=1`). - Monitor em background na própria API para geração contínua de propostas (`OPS_AI_MONITOR_*`). - Guardrails adicionais: - `/query` com allowlist de comandos de consulta e bloqueio de comandos destrutivos/sensíveis. - `/sql` bloqueando qualquer instrução de escrita e múltiplas statements. - Unit files systemd: - `ops/systemd/betinasia-ops-ai-copilot-api.service` - `betinasia-ops-ai-copilot-api.service` (cópia para deploy rápido) - Novas variáveis em `.env.example`: - `OPS_AI_API_HOST` - `OPS_AI_API_PORT` - `OPS_AI_API_TOKEN` - `OPS_AI_API_ALLOW_NO_TOKEN` - `OPS_AI_QUERY_ENABLE` - `OPS_AI_QUERY_TIMEOUT_SEC` - `OPS_AI_QUERY_MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS` - `OPS_AI_SQL_ENABLE` - `OPS_AI_SQL_MAX_ROWS` ## Daily report — melhorias implementadas ### 1) Back Pre fast (blocos de performance) - Inclusão de colunas de desfecho em ordens liquidadas: - `n_win (P&L>0)` - `n_loss (P&L<0)` - `n_neutro (P&L≈0)` - Aplicado tanto no bloco principal elegível HI quanto no bloco auxiliar (`stake < limiar HI`). ### 2) Back Pre fast vs slow (detalhamento expandido) Nova seção com tabela comparativa Fast vs Slow contendo: - `n_orders (exec)` - `n_orders com accounting (oid)` - `cobertura oid%` - `n_liquidadas / n_abertas` - `n_win / n_loss / n_neutro` - `stake total` e `stake médio` (liquidadas) - `P&L total accounting` e `ROIw accounting` - `ROI mean por ordem` - `mediana P&L por ordem` - `IC95 bootstrap` do ROI mean por grupo - `slippage_pre mean / mediana` - distribuição slippage 3-way (`<=-2% / (-2,2] / >2% / NA`) - latência `call_to_done_ms` p50/p90 - odds média/mediana (`odd_at_decision`) - coluna de cobertura de placar por grupo (explicitamente `—` quando indisponível no pipeline atual) Também foi expandida a subseção de diferença Fast−Slow com: - Delta ROI mean por ordem - Delta ROIw accounting - IC90 bootstrap do delta ROI mean - IC95 bootstrap do delta ROI mean ## Segurança e governança - Execução de ação continua restrita à allowlist já definida (`systemctl start|stop|restart`) via fluxo de aprovação. - A API não altera `.env`, policy WF, ou código automaticamente. - Ações de operação seguem dependentes de aprovação explícita (`POST /approve`). - Endpoints de consulta (`/query` e `/sql`) são estritamente read-only e validados. ## Validação - `python3 -m py_compile ops/ai_copilot_api.py` - `python3 -m py_compile ops/daily_full_report.py`

- **Core modules**: Ktor network client with auth interceptor, design system (Material3 theme, section color palette, shimmer loading, error/empty states), shared constants

- **Profile & Settings**: Stats dashboard, tech stack display, theme toggle, content density, account management

## Architecture

Clean architecture throughout: `domain/model` → `data/repository` → `presentation/viewmodel+screen`. Sealed classes for UI state (`Loading | Success | Error`). Koin for DI. SQLDelight for local persistence.

App navigation shell (NavHost + BottomNavBar), Android entry point (MainActivity), and Koin module registration remain to be added to connect all features.

## Summary

**Tier 2** of the 3-tier playground. Browser-side mock decision engine with explicit MOCK badge — no theater.

### Components

- \`lib/playground/scenarios.ts\` — 8 pre-loaded scenarios (allow-small / deny-provider / deny-mev / deny-token-gate / deny-expired / deny-replay / require-human / tampered-starter)
- \`lib/playground/mock-engine.ts\` — \`decideMock(aprpJson, policyToml)\`. Real APRP shape validation, mock pattern-match policy eval, real SHA-256 over canonical inputs (hashes prefixed \`\"mock:\"\` so they can't collide with daemon's). Capsule schema = \`sbo3l.playground_mock.v1\` (distinct from real). Signature = \`\"MOCK_NOT_SIGNED\"\`.
- \`pages/playground.astro\` — 3-area layout, persistent MOCK banner, scenario tabs, two textarea editors, decision panel with mock-capsule disclosure, sticky teaching rail.

### Why textarea, not Monaco

Adding \`@astrojs/react\` for Monaco would ship ~140 KB of React + scheduler hydration. Marketing site is Astro static specifically to avoid that. Monaco also pulls from jsdelivr CDN, requiring CSP relaxation. Styled monospace textarea preserves functional behavior + visual fidelity at 0 KB JS overhead.

### Boundary verification

Visitor can paste a mock capsule into \`/proof\` and watch strict-mode WASM verifier reject it (schema mismatch + missing signature). The MOCK badge is honest; the system enforces it.

author: cipher813
body:
## Summary

Closes the **prune+backfill loop** that recreated 7 S&P churn-out stragglers on every Saturday SF run. 2026-05-02 redrive #6 surfaced the loop:

1. Pre-MorningEnrich prune (PR #134, `absent_days=5`) drops stragglers ✓
2. Phase 1 step 8 (`builders.backfill`) loads ALL `predictor/price_cache/*.parquet` and writes EVERY ticker to ArcticDB universe — **including the ones we just pruned**, because their parquet files still exist (kept for historical lookup)
3. Loop closes; Backtester preflight ~2 hours later trips on the 8-day-stale rows

## Two fixes

### `builders/backfill.py`: constituents-filter on writes
Load current constituents via the `latest_weekly.json` pointer and filter `universe_tickers` against it. Churn-out parquet preserved (history kept) but no arctic row written. If a ticker returns to S&P, backfill picks it back up automatically. Hard-fails on constituents-load failure (no silent recreate-everything fallback).

### `sf_preflight.check_universe_drift`: WARN → FAIL
Now returns FAIL when any straggler is `>5d stale`. Forces operators to drop stragglers BEFORE launching recovery SFs that skip MorningEnrich (otherwise we burn a 120-min Backtester spot to re-discover them). Result includes remediation hint.

## Validation against current state (post manual prune)

```
[OK]   arctic_connectivity              ArcticDB reachable; universe library has 904 symbols
[OK]   universe_drift                   1 arctic stragglers; 0 would be pruned, 1 too fresh to drop
[OK]   backfill_source_freshness        Backfill source (2026-05-01) ≥ arctic (2026-05-01)
... Predicted SF outcome: PASS
```

## Test plan

- [x] 3 new tests in `test_backfill_no_regression.py`: loop closure, hard-fail on constituents-load failure, dry-run doesn't require S3
- [x] Existing 21 backfill tests still pass (mocks updated)
- [x] Updated test for `check_universe_drift` to expect FAIL on stragglers + remediation hint
- [x] Full suite: 406 passed
- [ ] Live verification: next Saturday SF that runs MorningEnrich → prune drops stragglers → backfill respects + doesn't recreate → no Backtester preflight halt

## Why not also add prune to Backtester?

Considered but rejected — the issue isn't Backtester missing a prune step, it's that the EXISTING DataPhase1 prune was getting undone by DataPhase1's own backfill. Fixing the loop in one place is cleaner than duplicating prune across modules.

body:
## Summary

Tier 4b — die drei großen Caldav/Google-Module strict, **120 Funde mit nur ~35 Edits gefasst** dank strukturierten Wrapper-Patterns (Hebel-Faktor 3.4).

> **Stack-Hinweis:** Dieser PR basiert auf [#167](https://github.com/leratos/Elder-Berry/pull/167) (Tier 4a). Erst #167 mergen, dann diesen PR auf `main` umrebasern.

| # | Modul | Funde | Commit |
|---|-------|-------|--------|
| 1 | tools/google_calendar | 32 | ac82493 |
| 2 | tools/caldav_calendar | 39 | 65c5284 |
| 3 | tools/caldav_tasks | 49 | b94d0aa |

## Strukturelle Patterns (warum es so wenig Edits sind)

Drei Patterns erklären 80%+ der Funde — alle drei Module hatten identische Stub-Probleme:

**1. §10.11 Lazy-Init mit `Any`-Type** (googleapiclient.Resource / caldav.* sind sehr permissiv im Stub):
```python
self._client: Any = None
def _get_service(self) -> Any: ...
```

**2. PEP-695-Generic `_call_with_retry[T]`** (Pattern aus Phase 76 `stt_router._run_async`):
```python
def _call_with_retry[T](self, operation: Callable[[], T]) -> T:
    try:
        return operation()
    except self._RETRIABLE_ERRORS:
        ...
        return operation()
```
Erschlägt "Returning Any from typed function" + "Call to untyped function" auf einen Schlag — sonst wären das ~12 einzelne Casts.

**3. icalendar Component-Cast**:
```python
for raw_component in cal.walk():
    component: Any = raw_component
    if component.name == "VEVENT": ...
```
Eine Zeile rettet 5×–8× `# type: ignore[no-untyped-call]` auf den `.get()`-Aufrufen.

## Inner-Function-Annotations (`def _op()`)

22 Stück über die 3 Module — `_op() -> list[CalendarEvent]`, `_op() -> TaskItem | None`, `_op() -> bool`. Mechanisch, aber notwendig.

## Drei verbleibende Type-Ignores (mit Begründung im Commit-Body)

- 2× `# type: ignore[operator]` für `caldav.DAVClient(...)` — caldav-Stub markiert `DAVClient` als `object` statt callable class. Stub-Bug, runtime ist OK.
- 1× `# type: ignore[no-untyped-call]` für `Credentials(...)` — `google.oauth2.credentials` Stub markiert `__init__` als untyped (akzeptiert `**kwargs`).

`warn_unused_ignores=True` ist global aktiv — wenn die Stubs mal verbessert werden, fällt das automatisch auf.

## Stand 76c

**34/39 Module strict (87%).** Tier 5 (Folge-PR) hat nur noch 5 Module + 60 Funde + den finalen Schritt: CI-Scope erweitern + WIP-Blöcke aus pyproject löschen → Phase abgeschlossen.

## Summary

Closes #3721 (the part deferred from #3856).

Every refusal path in `send_invoice`, `confirm_send_invoice`, and `create_payment_link` now emits a `tool_error` person event with `{ tool, reason, lookup_key, org_id?, error? }`. The original Greg-thread incident left zero trace in `person_events`; this closes that gap so admins can debug silent failures from the relationship timeline.

## Changes

- **`server/src/db/person-events-db.ts`**: add `tool_error` to the `PersonEventType` union.
- **`server/src/addie/mcp/billing-tools.ts`**:
  - `resolvePersonId(ctx)` resolves person_id from MemberContext (workos_user_id → slack_user_id fallback) at the tool boundary so we don't need to plumb person_id through context-building sites.
  - `recordToolError(ctx, tool, reason, data)` is best-effort and try/catch-wrapped — a buggy recorder never blocks the user-facing refusal message.
  - Wired into 13 refusal paths with distinct `reason` slugs:
    - `not_signed_in`, `no_workspace`, `unknown_lookup_key`, `stripe_not_configured`, `exception` (create_payment_link)
    - `not_signed_in_or_no_workspace`, `product_not_found_or_stripe_unconfigured`, `exception` (send_invoice)
    - `not_signed_in_or_no_workspace`, `org_not_loaded`, `missing_billing_address`, `send_returned_null`, `exception` (confirm_send_invoice)
- **`tests/addie/billing-tools.test.ts`**: add 5 unit tests covering the new emission shape, slack-only fallback, anonymous-no-event, and the safety contract that recordEvent throwing does not break the refusal.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run tests/addie/billing-tools.test.ts` — 25 pass (20 existing + 5 new)

## Related

- #3856 — empty-turn safeguard (the model-layer half of #3721)
- #3724 — billing-tooling fixes from the original incident

## Summary

Adds PR8 from the public-protocol roadmap as a stacked follow-up to #1952:

- adds public model capability protocols in `pyrecest.protocols.models`
- re-exports the existing likelihood/sampling model protocols from the public protocol module
- adds protocol-based model adapter helpers in `pyrecest.models.adapters`
- adds structural linear Gaussian argument adapters for existing Kalman-style APIs
- exports the adapter helpers from `pyrecest.models`
- documents the model protocols and adapters
- adds focused tests for the new adapter helpers

## Stack

This PR is intentionally based on `feature/public-protocol-seed` / #1952 rather than `main`, because it depends on the public `pyrecest.protocols` package seed.

After #1952 is merged, this PR can be retargeted to `main`.

## Notes

The implementation is additive. It does not change filter behavior or require existing model/filter classes to inherit from the new protocols.

It also removes the duplicate `LikelihoodMeasurementModel` / `SampleableTransitionModel` import/export ambiguity in `pyrecest.models.__init__`, which was already triggering F811/redefinition diagnostics on the stacked branch.

## Tests

Prepared patch was syntax-checked locally with:

```bash
python -m py_compile \
  src/pyrecest/protocols/models.py \
  src/pyrecest/models/adapters.py \
  src/pyrecest/models/likelihood.py \
  src/pyrecest/models/__init__.py \
```

author: johanneslichtenberger
body:
## Summary

Adds a long-running stress test, \`BitemporalSoakStressTest\`, that exercises the production-readiness pipeline end-to-end (commit + temporal-axis read + recovery), plus a GitHub Actions workflow to run it on demand and on a weekly schedule.

## What it tests

Three sequential phases share one configurable wall-clock budget:

| Phase | Body | What it locks down |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Writer | Up to 500 commits, each updating a single counter node | Sustained commit throughput, no partial commits |
| 2. Reader | N concurrent threads walking \`AllTimeAxis\` and \`PrefetchedAllTimeAxis\` | No rtx leak (\`activeTrxCount()\` returns to zero), both axes yield identical sequences |
| 3. Recovery | Close + reopen the session, read latest revision | \`.commit\`-marker recovery still works, every committed revision is readable, counter equals commit count |

## Why phases are sequential, not concurrent

Sirix's per-session \`RevisionEpochTracker\` has 4096 slots and committed revisions occupy them permanently within the session lifetime — running readers and writers concurrently on the same session saturates quickly and surfaces an internal tracker race that's out of scope for this PR. The \`MAX_COMMITS_PER_SOAK = 500\` cap leaves comfortable headroom for the reader phase's transient axis-walk rtxs.

(A future enhancement could add barrier-coordinated session cycling for true endurance testing past 2k revisions; tracked separately.)

## How to run

Disabled by default via \`@Disabled\` and gated at runtime by \`SIRIX_STRESS_ENABLE=1\` (belt-and-braces). Three ways to fire it:

\`\`\`bash
# Local opt-in (60s default)
SIRIX_STRESS_ENABLE=1 ./gradlew :sirix-core:test \\
    --tests io.sirix.stress.BitemporalSoakStressTest \\
    -Djunit.jupiter.conditions.deactivate='org.junit.*DisabledCondition'

# Local 1-hour soak
SIRIX_STRESS_ENABLE=1 SIRIX_STRESS_DURATION_SECONDS=3600 ./gradlew ...
\`\`\`

The companion \`.github/workflows/stress.yml\`:
- **\`workflow_dispatch\`** — manual UI trigger with adjustable \`duration_seconds\` (default 1800) and \`reader_threads\` (default 4) inputs.
- **Weekly cron** — Sunday 03:00 UTC, 30-minute soak.
- Uploads test reports as artifacts (30-day retention).

## Test plan
- [x] Local 20s smoke (default cap of 500 commits): \`elapsed=2.6s, commits=500, walks=5, revisions read=2505, cycles=1\`. Test passes, no leaks.
- [x] \`./gradlew :sirix-core:compileTestJava\` clean.
- [ ] Workflow manual trigger with 60s budget on this PR (verify CI plumbing).
